content.text: CI LLM reviewers in standard, deep, and overlay tiers (running on the Python module + LiteLLM abstraction shipped by epic c6de-76e7-5e4b-4968) receive only the diff. Local `/dso:review` reviewers — running in Claude Code's harness with full tool access — make 20-40 grounded tool calls per review to verify call sites, deletion impact, cross-file consistency, and framework-guarantee defenses against the actual codebase. CI reviewers therefore produce lower-fidelity findings on the same diff: speculation about callers, missed cross-file regressions, and false-positive defenses that a quick file read would refute.

This epic closes the CI <-> local fidelity gap by adding an application-level context-augmentation loop where the model emits structured context-request blocks (action + arguments — e.g., `{"action": "read_files", "paths": [...]}`, `{"action": "grep", "patterns": [...], "paths": [...]}`) as fenced text in plain-text assistant messages; the dispatcher parses any request blocks, executes them locally, and appends the results as a new user message before issuing the next `litellm.completion(...)` call. The provider-native tool-use API (`tools=[...]`, `tool_use` content blocks, `tool_calls` arrays) is deliberately not used — every call's message history is provider-agnostic plain text, which (a) sidesteps LiteLLM's known cross-provider tool-use translation bugs (LiteLLM #18271, #26529) and (b) preserves clean cross-provider fallback as configured by the LiteLLM substrate epic (c6de SC6). Industry pattern survey across multi-provider repo-aware AI tools (aider, Cline, OpenHands, SWE-agent) confirms this is the dominant pattern; PR-Agent demonstrates the single-shot alternative is less fit-for-purpose given the fidelity gap this epic targets. Light tier remains diff-only, single-shot.

Caching and turn-budget exhaustion handling ship together with the loop because they are load-bearing for one another: without prompt caching, the per-turn input-token cost across 15+ tool-style turns is prohibitive (the input prefix is re-sent every turn); without the soft-cap -> second-nudge -> fail-closed cascade, a misbehaving reviewer can loop indefinitely on a confused diff and either burn budget or hang the CI gate. Provider/tier fallback ships at the LiteLLM substrate layer (c6de SC6) — not in this epic — since it is fundamentally a substrate concern.

Outcome: PR authors see CI review comments grounded in actual code references (file:line citations) instead of speculative findings, reducing dismissed-as-noise rate and increasing review-verdict trust parity with local /dso:review.

- Application-level context-augmentation loop active for standard, deep (3 specialists + arch synthesis), and overlay reviewers; each can request additional context during its turn by emitting a structured request block in its assistant message per a documented contract (`docs/contracts/ci-review-context-request.md`). The dispatcher parses request blocks **only from assistant-role messages**, never re-parsing user-role / diff content (defending against the failure mode where a PR diff or a docs change containing literal example request syntax would otherwise be re-interpreted as a request). The dispatcher executes parsed requests locally and appends the results as a new user message before issuing the next `litellm.completion(...)` call. The provider tool-use API is not used — every call's message history is provider-agnostic plain text. Light tier dispatched in single-shot mode (no augmentation loop) and remains diff-only. Parser handles failure modes including the model emitting both a well-formed request block and a final-findings block in the same assistant message: well-formed-request takes precedence and findings are deferred to a subsequent turn. The structured-request format and the request-precedence rule are documented in the contract so request-block parsing is testable independently of the LLM call. Verified by context-request logs in fixture-corpus runs evidencing standard / deep reviewers grounding findings in fetched data (each such finding cites a `file:line` resolved by a recorded request-response cycle), light reviewers producing findings from the diff alone (no requests in the log), and parser unit tests against well-formed and malformed assistant outputs (including outputs that contain literal request-syntax in user-role positions, which must NOT trigger execution).

- `read_files` and `grep` tool implementations enforce a security boundary: repo-root jail (absolute paths and `..` parent traversal rejected; **paths canonicalized via realpath and re-verified to resolve under repo root, defending against committed or runtime-created symlinks pointing to /etc, $HOME, or sibling worktrees**); per-file size cap (configurable; default 256 KB); per-tool-result max output bytes (configurable; default 64 KB) with an explicit truncation marker appended when the cap is hit and an instruction to the model not to assert absence based on truncated content; **per-grep-invocation wall-clock timeout (configurable; default 5s) and binary-file exclusion (or use ripgrep with `--max-filesize`) to prevent ReDoS-class regex patterns from pinning a CI core**. Verified by unit tests covering absolute-path rejection, parent-traversal rejection, **symlink-escape rejection (test fixtures with both committed symlinks and runtime-created symlinks pointing outside repo root)**, file-size-cap rejection, multi-pattern multi-path tool argument acceptance, **grep-timeout enforcement with adversarial regex (e.g., `(a+)+$` against a long line)**, and truncation-marker emission.

- Anthropic prompt caching active with two `cache_control` breakpoints (after the system prompt; after the diff). OpenAI prefix caching applies automatically. The `cache_control` placement is derived from the rendered message structure at call time (not hardcoded by index), defending against agents that inject agent-specific instructions between system and diff. **A prefix-bytes hash invariant test asserts the cached prefix is byte-identical across turns within a run**, defending against silent invalidation from per-turn dynamic content (timestamps, turn counters, agent_id interpolation, randomized tip ordering, trailing whitespace from template rendering). A cache-hit assertion emits a warning to CI logs when `usage.cache_creation_input_tokens > 0` does not occur on the first Anthropic call per review run **AND `usage.cache_read_input_tokens` is also zero** (tolerating the legitimate first-call cache-warm case where a CI job is retried within the 5-minute Anthropic cache TTL); subsequent turns warn when `cache_read_input_tokens` does not increase. Verified by unit test asserting `cache_control` placement at the documented boundaries, prefix-bytes-hash invariant test across turns, and integration test asserting cache-creation on turn 1 and cache-read on turn 2 against a fixture review.

- Soft-cap nudge cascade: a per-tier configurable soft cap (**default 15 turns**) triggers a wrap-up nudge instructing the model to emit final `reviewer-findings` JSON. **If the model continues emitting structured context-request blocks past `soft_cap + 3` turns, a second harder nudge runs.** **Post-nudge state-machine rule: when an assistant turn after the first nudge contains both a well-formed request block and a final-findings block, the request is ignored AND counts as a strike toward the second nudge — preventing infinite loops where deferring findings indefinitely defeats the cap.** If the model still does not emit final JSON after the second nudge, the review records as failed (fail-closed) via the existing `record-review.sh` integration. Verified by tests covering: nudge -> final JSON path; second nudge -> fail-closed recording; per-tier soft-cap override; post-nudge mixed request+findings turn -> request ignored, strike counted.

- Per-feature unit tests using `respx` / `httpx.MockTransport`-style provider mocks cover: structured-request parsing (well-formed + malformed assistant outputs, including outputs with literal request-syntax in user-role positions), context-request dispatch (single + multiple requests in one assistant turn), soft-cap nudge state machine (each branch of the cascade including post-nudge mixed turn rule), `cache_control` breakpoint placement under all four (tier x tools-present) combinations, prefix-bytes-hash invariant across turns, jail enforcement (including symlink escape rejection and grep-timeout enforcement), and output truncation. Integration tests exercise the loop end-to-end against both Anthropic and OpenAI providers with fixture reviews. (Provider/tier fallback dispatch tests live in c6de's SC6 — out of scope here.)
- Resource: tool-mocking strategy in unit tests

If cost cliff is observed in production, a follow-up bug ticket addresses the integration.
- Resource: `docs/contracts/ci-review-context-request.md` referenced by reviewer agent prompt examples

Interaction: agent prompts (in `plugins/dso/agents/*.md`) embed examples of the context-request format. Drift between the contract doc and the agent prompts produces parser rejections during partial rollouts.

Gate: contract carries a `version` field; a referential-integrity check (similar to existing `check-skill-refs.sh`) validates agent prompt examples against the current contract version at pre-commit time.

- Cross-provider fallback bypasses cache and inflates cost (medium, runtime): when c6de's fallback fires mid-run, the alternate provider sees a cold prefix, wasting the Anthropic prompt cache built across earlier turns. Mitigation: documented in cross-epic interactions; integration-time mitigation deferred (fallback-after-N-turns demotion or per-run cost ceiling); follow-up bug ticket if observed in production.

- Contract doc drift between dispatcher and agent prompts (medium, deployment): `docs/contracts/ci-review-context-request.md` evolves but agent prompts embed old-format examples. Mitigation: contract version field in request blocks; referential-integrity check on agent prompt examples.

- CI runner filesystem differs from local repo layout (medium, deployment): GitHub Actions checkouts may use shallow clones, sparse checkouts, or symlinked workspace dirs; `read_files` for a file outside the checkout cone returns file-not-found, which the model may interpret as "file deleted" rather than "unavailable in this CI context." Mitigation: explicit fetch-depth / sparse-checkout requirements documented as CI prereqs; tool result for missing files distinguishes "not in checkout" from "does not exist in repo."

- Soft-cap default 15 turns interacts poorly with deep-tier 4 agents (medium, configuration): deep tier dispatches 3 specialists in parallel plus an arch synthesis agent serially; if each consumes ~15 turns, total turns per review is 60+, and Anthropic/OpenAI per-minute token rate limits apply per-key. Parallel deep-tier reviews on a busy repo can self-induce the 429s that trigger c6de SC6 fallback. Mitigation: SC4 per-tier configurable cap allows tightening defaults for deep-tier specialists separately; document the multiplier in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md.

- Per-file 256 KB cap defeats reading generated/lockfile artifacts (medium, configuration): default cap silently truncates package-lock.json, poetry.lock, large test fixture JSON, generated migration files. Truncation marker is per SC2, but the model receiving truncated content may make grounded-looking findings on incomplete data. Mitigation: SC2 truncation marker carries an explicit instruction to the model not to assert absence based on truncated content; consider per-extension caps in a follow-up if observed in production.

- Blocked by: c6de-76e7-5e4b-4968 (Python migration + LiteLLM provider abstraction + provider/tier fallback — this epic operates on the merged dso_ci_review/ module and depends on SC6's `streaming=False` + fallback substrate).

- Industry pattern survey (multi-provider repo-aware AI tools): aider, Cline, OpenHands (NonNativeToolCallingMixin fallback), SWE-agent (text parsers) dominantly implement application-level loops with text/XML-parsed structured requests rather than provider-native tool-use. Cline (the most-starred agent) uses XML-in-system-prompt despite being Anthropic-first because it works uniformly across providers. Aider explicitly observed that forcing GPT through function-calling degraded coding quality vs. structured-text emission. PR-Agent (Codium/Qodo) — closest to this CI reviewer use case — sidesteps the loop with single-shot diff compression but does not claim equivalent fidelity to a loop-based reviewer. Key insight: confirms the architectural choice. Key gotcha: Cline issue #3992 documents the failure mode where the model emits structured-request syntax as literal text rather than as parseable request — parser fence-strictness and assistant-role-only scanning are mitigations. Sources: aider docs, Cline issue #3992, OpenHands issue #8424, PR-Agent docs.

- LiteLLM tool-use translation bugs: LiteLLM's parallel-tool-result merging on Anthropic has documented production issues (#18271, #26529); related issues #16711 (Claude Code tool result incompatible with LiteLLM), #5277 (Bedrock parallel tool calls), PR #15315 (partial fix for Anthropic passthrough). These bugs only affect provider-native tool-use; this epic's plain-text completion path sidesteps them entirely.

- Anthropic prompt caching: cache prefix order is tools, system, then messages; `cache_control` on the last tool definition caches all tool definitions; up to 4 breakpoints. Two breakpoints (after system, after diff) keep both cached across the multi-turn loop. Source: platform.claude.com/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching.
- OpenAI prefix caching: automatic for prompts >=1024 tokens; no `cache_control` flag needed.

Build directly on c6de's merged Python module + LiteLLM abstraction (including SC6 provider/tier fallback): extend `dso_ci_review/dispatch.py` with an application-level context-augmentation loop using plain-text `litellm.completion(...)` calls (no provider tool-use API); add `read_files` and `grep` request handlers with a realpath-canonicalized repo-root jail, per-file size caps, grep wall-clock timeout, and per-result truncation; add Anthropic `cache_control` breakpoints (after system, after diff) derived from the rendered message structure with a prefix-bytes-hash invariant test and a cache-hit assertion that tolerates CI-retry cache-warm state; add a soft-cap nudge state machine that emits a wrap-up nudge at turn 15, then a second harder nudge at turn 18, then records the review failed via `record-review.sh`. Light tier dispatched in single-shot mode without the augmentation loop. Provider/tier fallback dispatch is inherited from c6de's substrate work — no fallback logic in this epic.

- Bright-line conditions that fired: external integration (LiteLLM tool-use API surface, Anthropic prompt caching with cache_control), novel architectural pattern (multi-turn application-level context-augmentation loop in CI without provider tool-use)
- Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 7 critical/high folded into SC text directly; 5 medium retained in Scenario Analysis section

- Industry pattern survey (Step 2.6 supplement): triggered — aider, Cline, OpenHands, PR-Agent, SWE-agent verified custom-loop dominance for multi-provider repo-aware AI tools

- Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5): VERIFIED for plain-text custom-loop architecture against Anthropic + OpenAI; the prior INSUFFICIENT-EVIDENCE risk for cross-provider tool-use translation does not apply since this epic does not use provider tool-use
- LLM-instruction signal (Step 5): triggered — keyword: agent definitions (reviewer agent system prompts gain a context-request availability section as part of this epic)

Comparison runs at epic close as a one-shot script and the delta is reported in the close artifact; per-fixture grounded-finding counts shift from zero (pre) to non-zero (post) on at least 60% of fixtures. **Quality-not-just-presence assertion: on a curated subset (>=5 fixtures) where local /dso:review findings are known, post-change CI findings overlap with local findings on >=N critical/important items (N defined per fixture in the curated set), OR speculation-marker frequency ("likely", "probably", "may break callers") in CI finding text decreases by >=25% relative to the pre-loop baseline.**

content.text: The Jira bridge (`plugins/dso/scripts/bridge/`) tracks only four fields in EDIT events: `priority`, `assignee`, `title`, `description` (see `_handle_edit.py:73-88`). Three DSO-local fields with direct Jira analogs are never synced: `parent_id` (Jira Epic Link), `tags` (Jira Labels), and `blocks`/`depends_on` link relations (Jira Issue Links of type "Blocks"). This leads to silent divergence where a local reparent or retag is invisible in Jira, and vice versa. Additionally, the new `supersedes` relation (scoped in Epic 6f7a-4ba6 expansion) must sync lossily as Jira "Relates" with a local-richer-wins precedence rule on inbound. This epic closes all four bridge sync gaps in one coherent remediation.

- `parent_id` synced bidirectionally via Jira Epic Link field. Outbound: local parent-child changes write the Epic Link on next sync. Inbound: Jira Epic Link changes write a local EDIT(parent_id) event. Reducer EDIT handler extended.
- `tags` synced bidirectionally via Jira Labels. Outbound: tag add/remove writes Jira label update. Inbound: Jira label change writes local EDIT(tags) event.

- `blocks` and `depends_on` link relations synced bidirectionally via Jira Issue Links of type "Blocks". Outbound: new LINK event triggers Jira issue-link create. Inbound: new Jira Issue Link triggers local LINK event. UNLINK symmetric.

- `supersedes` relation synced lossily as Jira "Relates" (no native Jira supersedes type). Local `supersedes` value is authoritative: on inbound, if a Jira "Relates" link matches an existing local `supersedes`, local wins; other "Relates" links are imported as local `relates_to`.
- Bridge EDIT event tracking extended in `_handle_edit.py` from 4 fields to 7 (adding parent_id, tags, link-deltas). Comprehensive integration tests covering all four sync directions pass.
- Conflict handling: on simultaneous local + remote change to the same field, bridge raises BRIDGE_ALERT for human resolution (existing pattern).

Extend `_handle_edit.py` to track `parent_id`, `tags`, and link-deltas in EDIT tracking. Extend `_outbound_handlers.py` to write Jira Epic Link, Labels, and Issue Links. Extend `_inbound_api.py` to read these Jira fields and emit local EDIT/LINK events. Add precedence rule for `supersedes`-over-`relates` in link handler. Coordinate with Epic 6f7a-4ba6 to ensure `supersedes` relation exists before this epics supersedes-sync work lands.

content.text: AI agents running the DSO test gate today endure significant friction from two legacy harnesses: `test-batched.sh` — a RUN-block handshake loop where the orchestrator re-invokes the same command ~13 times to complete a 337-test suite, re-printing progress on every pass — and `nohup-launch.sh` / `nohup-poll.sh` — a PID-registry harness with heartbeat-based stall detection and a process budget. Both were built as workarounds for Claude Code's ~73-second Bash-tool default ceiling and the exit-144 SIGTERM propagation bug (anthropics/claude-code#45717, currently unresolved). The Claude Code ecosystem has since converged on `Bash(run_in_background: true)` + `BashOutput(bash_id)` as the proven pattern: it decouples the background process group from Claude's main turn (so child SIGTERM does not kill the parent), returns only new output since the last drain (bounded context cost), and collapses the multi-turn handshake into one dispatch + incremental drain. Three per-language runner scripts (`bash-runner.sh`, `pytest-runner.sh`, `node-runner.sh`) under `plugins/dso/scripts/runners/` exist solely to support batched-resume; once batching goes away, so do they. Epic 87e9-0bc8 delivers the polyglot `commands.test_runner` / `commands.test_file_runner` config keys that this epic's launcher consumes. Primary beneficiaries: every DSO-consumer agent spending dozens of tool calls and thousands of tokens per commit on test-batched resume cycles.

- `plugins/dso/scripts/test-run.sh` exists and exposes three subcommands via the `.claude/scripts/dso test-run [start|status|kill]` shim. `start` reads `commands.test_runner` (defined by epic 87e9-0bc8) and launches it as a detached child, writing combined stdout+stderr to `<state_dir>/progress.log`, PID to `<state_dir>/pid`, and — on completion — exit code to `<state_dir>/exit-code` **via atomic write-then-rename** (write to `<state_dir>/.exit-code.tmp`, `mv` to `<state_dir>/exit-code`, then `touch <state_dir>/done` last). `status` prints one of `running <pid>`, `done <exit-code>`, or `idle`. `kill` runs identity-verified liveness check (see below) before terminating + clears state via SIGTERM, grace period from `commands.test_kill_grace_seconds` (default 30s to accommodate pytest teardown / coverage finalization), then SIGKILL.

- Per-session isolation: the DSO session-start hook captures the Claude Code `session_id` from hook input, **sanitizes it to `[a-f0-9-]+` (rejecting any input containing `/`, `..`, whitespace, or path-traversal sequences — fall back to a hash of the raw session_id when the input is non-conforming)**, and writes it to `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dso-test-run/.current-session`. The launcher reads that file to scope all state under `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dso-test-run/<session_id>/`. Two Claude sessions running in different worktrees (or the same worktree) can invoke `test-run start` simultaneously without any shared-state collision. **When `.current-session` is missing (CI runs, session-start hook failed to fire, upgraded plugin with stale hooks), the launcher falls back to a deterministic key derived from `$GITHUB_RUN_ID`, `$CI_JOB_ID`, or a cwd-hash in that precedence order — never silently using a shared default.**

- Same-session duplicate-launch guard with **identity-verified liveness**: when `test-run start` is invoked while `<state_dir>/pid` exists, the launcher tests both (a) `kill -0 <pid>` succeeds AND (b) the process's current cmdline matches the `<state_dir>/cmdline` snapshot written at launch time (guards against PID reuse by an unrelated process). If both match, exit non-zero with an error message whose body contains the exact override command string (`.claude/scripts/dso test-run start --force`). If `kill -0` succeeds but cmdline does not match, auto-clear the state dir (stale-state recovery — PID was reused).

- Atomic duplicate-launch guard: the start subcommand acquires an `flock` on `<state_dir>/.launch-lock` before the liveness check and holds it through the pid write, preventing two rapid-fire `test-run start` invocations in the same session from both passing the check and spawning parallel orphans.

- Stale-state auto-recovery: when the launcher sees `<state_dir>` but `<state_dir>/pid` is missing, or `kill -0 <pid>` fails, or cmdline does not match the snapshot, the launcher silently clears the state dir and proceeds without requiring the override flag. No error, no agent friction, no ticket for stuck state.

- Override flag: `.claude/scripts/dso test-run start --force` unconditionally terminates the recorded PID via the same SIGTERM→grace→SIGKILL ladder the `kill` subcommand uses, but only after confirming the cmdline snapshot matches (refuses to kill a process whose cmdline does not match — returns a clear error). Clears the state dir and starts the new run.

- Orchestrator invocation contract — documented in COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md: the orchestrator invokes `test-run start` via `Bash(run_in_background: true)` to get a `bash_id`. `BashOutput(bash_id)` is used to drain progress streaming only — **it is NOT the completion signal**. Completion is determined by polling for `<state_dir>/done`; on completion the orchestrator reads `<state_dir>/exit-code` as authoritative. This contract is documented with an explicit "do not treat BashOutput return-empty as completion" note.

- Config migration + fail-closed guards: before launching, `start` validates (a) `commands.test_runner` is set and non-empty — if missing/empty, exits non-zero with a fail-closed error (no silently-green gate); (b) the resolved runner path does not reference `plugins/dso/scripts/runners/` — if it does (pre-migration host config), emits a migration warning with the recommended replacement value and exits non-zero. `commands.test_file_runner` uses a documented `{file}` placeholder that the per-file gate substitutes before invocation.

- Host shim compatibility: after upgrading the plugin, a host project that runs `.claude/scripts/dso test-run start` with an outdated shim receives an actionable error directing the user to run `dso update-artifacts`, not a raw `command not found`. The plugin version is bumped in the same commit so existing `update-artifacts` detection triggers on next invocation. COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md documents this upgrade path.

The a524 sprint exercises the new background test-execution primitive on its own commits during sprint execution. At least one sprint commit triggers the new test-run primitive end-to-end (start + wait + complete), and the canary value-validation SC (already in the spec) is exercised on a real sprint code path.
- `.claude/scripts/dso test-run start <test-target>` is invoked during the sprint; status transitions through running → complete; final exit code captured.
- `${TMPDIR}/dso-test-run/.current-session` exists during a run and is cleaned up post-completion.
- The canary value-validation SC's verification command runs against the sprint's own test-execution path (not just a fixture).
| `commands.test_runner` (dso-config.conf) | `/dso:onboarding` writes per detected stack | Re-onboarding refreshes on stack change | test-run primitive; pre-commit gate | N/A — persistent config |
| `commands.test_kill_grace_seconds` | Onboarding default | Operator edit | test-run primitive kill-grace | N/A |

| `${TMPDIR}/dso-test-run/.current-session` | test-run start writes | Updated each new run | test-run wait / status / cmdline-verified-safety | **Retired on run completion** — test-run end removes the file; orphan-cleanup hook at session-start scans for stale sessions (PID dead + .current-session present) and removes them with a structured warning log entry. Closes the audit gap. |

| Plugin version bump | Plugin maintainer at release | Each plugin release | update-artifacts detection | N/A — versioned artifact lineage |
`.claude/scripts/dso test-run start --force` unconditionally terminates in-flight runs + clears state. Pairing with structured governance:

- **Audit log:** every `--force` invocation writes a structured JSON line to `${TMPDIR}/dso-test-run/force.log` with `{timestamp, killed_pid, killed_cmdline, justification, session_id}`. The log is rotated on session end (last 30 entries retained).
- **Required justification companion:** `--force` requires `--reason="..."` with non-empty content; test-run exits non-zero without it. (Hard enforcement.)

- **Abuse-detection at sprint Phase I:** sprint closure invokes `wc -l < ${TMPDIR}/dso-test-run/force.log` (if file exists); count > `test_run.force_alert_threshold` (default 3 per session) surfaces a MUST-display block requiring operator confirmation before sprint closure.
- **Verification:** synthetic test invokes `--force` without `--reason`; asserts non-zero exit + error. Then with `--reason="test"` succeeds; log captures entry.

| `dso update-artifacts` ran in host project | `.claude/scripts/dso --version` returns the expected version after plugin upgrade; `diff <(./.claude/scripts/dso --version) <(<plugin-version-source>)` matches | Test pass |
| `${TMPDIR}` writable for macOS sandbox | `test -w "${TMPDIR}" && touch "${TMPDIR}/dso-probe.$$" && rm "${TMPDIR}/dso-probe.$$"` | Returns 0 |

| Plugin version bump triggers update-artifacts detection | Synthetic: bump version, run session-start hook; assert detection emits the `update-artifacts needed` advisory | Test pass before sprint close |

The "host project operator runs update-artifacts" is an operational responsibility; in-session sprint verification confirms the detection mechanism fires correctly so the operator is reliably prompted. Capability is verified in-session; emergence (operator actually runs it) is operational.

- **87e9-0bc8** (Polyglot test-gate config layer) — depends_on. Epic 87e9-0bc8 defines `commands.test_runner` and `commands.test_file_runner`; this epic's launcher reads those keys. 87e9-0bc8 must land first.

Introduce `plugins/dso/scripts/test-run.sh` with three thin subcommands: `start`, `status`, `kill`. `start` reads `commands.test_runner` via the existing `read-config.sh` shim, validates the resolved command (non-empty, not pointing at deleted `scripts/runners/`), acquires `flock` on `<state_dir>/.launch-lock`, checks for an existing liveness-verified run (kill -0 + cmdline-snapshot match), writes the new pid + cmdline snapshot atomically, then releases the lock and `exec`s the runner via `setsid` (detaching from the controlling terminal to survive orchestrator crashes) with stdout+stderr teed to `<state_dir>/progress.log`. On child exit, `start` writes exit code via write-then-rename and creates the `done` marker last (strict ordering: readers check `done` before reading `exit-code`). `--force` unconditionally executes the cmdline-verified kill-and-clear path. Session state dir is keyed on the sanitized Claude Code `session_id` captured by the session-start hook into `.current-session`; cross-session isolation is a natural consequence of the per-session dir layout. The session-start hook also registers a Stop hook cleanup: when a session ends with a `<state_dir>/pid` still present, the cleanup logs the orphan rather than killing it (detached test process gets to complete its work). CI fallback: when `.current-session` is absent, the launcher derives a session key from `$GITHUB_RUN_ID` → `$CI_JOB_ID` → `sha256(cwd)[:16]`, never from a shared static default. The orchestrator invokes `start` via `Bash(run_in_background: true)` for a `bash_id`, drains progress via `BashOutput(bash_id)`, polls `<state_dir>/done` for completion, and reads `<state_dir>/exit-code` as the authoritative result. The per-file test gate in the pre-commit hook invokes `commands.test_file_runner` with `{file}` placeholder substitution; when the key is unset, the per-file gate falls back to `$commands.test_runner <file>` with the file appended positionally. Migration is a single atomic commit: delete the 6 legacy scripts, add `test-run.sh`, update the 24 caller files, amend dso-config.conf with the new key defaults, and add test coverage for every start/status/kill + --force + stale-state + cross-session + duplicate-guard + cmdline-identity + CI-fallback + config-validation path. Because the atomic commit breaks bisect for regression recovery (the implementation plan notes this), the implementation plan includes a pre-merge validation run on a canary worktree.

**Atomic-commit rationale (defense against split recommendation)**: the Scope reviewer recommended splitting this epic into two — (A) introduce the primitive alongside legacy harnesses, (B) cut over callers and delete legacy. That split was considered and explicitly rejected by the practitioner in favor of a single atomic commit (option `c` in the Phase 1 flag-semantics decision). Rationale: (1) transitional coexistence of two harnesses doubles the test surface and creates a window where some callers invoke the new primitive and others still dispatch via `test-batched.sh`, producing inconsistent test gate semantics across the codebase; (2) the 24 caller updates are mechanical replacements validated by the zero-live-reference grep assertion in SC 8, bounding risk; (3) bisect risk is accepted in exchange for the cleaner cutover. Downside mitigations: pre-merge canary worktree validation (above), the Value validation SC gating closure on measured improvement, and commit revert as the rollback path.

- **setsid orphan survives session end** (`high`, `runtime`): detached test process continues after Claude session ends. Addressed by session-start Stop hook cleanup logging (not killing — the test completion is still valuable); cross-session state isolation means another session cannot accidentally adopt or collide with the orphan.

- **PID reuse collision after stale-state detection window** (`critical`, `runtime`): OS PID reuse could let `kill -0` succeed on an unrelated process. Addressed by identity-verified liveness — cmdline snapshot match required in addition to `kill -0`.

- **Exit-code write race with readers** (`high`, `runtime`): non-atomic write + ordering bug in reader. Addressed by atomic write-then-rename + strict `done` marker ordering (write exit-code first, `done` last; readers check `done` before reading exit-code).

- **SIGTERM grace period insufficient for pytest teardown** (`medium`, `runtime`): 5s insufficient for coverage finalization / fixture cleanup. Addressed by `commands.test_kill_grace_seconds` config key, default 30s.

- **progress.log unbounded growth during long suites** (`medium`, `runtime`): tens of MB on tmpfs could trigger ENOSPC. Noted in implementation plan — add `progress.log` size cap (e.g., 50 MB with head-truncation warning line). Not escalated to SC because it is an operational guard rather than a correctness property.

- **BashOutput drain misses final bytes after done marker** (`critical`, `runtime`): orchestrator treating BashOutput-empty as completion would misread test state. Addressed by the Orchestrator Invocation Contract SC: BashOutput is progress-streaming only; completion = `done` marker; result = `exit-code` file.

- **Concurrent start in same session without lock** (`high`, `runtime`): TOCTOU between liveness check and pid write. Addressed by the atomic-duplicate-launch-guard SC requiring `flock` on `.launch-lock`.

- **session-start hook not registered on upgrade** (`critical`, `deployment`): upgraded plugin with stale hook config fails to write `.current-session`. Addressed by the per-session-isolation SC's CI-and-degraded fallback precedence ($GITHUB_RUN_ID → $CI_JOB_ID → sha256(cwd)); never uses a silent shared default.

- **Atomic migration commit breaks bisect** (`medium`, `deployment`): single commit removes backward compatibility. Addressed in the Approach narrative (pre-merge canary worktree validation). Not escalated to SC because the risk is accepted — user explicitly chose no BC.

- **Host project `.claude/scripts/dso` shim not updated** (`high`, `deployment`): consumer projects need shim refresh. Addressed by the shim-refresh-precondition SC + plugin version bump in the same commit.
- **CI environment lacks session_id** (`critical`, `deployment`): CI is not a Claude session. Addressed by the per-session-isolation SC's CI fallback chain.

- **macOS /tmp cleanup wipes active state** (`low`, `deployment`): 3-day periodic cleanup removes stale state dirs. Mitigated by use of `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}` (macOS `$TMPDIR` is per-user, not auto-cleaned). Not escalated to SC — cleanup of truly idle state dirs is acceptable.
- **`commands.test_runner` missing or empty** (`critical`, `configuration`): silently-green gate allows broken code. Addressed by the config-migration-and-fail-closed SC.
- **`test_runner` references deleted runner scripts** (`high`, `configuration`): pre-migration config points at `scripts/runners/`. Addressed by the same fail-closed SC emitting a migration warning.

- **TMPDIR pointing to non-writable or non-executable fs** (`medium`, `configuration`): `setsid` / exec fails. Addressed by `start`'s pre-flight check on `<state_dir>` writability; exits non-zero with a clear error rather than hanging on `running`.
- **session_id contains path-unsafe characters** (`high`, `configuration`): path traversal via untrusted session_id. Addressed by the sanitization SC — strict charset + fall-through to hash.

- **`test_file_runner` assumes pytest-style file arguments** (`high`, `configuration`): per-language argument conventions differ. Addressed by the documented `{file}` placeholder convention in the config-migration-and-fail-closed SC.

- **Web research (Step 2.6)**: triggered inline during the preceding analysis turn (MindStudio monitor-tool patterns, Claude Code issue #45717 SIGTERM propagation, claude-flow background commands wiki). Bright-line conditions that fired: novel pattern adoption + upstream-tool bug reliance.

- **Scenario analysis (Step 2.75)**: **triggered — red team + blue team sub-agents dispatched** on the retrospective scrutiny pass after user challenge. 17 scenarios generated, 17 surviving blue-team filter (none rejected — all judged possible, actionable, distinct, high-confidence). Eleven of seventeen surfaced genuine spec gaps that drove this revision.
- **Practitioner-requested additional cycles**: yes — user directed retroactive scrutiny run after initial brainstorm:complete tag was applied without dispatching sub-agents.
- **Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5)**: not triggered — no external integration signals (Claude Code internal primitive migration).

- **LLM-instruction signal (Step 5)**: triggered by hook behavioral logic changes (session-start hook). Prior-art not searched separately — the ecosystem analysis from earlier in this session (MindStudio, claude-flow) covered the relevant prior-art domain.
- **Scale context (Step 0)**: not applicable (primitive migration, no volume axis).

- **Initial brainstorm:complete violation**: recorded as bug `3dae-af1a`. Tag was applied without sub-agent dispatch; retroactively removed, scrutiny pipeline executed, SCs revised in response to surviving scenarios, this log corrected.

- Legacy harness removal: `test-batched.sh`, `nohup-launch.sh`, `nohup-poll.sh`, and `plugins/dso/scripts/runners/{bash,pytest,node}-runner.sh` are deleted in the same commit as the callers are migrated. COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md, validate.sh, validate-phase.sh, the test-gate recording script, the per-commit test-gate hook, deps.sh, post-functions.sh, pre-bash-functions.sh, CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md, and every referencing test file (approximately 15) are updated. A tree-wide grep for the four removed script basenames plus the `scripts/runners/` path returns zero live references after the epic lands.

- Value validation (sprint-executable): before closing the epic, a canary worktree runs one representative test-gate cycle under (a) the legacy test-batched path and (b) the new background primitive, on the same commit. The epic closure comment records both tool-call counts and total tokens consumed from dispatch to verdict. Acceptance: the new path completes in ≤3 tool calls (1 dispatch + ≤2 drains) and reduces tokens by ≥50% vs the legacy path on the same suite. Failure to meet either threshold blocks epic closure pending approach revision.

content.text: The DSO ticket system — event-sourced log on an orphan `tickets` branch, reducer-computed state, Jira bridge, optimistic-concurrency STATUS transitions — is a general-purpose LLM-first ticket tracker conceptually decoupled from the DSO plugin itself. Multiple external teams have informally expressed interest in adopting it standalone. Packaging it as a distributable library (pip-installable or npm-equivalent shell script bundle) would let non-DSO adopters consume it without installing the full DSO plugin. This epic does the extraction and packaging work.
- Boundary audit confirms zero imports from `plugins/dso/scripts/` outside the ticket system into the ticket system itself (enforced by `check-plugin-self-ref.sh` equivalent).

- Ticket system ships as an independently installable package with its own semver-released artifacts (tarball or wheel). Installation into a bare git repo produces a working `ticket init`, `ticket create`, `ticket show`, `ticket list`, `ticket transition`, `ticket link`, `ticket deps`.
- Jira bridge ships as an optional plugin (extra-dependency) rather than a required dependency; non-Jira adopters install the core only.
- Reference CLI documentation, migration guide, and contribution guide shipped with the package.

- Integration test: in a scratch git repository, install the package, create an epic with two child stories, transition through states, run a Jira sync (mocked), and verify event log structure via reducer.
- External adopter docs explain: required git layout, orphan `tickets` branch creation, environment variables, and migration from legacy ticket systems.

Identify all cross-module dependencies (`_PLUGIN_ROOT` references, sourcing of DSO-only libraries, config file paths) and extract the ticket system into a self-contained subtree. Introduce a stable public API surface for the reducer and bridge abstractions. Use `pyproject.toml` for the Python portions (reducer, bridge) and a shell script bundle for the CLI dispatcher. Jira bridge becomes `dso-ticket-bridge-jira` as an extras package. Include a migration script for existing DSO-plugin users to switch from in-plugin scripts to the standalone package without event-log disruption.
- Blocks on e1b2-2653 (ticket system boundary enforcement and documentation sweep) — until the boundary is enforced, extraction is infeasible.
- Depends on 78fc-3858 (sourceable ticket-lib API) — external consumers should use the library API rather than subprocess CLI calls.
- Web UI (the CLI + Jira are the only supported interfaces)
- Non-Jira bridges (GitHub Issues, Linear, etc.) — possible future extras packages

content.text: ## Story S4: Stale-state auto-recovery + `--force` override with cmdline safety

**What**: When `test-run start` observes a state dir whose `pid` file is missing, or `kill -0` fails, or the cmdline snapshot mismatches, silently clear the state dir and proceed — no error, no user friction. When invoked with `--force`, unconditionally run the SIGTERM → grace → SIGKILL ladder on the recorded PID, but only after confirming the cmdline snapshot matches. If cmdline does not match, refuse with a clear error (guards against `--force` killing unrelated processes after PID reuse).

**Why**: Without auto-recovery, every orchestrator crash leaves a stuck state dir the user has to clear manually. `--force` is the legitimate "I really do want to restart my own run" path; without cmdline safety it becomes a gun pointed at the user's editor after PID reuse.
- IN: stale-state auto-clear logic, `--force` flag + cmdline-verified termination, error messages for the `--force` refusal case
- OUT: duplicate-launch guard (S3), legacy harness removal (S6)
- When this story is complete, a state dir with a dead recorded PID is silently cleared and `test-run start` proceeds without requiring `--force`

← Satisfies: "when the launcher sees <state_dir> but <state_dir>/pid is missing, or kill -0 <pid> fails, or cmdline does not match the snapshot, the launcher silently clears the state dir and proceeds without requiring the override flag. No error, no agent friction"
- When this story is complete, `.claude/scripts/dso test-run start --force` terminates the recorded PID via SIGTERM → grace → SIGKILL and starts a new run
← Satisfies: "--force unconditionally terminates the recorded PID via the same SIGTERM→grace→SIGKILL ladder the kill subcommand uses"
- When this story is complete, `--force` on a state dir whose cmdline does not match the live process refuses with a clear error instead of sending signals to the unrelated process
← Satisfies: "refuses to kill a process whose cmdline does not match — returns a clear error"
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic
- [Security] cmdline-verified kill prevents signalling an arbitrary process under PID reuse — covered by the same cmdline snapshot mechanism as S3

content.text: Four test runners coexist in DSO: bash-runner.sh, suite-engine.sh, run-hook-tests.sh, and validate.sh. They have drifted on RED-marker tolerance, command_hash tracking, scope coverage, and timeout budget. Each drift was caught reactively post-merge — the bash-runner is updated after a CI failure, not as part of the same change that updated suite-engine. There is no convergence test asserting that all runners produce equivalent classification (pass/fail/skip) for the same input.

This epic delivers the standing equivalence contract test that closes the drift class. Pairs with the ab57-b534 scope expansion (G2-M2), which mandates planner-level corpus updates whenever runner code is touched — this epic is the receiving home for those corpus contributions.
See docs/observed-failure-patterns-4-26.md Pattern 2 and docs/process-gaps-4-26.md G2.
Pattern 2 — Test-runner / gate semantic divergence (~15% of recent fixes):
- 7225-7708 (commit 48a84914e7): bash-runner.sh does not honor SUITE_TEST_INDEX RED markers that suite-engine tolerates; ~25 false-positive failures vs CI; blocks scripts/release.sh precondition #8
- bf39-4494 (commit dc53a44c51): validate.sh --ci infinite PENDING loop because per-file timeout >45s under sequential runner
- e2b6-1059 (commit d1f7877896): validate.sh test scope diverges from CI workflow (validate covers tests/skills, CI covers only tests/hooks + tests/scripts) — main stays green while skills tests fail
- e8a9-136f (commit 9b073eb686): figma-pullback test missing RED-marker registration
- 8305-2091 (open/recent): test-status recording with source-file mode preserves stale failures — fixed tests not re-run
- 610f-c021 (open): test-status recorder blocked by pre-bash-functions.sh guard within /dso:commit workflow
- plugins/dso/scripts/runners/bash-runner.sh:131-133 — comments acknowledge mirroring suite-engine semantics, but the mirror is maintained by hand
- plugins/dso/docs/workflows/REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md:54-116 — reviewer Step 1 runs validate.sh --ci only; does not also run the suite-engine path or compare outputs
- plugins/dso/skills/sprint/SKILL.md — sprint orchestrator dispatches test execution but has no step asserting "if you touched bash-runner.sh, also run the suite-engine equivalence check"

Discovery channel pattern: all four cited Pattern 2 tickets were caught either by validate.sh --ci (release-time integration test) or by CI itself, never by pre-commit. Each fix was authored as a standalone change without a convergence test.

- G2-M1 — Create tests/runners/test-runner-equivalence.sh that takes a fixed corpus of test files (known-passing set, known-RED-marker set, known-skipping set) and runs each through every runner declared in plugins/dso/scripts/runners/. Asserts all runners produce the same pass/fail/skip classification for each file. Add the test to validate.sh --ci. Add new pre-commit hook runner-touch-check.sh that fires only when the diff touches a file under plugins/dso/scripts/runners/ and runs the equivalence test before the commit.
1. A fixed corpus exists under tests/runners/fixtures/ covering the three classification axes (passing, RED-marker, skipping); corpus is documented and stable
2. Equivalence test asserts identical classification across all declared runners; runs in validate.sh --ci
3. Pre-commit hook runner-touch-check.sh runs the equivalence test only when the diff touches runner code; failure blocks the commit
4. New runner additions are detected automatically (the test enumerates runners from a manifest at plugins/dso/config/test-runners.yaml, not a hardcoded list)

5. Each cited drift ticket (7225-7708, bf39-4494, e2b6-1059, e8a9-136f) corresponds to a regression case in the corpus; re-running the equivalence test against pre-fix runner code reproduces the drift
6. Test runtime budget: equivalence test completes in under 30s on macOS local; under 60s in CI
- Pairs with ab57-b534's new sub-criterion (G2-M2 absorbed there): planner mandates a corpus update in any runner-touching task, and this epic delivers the corpus + test that the planner references
- Pairs with New Epic B (G2-M3 reviewer rubric for runner changes): reviewer rubric and equivalence test both fire on the same diff trigger — independent rings of defense
- Coexists with cf7b-86a9's shellcheck/ruff parity work — different surface (test classification semantics vs static lint coverage)

content.text: ## Story S3: Same-session duplicate-launch guard with identity-verified liveness and flock

**What**: Before `start` launches a new child, check `<state_dir>/pid`. If present: (a) run `kill -0 <pid>` and (b) compare the live process cmdline against the snapshot at `<state_dir>/cmdline`. Both match → exit non-zero with an error whose body contains the exact override command string. Only `kill -0` succeeds but cmdline mismatches → auto-clear (PID was reused). Acquire `flock` on `<state_dir>/.launch-lock` before the liveness check and hold it through pid+cmdline write so rapid-fire invocations cannot both pass the check.

**Why**: Without identity-verified liveness, OS PID reuse can cause the launcher to refuse a legitimate new run (or kill an unrelated process via `--force`). Without flock, TOCTOU between check and write lets two rapid-fire `start` invocations both spawn children, orphaning the first.
- IN: pid + cmdline-snapshot writes, identity-verified liveness check, `flock`-gated critical section, error message content
- OUT: stale-state auto-recovery when pid is missing (S5 — same story/file/module as this but a distinct DD), `--force` override (S6)

- When this story is complete, invoking `test-run start` while a liveness-verified active run exists exits non-zero with an error message containing the literal string `.claude/scripts/dso test-run start --force`

← Satisfies: "the launcher exits non-zero with an error message whose body contains the exact override command string (.claude/scripts/dso test-run start --force) so the agent can copy-paste it without guessing"
- When this story is complete, `kill -0 <pid>` succeeds but cmdline snapshot mismatch auto-clears the state dir (PID reuse case) rather than blocking the user
← Satisfies: "If kill -0 succeeds but cmdline does not match, auto-clear the state dir (stale-state recovery — PID was reused)"
- When this story is complete, two rapid-fire `test-run start` invocations in the same session cannot both pass the liveness check (flock serializes the critical section)

← Satisfies: "start acquires an flock on <state_dir>/.launch-lock before the liveness check and holds it through the pid write, preventing two rapid-fire test-run start invocations in the same session from both passing the check and spawning parallel orphans"
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic
- [Reliability] cmdline read source varies by OS (Linux `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`, macOS `ps -o command=`) — handle both platforms uniformly in the identity check
- [Testing] TOCTOU / race-condition tests should deliberately attempt concurrent launches and assert at most one succeeds

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

content.text: Bug analysis of 818 closed bugs identified a cross-cutting failure pattern: mid-workflow orchestrator attention loss after sub-agent Task/Skill completion. Orchestrators receive a result (e.g., REVIEW_RESULT:passed, SKILL_RESUMED) but fail to execute the next required step, going idle or bypassing the result entirely.

Example bugs: 007a-62eb (sprint idle after REVIEW_RESULT:passed, record-review skipped), 7d7a-b707 (skill completes, orchestrator doesn't resume), 8985-4efc (skill result ignored, file read directly instead), b509-0590 (sub-skill dispatch orphans caller).

This is NOT catchable by declarative manifest fields — if the orchestrator stalls, it also fails to update any field. Requires harness-level intervention: a PostToolUse hook that fires after Task/Skill returns and injects an explicit next-step reminder into orchestrator context.
Related to (but distinct from) the broader stage-boundary preconditions manifest epic. That epic catches declarative end-of-workflow gaps; this hook catches mid-workflow attention failures.
- PostToolUse hook fires after Task or Skill tool completion in orchestrator sessions
- Hook reads the sub-agent's structured signal (REVIEW_RESULT, SKILL_RESUMED, COMPLETION_VERIFIER_VERDICT, etc.) from the tool result
- Hook injects a next-step reminder into the orchestrator's context referencing the completed sub-agent type and the expected follow-up action per the skill's workflow contract
- Hook does not fire for sub-agents operating inside another sub-agent (scoped to main-session orchestrator only)
- Coverage: sprint, fix-bug, preplanning, implementation-plan, review dispatches
- Does not block the preconditions manifest epic; they are complementary
- May inform the signal contracts required (if sub-agents need to emit structured handoff signals consistently)

content.text: Placeholder epic tracking patterns where CI (Ubuntu/Linux) catches failures that the local test gate (macOS) misses. Patterns identified from session analysis:

1. **Platform portability (macOS vs Linux)**: mktemp template format (GNU mktemp requires trailing X's for -t; BSD mktemp is lenient), sed -i '' vs sed -i, bash version differences (macOS ships bash 3.2), grep/awk flag differences, stat/date flag differences. Example CI-only failure: tests/hooks/test-hook-inline-trap-consolidation.sh failed on CI because 'mktemp -t prefix' without X's errors on Linux but returns a valid path on macOS.

2. **Script CWD assumptions**: Plugin scripts that assume they run from a specific directory; relative path constructions like '../lib/deps.sh' that fail when CWD changes. Example CI-only failure: plugins/dso/scripts/recipe-executor.sh, scaffold-adapter.sh, and update-shim.sh broke under CI because their '../' relative path resolution was fragile. Local tests pass because local test harness runs from the plugin directory; CI invokes scripts from REPO_ROOT.

3. **ARTIFACTS_DIR context mismatch**: Reviewer sub-agents dispatched into worktrees compute a different ARTIFACTS_DIR (/tmp/lockpick-test-artifacts-<worktree-basename>) than the orchestrator reading from the session branch, causing hash mismatches in the review gate. Systemic gap: no local test reproduces the worktree-vs-session ARTIFACTS_DIR divergence.

4. **Missing Linux-only test coverage in local suite**: CI runs shellcheck (severity=warning) on plugins/dso/scripts/*.sh and hooks, plus ruff check + ruff format --check. The local test gate does NOT run shellcheck on staged shell files and does NOT run ruff across the full Python scope CI checks. Validate.sh runs ruff on app/ only, not on plugins/dso/scripts/*.py. Files like plugins/dso/hooks/*.sh are only shellchecked in CI.

5. **Stale agent worktrees polluting scan results**: scan-config-keys.sh and other static scanners scan .claude/worktrees/ agent directories on local runs, picking up fixture config keys from test files. CI does not have stale worktrees, so scans return cleaner results there. Locally-clean scans can pass CI-dirty scans.
- CI shellcheck coverage: plugins/dso/scripts/*.sh + plugins/dso/hooks/*.sh + **/*.sh -- not run locally in pre-commit or record-test-status flows
- CI ruff scope: plugins/dso/scripts/*.py + tests/**/*.py -- validate.sh only runs ruff inside app/
- CI Linux mktemp/sed/grep flavor: not reproduced by any local test
- Local test gate fuzzy-match only associates tests with source via name similarity — no test exists that validates cross-platform portability of the source under test

**Recommended highest-impact fix**: Add 'shellcheck staged shell files' and 'ruff plugins/dso/scripts+tests' to validate.sh (or a new local-ci.sh script) and wire them into the same pre-commit gate. This would eliminate ~80% of CI-only failure surface area without requiring actual Linux test runners.
See session notes for full details. Priority: investigate systemic patterns and add CI-equivalent local tests.

content.text: This epic applies only when enforcement.strategy=ci AND merge.strategy=pr AND a remote is present (verified by git remote get-url origin). At sprint Phase A, the orchestrator detects mode and emits exactly one of two banners: "MODE: ci-pr" (epic mechanisms active) or "MODE: local — per-story PR mechanisms inactive" (existing local workflow unchanged, no breakage). Local-mode parity is filed as a follow-on epic with this scope: TrackerDefenseStore per-story SHA-range support, in-session /dso:review story-close trigger, local Strategy E equivalent, shared pre-merge validation, dual-mode trailer linking.
- session worktree: Claude Code working directory for a sprint
- session branch: git branch checked out there, source of the long-lived draft PR
- story branch: story/<ticket-id> forked from session branch at story dispatch
- Phase A/E/F/I: sprint orchestration phases (Init / Task Dispatch / Post-Batch Processing / Primary Ticket Closure)
- Strategy A: per-story PR + size-gate (this epic)
- Strategy E: region-split FALLBACK for oversized review surfaces
- hash-of-record: diff_hash + SHA range recorded with each attestation, defining the exact range covered
- long-lived draft PR: single draft PR (session→main) opened at Phase A and refreshed across all stories
- claim-fingerprint: SHA-256 of lowercased, whitespace-normalized claim text
- SPRINT_SESSION_ID: sprint-init-generated UUID; written to .sprint-active marker file at Phase A and exposed to CI as a repository variable (vars.SPRINT_SESSION_ID) refreshed by a Phase A step
- sprint-active state: presence of .sprint-active marker file in artifacts dir; created Phase A, removed Phase I

Today's review pipeline becomes unreliable on large PRs. Empirical PR data on this project since 2026-04-27 (~50 merged) shows every >2-cycle PR was ≥500 LOC and ≥10 files; PR #37 at ~4000 LOC escalated to user with "findings have not converged." Published research (SmartBear/Cisco, Microsoft Research, Google eng-practices) converges on ~200–400 LOC as the reliability cliff. Review-pipeline-side hardening (closed epic 6da2-4cff) addressed reviewer calibration but not surface area. The lever is splitting review into per-story increments on a single long-lived draft PR (Strategy A), with attestation accumulating across stories so the final epic→main merge re-reviews only the unattested delta.

The current /dso:sprint workflow harvests per-task worktrees back to a shared session worktree without per-story isolation, batches mix tasks from multiple stories, and observed reality is that some sub-agents write directly to the session worktree despite worktree.isolation_enabled=true — no leakage detector exists today. This epic adds story-isolated branches with deterministic trailer-based attribution (composing on top of hard dependency 170b-2ac9, which delivers the git-trailer injection library, the DSO-Story/DSO-Task/DSO-Epic trailer schema, and the attribution.enabled config gate), restricts session-worktree commits to merges, fires CI llm-review per-story push against a draft PR pre-created at sprint init, and routes oversized story deltas through a true region-split FALLBACK path (Strategy E) — the current FALLBACK passes the whole diff to one reviewer.

1. Mode detection and ci-pr gating: At Phase A, sprint orchestrator detects mode and emits a banner. Local-mode users see "MODE: local — per-story PR mechanisms inactive" and proceed with existing workflow unchanged. ci-pr-mode users see "MODE: ci-pr" and continue with Phase A draft PR creation. Verification: integration test with mocked git remote get-url returning empty asserts banner is "MODE: local" and no gh pr create invocation occurs; with remote present + ci-pr config asserts "MODE: ci-pr" and PR creation proceeds.

2. Story-isolated branches with merge gating (ci-pr mode only): Sprint creates story/<id> per dispatched story; merges into session branch only after that story's CI llm-review attests passed; orphan trailer commits route to story/orphan-<sprint-session-id>. Verification: post-sprint validation script asserts (a) git branch --list story/* shows exactly one branch per dispatched story plus optionally the orphan branch; (b) git log --merges <session-branch> shows one merge commit per story containing a DSO-Story trailer matching the story ID; (c) no non-merge commit appears on the session branch between story merges.

3. Mandatory DSO-Story trailer with explicit --message injection (ci-pr mode only): Sprint-mode commits via /dso:commit carry a DSO-Story (or routed orphan) trailer; session-branch merges constructed by the orchestrator using git merge --no-ff --message=<msg-with-trailer> so trailers survive on every merge SHA. Pre-commit hook validates trailer presence and rejects commits without a DSO trailer. Verification: (a) trailer-less commit rejected with documented error; (b) integration test asserts git interpret-trailers --parse <merge-sha> returns the DSO-Story line on every story-merge SHA; (c) test outside sprint mode with attribution.enabled=false asserts no enforcement.

4. Session-worktree merge-only policy and deterministic leakage handling (ci-pr mode only): Pre-commit hook scoped to sprint-active state via .sprint-active marker file (created Phase A, removed Phase I). Hook accepts merge commits and rejects all non-merge commits with a clear error directing the user to a story worktree. Escape hatch: setting DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0 env var bypasses the hook for emergency commits with an audit log entry. The release pipeline (merge-to-main.sh) operates outside sprint-active state so its non-merge commits are accepted. When a non-merge commit lands on the session branch (bypassing the hook), the post-Phase-F leakage detector cherry-picks it onto the branch named by its DSO-Story trailer; orphan trailers route to story/orphan-<sprint-session-id>; missing-trailer commits cause sprint to hard-fail with a manual-attribution prompt; closed-story-trailer commits hard-fail with named recovery options (rebase-and-retag with git rebase -i and manual trailer edit, or --force-route-to=<story-id> override flag); cherry-pick conflicts trigger git cherry-pick --abort and emit a hard-fail with the conflicting commit SHA and named conflicting paths. Verification: 5 test cases covering each path including the closed-story-recovery flag exercise.

5. Long-lived draft PR with per-story CI review and region-split FALLBACK (ci-pr mode only): At Phase A the orchestrator opens a draft PR via gh pr create --draft, completing before any story-branch dispatch in Phase E (PR creation is a Phase A blocking step, not concurrent with Phase E push triggers). The merge-to-main-pr.sh "refuse if open PR exists" guard is amended to "refuse if non-draft PR exists" — draft PRs are expected for the long-lived pattern. A new workflow file fires CI llm-review on every push to story/* branches, scoped to merge-base(session, story/<branch>)..story/<branch>, with concurrency-group keyed ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-${{ vars.SPRINT_SESSION_ID }} (using vars context per GitHub Actions docs — env is not allowed in concurrency expressions). The PR-scoped GitHubPRDefenseStore is active from day one. When a story-branch delta exceeds 400 LOC or 15 files, the HUGE-diff FALLBACK path activates true region-split review: file-clustered regions reviewed in parallel by tier-appropriate reviewers, findings deduplicated on (file, line-range, dimension, claim-fingerprint) with line-range overlap matching (not exact-match), conflicting severities resolved to MAX, both rationales preserved as a merged-rationale field when severities differ (no silent rationale discard), opus arch synthesis pass for boundary-only issues. Verification: 5 test cases including overlapping-region fixture asserting dedup with MAX-severity and dual-rationale preservation, and second-push assertion that DefenseStore returns prior attestations on the same story branch.

6. Hash-of-record protocol (ci-pr mode only): Each attestation records the diff_hash at the time of attestation plus the SHA range it covers (story-branch tip SHA, story-branch base SHA). DefenseStore.load_for_region validates by SHA-range membership, not by diff_hash equality alone. Merge commits do not invalidate attestations whose covered SHA range is preserved in the merge ancestry. Verification: integration test merges story A into the session branch, then queries DefenseStore for story A's attestations from a final-PR-context session and asserts the attestations are returned (not stale-invalidated).

7. Bug 4724-41a7 fix as Phase 1 prerequisite (applies to all modes): Resolution of bug 4724-41a7 (Claude Code creates sub-agent worktrees from main repo HEAD instead of session HEAD when orchestrator is in a session worktree) ships as Phase 1 of this epic, before any story-branch infrastructure depends on it. Regression test: dispatching a sub-agent from a session worktree with worktree.isolation_enabled=true produces a sub-agent worktree whose base SHA equals the session HEAD SHA, not the main HEAD SHA. Verification: regression test runs at every CI invocation thereafter.

8. Validation acceptance with inline value-signal (ci-pr mode only): A validation sprint of at least 1500 total changed LOC across at least 3 stories runs the entire pipeline end-to-end and lands one final PR to main. Mechanical proxies: (a) the long-lived draft PR exists from Phase A; (b) every story merge into the session branch carries a DSO-Story trailer readable by git interpret-trailers; (c) each story-branch CI run produces a reviewer-findings.json and writes to GitHubPRDefenseStore; (d) on the final PR ready-for-review transition, DefenseStore.load_for_region returns attestations covering each merged story branch; (e) the leakage detector test suite passes 5-case matrix. Inline value-signal assertion: re-reviewed-LOC / total-LOC < 50% (loose falsifiable threshold to confirm the mechanism reduces re-review surface). The headline "<15% LOC re-reviewed" target is filed as a follow-on observability ticket with continuous tracking via the sprint summary log.

- Hard: 170b-2ac9 (Commit-level source attribution via git-native trailers) must reach closed before this epic enters sprint. Provides DSO-Task/DSO-Story/DSO-Epic trailer infrastructure and attribution.enabled config gate.

content.text: Migrate four existing consumers (harvest-worktree, completion-verifier, merge-to-main archive, ticket CLI list/show) to read PRECONDITIONS events. Add compaction-on-closure with explicit ordering contract relative to Story 4's epic-closure validator. Define legacy-ticket graceful degradation.
- **harvest-worktree** reads PRECONDITIONS via `_read_latest_preconditions` and consumes latest per-stage summary; no behavioral regression on existing harvests.
- **completion-verifier** reads upstream PRECONDITIONS for its story/epic closure checks (coordinated with Story 4's epic-closure validator write path via the ordering contract below).
- **merge-to-main archive** reads PRECONDITIONS to populate archive summary; mixed-format archives (pre-rollout + rollout tickets) render correctly.
- **ticket CLI list/show** reads PRECONDITIONS to display manifest summary; legacy tickets (no PRECONDITIONS events) render with "pre-manifest" placeholder; no blocking, no synthesis.

- **Compaction on epic closure**: after epic-closure validator exits, rewrite all PRECONDITIONS events for the epic into one snapshot event `<ts>-<uuid>-PRECONDITIONS-SNAPSHOT.json`; individual events marked retired.

- **Ordering contract pinned**: (1) epic-closure validator runs BEFORE compaction; (2) compaction uses atomic rename to publish snapshot; (3) Story 1's `_read_latest_preconditions` transparently handles both flat events and snapshot format (snapshot returned only when no live events remain, or snapshot timestamp ≥ all live events); (4) readers retry-once on transient file-missing during compaction window.

- **Legacy-ticket handling**: all four migrated consumers gracefully degrade when a ticket has zero PRECONDITIONS events — log once per (consumer, ticket), proceed without blocking, never synthesize fake events. Mixed-corpus tests (pre-rollout + rollout tickets) pass for every consumer.
- Per-consumer unit tests + integration tests covering the pre-rollout/rollout boundary.
- p95 latency budget per consumer migration step (target TBD in Story 7 contract; measured in Story 6 benchmark).
- [Reliability] Compaction races with concurrent reads — the atomic-rename + retry-once contract must be tested with a fault-injection harness.
- [Maintainability] Legacy-ticket degradation is operational-readiness — document the diagnostic log format so operators can distinguish "missing event" from "corrupt event".
- [Consumer impact] Completion-verifier is both a Story 4 writer and a Story 5 reader — Story 4 depends on this story to avoid the double-modification race.
