content.text: DSO's per-step HARD-GATE workflows (COMMIT, REVIEW) currently express compliance as prose inside the workflow docs. A bot-psychologist Probe B (sycophancy probe against a fresh sub-agent) confirmed the gate is reachable when an agent is challenged but is not load-bearing during silent autonomous execution: agents batch steps, skip advisory breadcrumb writes, drop classifier-flagged overlay dispatches (bug 94e8-9f91), pipe validation output through truncating filters that mask diagnostics, and never write the breadcrumb log (bug 7b41-3061). A user reporter on a host .NET project experienced this across multiple sessions before catching it manually. The same psychology was hardened on the reviewer surface in closed epic db68-ca95; this epic is its orchestrator-side counterpart.

The single outcome of this epic is: ship a load-bearing pre-commit verifier gate that is safe to deploy in production sessions — meaning (a) the gate enforces the right thing, (b) agents cannot silently bypass it, (c) the gate has a sane override path so legitimate commits aren't permanently blocked when the gate is wrong, (d) the gate has zero false positives on existing valid commit paths.

- SC1 — Verifier as load-bearing pre-commit gate. A new pre-commit hook (parity tier with existing test-gate / review-gate) reads the breadcrumb log and wrapper-written validation artifacts for the worktree where the commit is being made and refuses the commit when (a) any expected artifact is missing for a step that should have run under the active enforcement.strategy and SKIP_REVIEW state, or (b) the classifier flagged one or more REVIEW overlays without their corresponding findings artifacts. Test fixtures: synthetically removing a wrapper artifact triggers the block; synthetic missing overlay findings file (with classifier-flagged overlay) triggers the block. Regression tests reproduce the failure surfaces of bugs 94e8-9f91 (overlay flags ignored) and 7b41-3061 (empty breadcrumb log) and confirm both are mechanically prevented as a direct consequence of SC1's enforcement.

- SC2 — Truncation-masking immunity. Validation commands (test, format, lint, classifier dispatch, reviewer dispatch) run through wrappers that capture full output into result artifacts. The verifier reads from the artifact, not from the agent's terminal stream. Test fixture: an agent invoking the wrapper with `2>&1 | tail -3` (or any other agent-side output filter) does not change what the verifier sees and does not allow a hidden lint/test failure to slip through.

- SC3 — Per-commit interactive override path (release-blocking precondition for SC1). A hard-blocking gate is unsafe to deploy without a sane escape hatch for legitimate commits the gate gets wrong. Override is reachable only via explicit `dso commit-override --reason="<text>"` invoked by the user (not the agent). Override applies to exactly one commit attempt and writes a durable audit record (in $ARTIFACTS_DIR and as a comment/trailer on the commit) listing the missing artifacts and the user's reason. Test fixture: a single override clears the next commit; a second attempt without re-authorization is blocked again. Cross-epic constraint: when dso-fbky autonomous mode is active, dso commit-override returns an error and the hook still blocks.

- SC4 — Worktree-context safety in all three execution contexts. Verifier and wrappers behave correctly when commit runs in (a) the main repo, (b) a session worktree, (c) an isolated sub-agent worktree harvested back via the existing harvest-worktree.sh / record-test-status.sh --attest paths. Verifier reads artifacts only from the worktree where the commit is being made; sub-agent artifacts reach it only through the existing harvest path. A wrapper invoked from a CWD that does not match the worktree it would write to fails fast with a clear error rather than silently writing to a sibling worktree's artifacts dir. Test fixtures cover all three contexts plus the misconfigured-CWD failure mode.

- SC5 — Conditional-step skip markers and zero false-positive baseline. Legitimately-skipped steps (e.g., enforcement.strategy=ci, SKIP_REVIEW=true, commands.test_changed unset) emit explicit `skipped:<reason>` artifacts that the verifier accepts. A passing run of validate.sh --ci and a clean DSO-self-commit on this epic demonstrate the verifier introduces zero false positives on existing valid commit paths — the gate fires only on actual non-compliance.

This epic blocks: af26-dd5a-df6d-4f81 (forbidden-action HARD-GATE follow-on; reuses the override-path infrastructure, artifacts-dir resolution, and audit-trail pattern delivered here) and f61f-7e0a-36d3-4e7d (per-story PR review with incremental attestation; f61f's attestation strategy must build on this epic's verifier — clarified during f61f's own brainstorm).
Subsumed: bugs 94e8-9f91 (overlay flags silently dropped) and 7b41-3061 (breadcrumb log empty) close as a direct consequence of SC1 — no separate work axis.
Related, not blocking: closed epic db68-ca95 (reviewer-side AI-blindspot hardening — same psychology, different surface).

Wrapper-driven artifact verification (Option A from Phase 2). Each per-step validation command (test, format, lint, classifier dispatch, reviewer dispatch) is invoked through a thin wrapper (`.claude/scripts/dso commit-step <name>`) that runs the underlying command, captures the full output, and atomically writes a result artifact alongside the breadcrumb. A new pre-commit hook reads the artifacts (not agent stdout) and refuses commits with missing artifacts, missing overlay findings, or visible truncation markers. Override is reachable only via `dso commit-override --reason="..."` invoked by the user. The verifier resolves artifacts via get_artifacts_dir() of the worktree where commit happens; cross-worktree artifact transfer remains via the existing harvest-worktree.sh / --attest mechanism — no new cross-worktree paths.

- Resource: per-commit override mechanism. Interaction: dso-fbky autonomous mode must NOT bypass this epic's verifier or override path. Gate: when autonomous mode is active, dso commit-override returns an error and the hook still blocks on missing artifacts.

- Resource: artifacts-dir / harvest atomicity. Interaction: 70f6-05f1 parallel-worktree review introduces N concurrent harvests. Gate: harvest into a target worktree's artifacts dir is atomic per-target; verifier does not race when multiple sub-agent worktrees harvest concurrently.

- Resource: reviewer-findings artifact family. Interaction: dbbc-cf67-8cfc-4b4d stateful re-review persists multi-cycle review state. Gate: overlay-dispatch verification reads the latest cycle's classifier output and findings files; multi-cycle state does not produce false-positive missing-findings blocks.

- Resource: test step execution path. Interaction: a524-fded migrates test execution to a background primitive. Gate: the wrapper for the test step captures full output regardless of whether the underlying test command runs synchronously or backgrounded.

- Resource: skipped-step structural records. Interaction: a154-98de PRECONDITIONS degradation channel introduces structural attestation for graceful-degradation paths. Gate: SC5 skipped:<reason> markers conform to the same schema as PRECONDITIONS attestation records, or the schemas are explicitly aligned in a follow-up.

- Resource: silent-skip detection psychology. Interaction: e884-d0ad PostToolUse forced next-step reminder targets the same root-cause failure mode at a different point in the loop. Gate: pre-commit verifier and PostToolUse reminder do not double-fire on the same skip event; one is authoritative for any given skip class.

- Resource: commit message construction order. Interaction: 170b-2ac9 commit-level source attribution via git-native trailers. Gate: artifact verification runs before trailer injection; ordering documented in COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md.

- Resource: breadcrumb log format. Interaction: 5df7-63ac integrated observability. Gate: breadcrumb log entries written by wrappers include observability-compatible fields (timestamp, step name, agent context, optional cost hooks) so 5df7-63ac can consume the same log without duplicating infrastructure.

- Resource: wrapper-written artifact metadata. Interaction: e407-d35c source attribution. Gate: wrapper artifacts include attribution metadata fields (skill name, agent ID, sub-agent context) that e407-d35c can read without separate metadata files.

- Resource: classifier / reviewer dispatch interface. Interaction: f9f8-a15c-79e0-4dc3 add Gemini provider to CI LLM review provider abstraction. Gate: wrapper output capture for classifier and reviewer dispatch is provider-agnostic; the artifact contract does not depend on a specific provider.

- Resource: hook installation pipeline. Interaction: 87e9-0bc8 polyglot test gate modifies reinstall-hooks.sh. Gate: the new pre-commit verifier registers via the same install path; hook execution order documented so polyglot test-gate and verifier compose deterministically.

- Resource: pre-commit gate execution order. Interaction: 88d2-6756 / jira-dig-1671 required CodeQL + code-quality scanning gates. Gate: artifact verification, CodeQL scanning, and other pre-commit gates each run as discrete steps that compose; no implicit dependence on each other's output beyond pass/fail signaling.

- Resource: reviewer override semantics. Interaction: jira-dig-1673 reviewer override discipline. Gate: dso commit-override composes with — does not bypass — reviewer override discipline; user-invoked override does not silently dismiss reviewer findings; produces an audit record both gates can consume.

- Resource: REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md overlay-dispatch verified-artifact set. Interaction: cbea-3722 ACCESSIBILITY_REVIEWER agent integration. Gate: when accessibility reviewer is dispatched as part of REVIEW Step 4b, its findings file is part of the verified-artifact set; missing accessibility-findings.json (when accessibility was flagged) triggers the same block as missing security-redteam-findings.json.
11 surviving failure scenarios from red/blue team filter (16 raised; 5 filtered as speculative or already-handled).

- CWD mismatch fast-fail triggers inside legitimate sub-agent worktrees during harvest — wrapper's CWD check must compare resolved target artifacts dir's worktree root, not process CWD, or every harvest invocation rejects.
- New pre-commit hook not executable after fresh clone or plugin sync overwrites it — git silently skips non-executable hooks; entire load-bearing gate is bypassed without error.
- Artifact write and pre-commit hook read race under parallel sub-agent harvest; spurious gate failures during in-flight harvests.
- Wrapper artifact write swallowed when underlying command times out (~73s ceiling); missing artifact with no diagnostic trail.
- a524-fded background test primitive output not captured when test runs detached; empty/stub artifact misinterpreted as test failure.
- ARTIFACTS_DIR undefined in CI environment causes hook to crash or resolve to wrong path.
- Hook added after existing pre-commit hook causes silent override of prior hook chain in host projects.
- First-run artifact directory missing causes hook to block all commits before any wrapper has run.
- commands.test_changed unset causes wrapper to emit no artifact and hook to block instead of skip.
- review.max_resolution_attempts exhaustion + verifier block produces deadlock — agent has no automated path to unblock.
- Breadcrumb log path diverges between wrapper write and hook read when worktree uses non-default branch name with special characters.
- Bright-line conditions that fired: none (no third-party API, no new dependency, no auth/credentials, no migration; wrapper pattern is established internally via existing test-gate / review-gate)
- Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 11 (of 16 red team findings)

- **Practitioner-requested additional cycles**: cross-epic scan re-triggered via gate (manual triage initially; full classifier dispatch on practitioner authorization, surfacing 1 additional ambiguity (f61f-7e0a-36d3-4e7d) and 8 additional considerations injected as Cross-Epic Interactions ACs)
- **Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0)**: triggered — depth: 0 (forbidden-action HARD-GATE follow-on stub created as af26-dd5a-df6d-4f81; scrutiny intentionally skipped at practitioner's direction)

- **LLM-instruction signal (Step 5)**: triggered — keyword: hook behavioral logic (bot-psychologist Probe B during pre-Phase 1 covered the orchestrator behavioral surface; concrete prompt edits will go through plan-review during /dso:preplanning)

content.text: Placeholder epic capturing the research baseline for considering idempotent task semantics in `/dso:implementation-plan` output. The reference pattern (from `navapbc/bao-nguyen-agent-skills` and similar projects): every task an agent emits checks for existing state before performing the action — grep Gemfile before appending; check generator already-run before invoking; collision-detect before scaffolding. Currently DSO's planning skills emit tasks that describe desired state without idempotency guards; the implementer (human or sub-agent) is responsible for state-checks at run time.
This epic is NOT yet brainstormed; it is a durable capture of research so the work can be picked up in a future `/dso:brainstorm` session without re-doing the survey.
## Research baseline (2026-05-08, dispatched as part of Epic B brainstorm)

Surveyed 15 popular agentic / AI-assisted code-generation projects: Cline, Roo Code, Cursor (Composer), Continue.dev, Aider, GitHub Copilot Workspace, SWE-agent, OpenHands/OpenDevin, Devin/Cognition, Goose (Block), Cody (Sourcegraph), Augment Code, smol-developer, MetaGPT, CrewAI, plus LangGraph as orchestration framework reference.

Adoption strength: **weak-to-moderate** (high confidence). Idempotent task semantics as an explicit, default-enforced design principle is rare across the surveyed tools. The dominant pattern: file-write tools overwrite freely; user approval (or git-revert recovery) is the guard, not pre-write state checks. Diff-based editing reduces blast radius but doesn't enforce existence checks.

Strongest exception: LangGraph's persistence/checkpointing layer prevents re-execution of completed workflow tasks (workflow-level idempotency). LangGraph docs *recommend* idempotency at the task level but do not enforce it.

`bao-nguyen-agent-skills` is one of the few projects where the pattern is enforced explicitly at the workflow-as-skill scale — every skill grep-checks Gemfile before appending, checks for existing files before generator invocation, etc. It is a small public collection (4 skills), not a widely-adopted framework.
- GitHub Copilot Agent double-edit bug: "Agent will edit a file twice, fixing the issue twice, often making worse code" — vscode-copilot-release#9439

- "LLM agents retry tool calls 15-30% of the time due to timeouts, validation errors, or model uncertainty. Without idempotency, a simple retry could corrupt a file, duplicate a transaction, or crash a workflow." — fast.io/resources/ai-agent-idempotent-operations/
- Armin Ronacher's "chaos monkey" principle: tools must be "protected against an LLM chaos monkey using them completely wrong." — lucumr.pocoo.org/2025/6/12/agentic-coding/
- Anthropic engineering on long-running agents: state-verification-before-action via progress notes + git log review. — anthropic.com/engineering/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents

- Where does the idempotency guard live: in the task TEXT emitted by `/dso:implementation-plan` (a guard clause like "skip if Gemfile already contains gem X"), or in the TOOL LAYER (a file-write wrapper that checks before acting), or at the WORKFLOW LAYER (LangGraph-style checkpoint)? These have very different implementation costs and failure modes.
- False-skip rate: how often would an idempotency guard incorrectly conclude "already done" and skip a legitimately-needed update?
- Sub-agent compliance reliability: do DSO's sub-agents reliably honor guard clause language, or treat it as advisory like LangGraph does?
- Specific semantics of "idempotent" for our purposes: workflow-level, task-level, or operation-level?
- Pilot scope: which task type to pilot the pattern on first (e.g., "add dependency to manifest file") before universalizing?
- Interaction with DSO's testing_mode discipline: how does idempotency-by-default coexist with RED test gating?
- `navapbc/bao-nguyen-agent-skills` — small public skill collection where the pattern is enforced explicitly
- This baseline was dispatched during Epic B (Strata SDK planning context) brainstorming on 2026-05-08; full sub-agent report lives in this session's transcript.
Captured for future brainstorming. Do NOT plan or implement until `/dso:brainstorm <epic-id>` has been run interactively. Tagged `scrutiny:pending`.

content.text: Multi-skill HARD-GATEs in brainstorm, sprint, fix-bug, and implementation-plan SKILL.md files prohibit specific actions during specific phases — e.g., "do not write code until brainstorm Phase 3", "do not dispatch new sprint batch without committing previous", "do not skip fix-bug phase ordering". The sibling epic's fix (post-hoc artifact verification) does not fit forbidden-action gates because they concern actions that haven't happened yet (or shouldn't). The fix shape is tool-use-time enforcement via PreToolUse hooks that block forbidden tool calls during specific phases, sourcing phase state from durable session metadata that the relevant skills already track.

This is a stub epic created during the sibling epic's brainstorm session as an explicitly-named follow-on. It requires its own /dso:brainstorm session before implementation — the SCs below are stub-quality and will be refined, scrutinized via the full pipeline, and approved during that session.

Blocked by the sibling epic (wrapper-driven artifact verification for HARD-GATE per-step workflow compliance) — the override-path infrastructure (dso commit-override audit-trail pattern), the artifacts-dir / get_artifacts_dir() worktree-resolution logic, and the session-state-aware hook installation pattern are all reused.

content.text: Placeholder epic for incorporating a Strata DSL as ingested INPUT context at the start of `/dso:brainstorm` — analogous to how brainstorm currently reads `PRD.md` and `.claude/design-notes.md` for project context. The DSL would augment the brainstorm dialogue with structured Strata-specific facts about the epic being designed (existing form structure, case shapes, business process steps that already exist in the project, etc.), giving the brainstorming agent richer grounding without forcing structural commitments that belong in implementation.
This epic is NOT yet brainstormed; it is a durable capture so the work can be picked up in a future `/dso:brainstorm` session without re-doing the analysis.

- **DSL is INPUT context, not OUTPUT artifact**: user does NOT review or interact with the DSL during brainstorming. The DSL is consumed silently by the agent; the user sees the resulting prose epic spec as today.
- **Ingestion happens at the START of brainstorming**: equivalent to existing PRD/design-notes loading at Phase 1 Step 1; the agent has DSL context available before Socratic dialogue begins.
- **Scope is brainstorm-only initially**: do NOT generalize to preplanning/implementation-plan as DSL emitters or transpilers. Expanding scope is a separate future decision.
## Why this is a placeholder rather than part of Epic B

Epic B (Strata SDK planning context) deliberately excluded DSL emission/validation/transpilation as too architecturally heavy. B's tradeoff analysis (full DSL pipeline = schema + emitter + validator + transpiler + sprint integration; multiplicative complexity for incremental fidelity gain) concluded LLM-based validation against `decomposition.md` was sufficient for the validation use case.
This epic is a NARROWER scope: DSL as INPUT only (one direction; no emission). That sidesteps most of B's complexity concerns. It still deserves its own brainstorming because:
- DSL discovery mechanism (where does the DSL come from?) is its own design problem
- DSL schema rigidity (full Strata DSL vs. thin feature-manifest YAML?) needs evaluation
- Multi-source DSL handling (form DSL + API DSL in one epic?) needs a model
- Versioning between DSL schema and Strata SDK schema needs a sync strategy
- Interaction with B's tiered facts/guidance — does DSL context coexist, complement, or supersede facts content?

- `navapbc/lockpick-il-ides` — Strata DSL pattern in practice (Flow + Model + Controller as structured representation; round-trips to SDK generator commands). Lockpick uses DSL primarily for REVERSE engineering (extract from existing code → generate app). Our use case is FORWARD design, so the DSL serves a different purpose: as input grounding for the agent, not as a generated artifact.

- Epic B (Strata SDK planning context) — predecessor; this epic builds on B's tiered facts (`concepts.md` / `decomposition.md` / `implementation.md`) and adds DSL as a fourth context source available to brainstorm only.
- DSL discovery: where does the DSL live? Pre-existing artifact in the repo? Path passed to /dso:brainstorm as a flag? Auto-extracted from existing code via a tool akin to lockpick's `/parse-form`?
- DSL schema rigidity: full Strata DSL (Flow + Model + Controller classes), thin "Strata feature manifest" YAML, or both supported?
- Multi-source DSL: an epic spanning form + API DSL — do we ingest both? How does the agent disambiguate?
- DSL ↔ SDK schema versioning: how are the two kept in sync? Regeneration tool reads both?
- Interaction with B's tiered facts: when DSL context is present, does it supersede `decomposition.md` for the specific concepts the DSL covers, or coexist as complementary detail?

- Token cost: tiered facts already weigh against token economy; adding DSL ingestion further loads brainstorm's context window. Does DSL replace some facts content for in-scope concepts, or stack on top?
- Discovery for non-existent DSL: most epics will not have a DSL artifact to ingest. Detection-and-graceful-skip path needed.

- User-facing surface: should the brainstorming agent surface DSL-derived insights to the user (e.g., "I see your existing intake form has fields X, Y; this new feature could extend it as Z") — that's still NOT user review of the DSL, but is it information disclosure the agent makes?
Captured for future brainstorming. Do NOT plan or implement until `/dso:brainstorm <epic-id>` has been run interactively. Tagged `scrutiny:pending`.

content.text: **What**: Define and implement the recovery contract for dso-config.conf auto-migration when the migration is interrupted (SIGKILL between mktemp write and mv, disk full mid-write, EROFS surfacing after a partial in-memory translation).

**Why**: S4's flock + atomic mktemp/mv handles the happy-path race. It does not specify a recovery story for partial migrations or hand-rolled recovery by users hitting disk-full or interrupted processes. Without an explicit backup-and-restore contract, users have no documented path back to a working state.

- IN: Backup file naming convention (e.g., `dso-config.conf.v1.bak` written before the atomic rename); restore command/instructions; behavior detection for half-written tempfiles (cleanup on next run); recovery test where SIGKILL fires between tempfile write and mv; recovery test for disk-full after backup but before tempfile write; documented EROFS persistent fallback (in-memory translation + WARN, no backup attempt).
- OUT: Migrating consumer code (S5); the atomic write itself (S4); pre-commit hook (S7).
- When complete, a backup of the v1 file is written before any v2 atomic rename ← Satisfies: SC2
- When complete, an interrupted migration (SIGKILL between tempfile write and mv) is detectable on next run; orphaned tempfiles are cleaned up; user is warned via [DSO WARN] log ← Satisfies: SC2

- When complete, unit tests written and passing for SIGKILL recovery and disk-full edge cases
- [Reliability] Backup creation must itself be atomic enough that a crash mid-backup is recoverable
- [Maintainability] Document EROFS as the one path where no backup is created (in-memory translation only)

content.text: After A2's onboarding wires Strata-aware DSO config, planning skills (`/dso:brainstorm`, `/dso:preplanning`, `/dso:implementation-plan`) still have no SDK awareness. Plans propose intake forms as plain Rails models, miss `strata:application_form` generators, recommend `belongs_to :case` (forbidden by SDK design), invent attribute types the SDK already provides (`:money`, `:tax_id`, `:memorable_date`). This epic delivers tiered facts (concept / decomposition / implementation) auto-regenerated from upstream `strata-sdk-rails` plus per-skill manual guidance, loaded conditionally per epic-level `strata:scoped` tag set by brainstorm. Brainstorm uses concept-level facts in every Strata-detected project to assess SDK fit; sets the tag in its emitted epic spec; preplanning + implementation-plan inherit and load deeper tiers only when scoped. Plan-validation extends existing scrutiny prompts with SDK-aware checklists derived from the decomposition tier — no new sub-agents.

- `concepts.md` (~30 lines): three SDK concepts (ApplicationForm, Case, BusinessProcess) with class doc-comment purposes; four generator names with one-line purposes; two UI surfaces; SDK layer position

- `decomposition.md` (~60 lines): generator chain rules; base attributes per generator; domain model relationship rules (Case→Form via `application_form_id:uuid`, NOT `belongs_to`); Pundit policy structural requirement

- `implementation.md` (~120 lines): exact CLI signatures with hyphenated flag spelling (e.g., `--application-form` not `--application_form`); Strata attribute type registry; file path conventions per generator; class hierarchy; gem dependencies + Rails version compatibility
- `README.md`: index documenting which file is loaded by which skill at which abstraction tier
- `brainstorm.md` (~30 lines): when-to-use Strata SDK vs. plain Rails; common epic shapes for SDK; capability-verification heuristics

- `preplanning.md` (~30 lines): story-decomposition heuristics for SDK chains; E2E nudge for Strata-scoped epics ensuring acceptance criterion exercises SDK call sequence; multi-concept reconciliation checklist for red-team

- `implementation-plan.md` (~30 lines): pitfall WHYs (ActionController::API hook mechanics; Case-Form FK rationale; generator chain semantics; underscored-flag silent-ignore); SDK test helper exemplars (~15 lines: signature table only — `fill_address`, `choose_yes`, `fill_ssn`, `fill_date`, `click_next`, `start_next_task`, `wait_for_conditional` — citing lockpick as implementation source, marked exemplars not canonical)

- `/dso:brainstorm` — gated by A2's project-level detection (STRATA_DETECTED=yes + STRATA_TEMPLATE_KIND=rails + strata.skip != true). When gated open, Reads `concepts.md` + `guidance/brainstorm.md` at Phase 1 Step 1 (~60 lines). During Phase 1 Gate Step 2, if `STRATA_UNCERTAINTY` binary signal fires (capability-verification cannot be answered from concepts.md alone), on-demand Reads `decomposition.md` for deeper structural verification. At Phase 2 Step 2, brainstorm sets `strata:scoped` tag on epic based on its structural fit assessment. Tag UX disclosure: brainstorm emits visible inline message on tag set/unset with override path. Tag lifecycle symmetric (set + unset paths supported via brainstorm re-runs)

- `/dso:preplanning` — gated by epic's `strata:scoped` tag. Tag-scoped read (bound to specific epic-id, not global). When gated open, Reads `concepts.md` + `decomposition.md` + `guidance/preplanning.md` at appropriate phases (~120 lines). Read-after-write fence: preplanning's first action verifies tag present with retry + escalation
- `/dso:implementation-plan` — gated by epic's `strata:scoped` tag (inherited via story → epic chain). When gated open, Reads all three facts + `guidance/implementation-plan.md` (~240 lines)

- Plan-validation extension (no new sub-agents): existing scrutiny prompts (preplanning red-team / blue-team / phase-e-adversarial-review; implementation-plan gap-analysis) gain conditional Strata-violation checklist sections that load when Strata context is present. Conditional sections OMITTED (not empty blocks) when epic lacks `strata:scoped`. Section header named "REQUIRED when strata:scoped tag present", positioned EARLY in prompt. Checklist content data-driven from `decomposition.md` structural-rules section. Validation checks: plan uses SDK generators; Case→Form via `application_form_id:uuid`; Pundit policy required; generator flags hyphenated; chained generators not double-invoked; multi-concept consistency

- Regeneration tool (`plugins/dso/scripts/regenerate-strata-sdk-facts.sh`): pinned to specific upstream `strata-sdk-rails` tag/commit recorded in `plugins/dso/scripts/lib/strata-template-vars.sh`. Reads SDK source via `gh api` at pinned ref. Parses generators (class_option/argument declarations + invoke calls), attribute types (Strata::Attributes module includes), class hierarchy, gem dependencies, route definitions, class doc-comments into structured intermediate (JSON). Renders three views from intermediate. Each output gets `# AUTOGENERATED — do not hand-edit; regenerate via plugins/dso/scripts/regenerate-strata-sdk-facts.sh` header + `# strata-sdk-facts-schema-version: 1` + `# pinned-sdk-ref: <tag-or-commit>` + completeness flag (`# completeness: full | partial-conditional-chain-<N> | partial-runtime-types-<N>`). Documents 5 spike-identified caveats inline (conditional generator chains as `[optional]`; Pundit-as-mixin not auto-generated per model; Determination's hardcoded paths exception; Rails 8 compat pending; runtime-registered attribute types not in registry)

- Manual-residual handling via `plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/strata-sdk-facts/manual-residual-index.json`: schema `{ topic_id: string (unique key), content: string (markdown fragment), last_modified: ISO 8601 timestamp }`. Regeneration script reads index, regenerates auto sections, splices manual content via deterministic key-lookup. LLMs never preserve markers because there ARE no markers in auto-generated content. Manual-residual-index.json hand-edits permitted (not gated by CI fresh-check)
- 5 behavioral guarantees with observable failure modes:
- Atomicity: facts file writes + manual-residual restoration are atomic. Concurrent reader sees partial-content facts file → guarantee violated

- Drift-detection correctness: weekly CI cron runs regeneration against latest upstream HEAD; substantive structural diffs trigger advisory PR. Substantive upstream change without advisory PR within 7 days → guarantee violated

- Fail-open-on-load: missing/malformed facts files do not block planning skills; emit clear `[B] facts unavailable; running without Strata context` warning; fall back to non-Strata behavior. Missing facts file blocks a planning skill → guarantee violated
- Tag-scoped-read: planning skills read `strata:scoped` tag bound to specific epic-id, never global. Planning skill loads facts when target epic lacks tag → guarantee violated

- Cross-skill-consistency: brainstorm tag write completes before exit; preplanning verifies tag presence before loading. Brainstorm completes setting tag; preplanning's first action sees tag absent → guarantee violated
- Single shared facts load for parallel reviewers: orchestrator loads facts ONCE and passes content to each scrutiny reviewer; reviewers do NOT re-Read facts files

- STRATA_SKIP early evaluation: each planning skill checks `strata.skip` BEFORE any Strata Read or sub-agent dispatch. Sub-agents inherit a `STRATA_SKIP=true` env var when set. STRATA_SKIP fail-open: when signal absent (A2 not yet merged or renamed), gating treats absence as `STRATA_SKIP=false` (proceed with detection)

- Spike-baseline artifact at `tests/audits/B-feasibility-spike-results.md` (PRE-SPRINT GATE): captures both 2026-05-07 concepts spike + 2026-05-08 decomposition+implementation spike findings, sample extractions for `strata:application_form`, the 5 documented caveats. Pre-sprint gate behavioral test at `tests/scripts/test-b-pre-sprint-gate.sh` exercises gate against fixture with/without spike artifact

content.text: After a Strata project is scaffolded — by Epic A1's `create-dso-app.sh` or by manual `nava-platform`/`gem "strata"` adoption — `/dso:onboarding` is unaware of Strata. It writes generic `commands.*` keys that silently shadow Strata's Make targets (the friction the CI/CD audit flagged), misses well-documented Strata footguns (e.g., `ActionController::API` load-time crash, Case→Form FK violation), and never tells users about `nava-platform app update` as the canonical upgrade path. This epic adds Strata-awareness to the consolidated `/dso:onboarding` (per 136b-6758) via a sibling detector script, a `prompts/strata/` topic-prompt directory loaded surgically by phase mechanism, and ONE Socratic-confirmation dialog turn (non-tech UX = one yes/edit/no click). Detection feeds A0's namespaced array; config writes consume A1's shared `strata-config-defaults.conf` (drift prevention).

- New `plugins/dso/scripts/detect-strata.sh` (sibling to `detect-stack.sh`). Scans for `.template-*/<file>.yml` markers at PROJECT root (per A1's spike); reads `_src_path` to sub-classify (`framework:strata-rails` / `framework:strata-nextjs` / `framework:strata-flask` / `infra:strata`); reads `_commit` for upgrade-lifecycle context. Gemfile fallback uses canonical fingerprint `gem ['"]strata['"].*github:\s*['"]navapbc/strata-sdk-rails['"]` (NOT bare `gem "strata"`). Emits namespaced tags into A0's `stack` array per the v2 schema. Writes structured detection-facts artifact at `${WORKFLOW_PLUGIN_ARTIFACTS_DIR}/strata-detection.env` (KEY=VALUE: STRATA_TEMPLATE_KIND, STRATA_COMMIT_PIN, STRATA_SRC_PATH, STRATA_DETECTION_SOURCE in {marker, gemfile-fallback}). YAML field values written via `printf '%s=%q\n'` (bash-quoted) to prevent injection. `mkdir -p "$WORKFLOW_PLUGIN_ARTIFACTS_DIR"` before write. Multiline-aware Gemfile scan via awk (handles continuation patterns). Glob `**/.template-*/[a-z][a-z0-9-_]*.yml` supports monorepos. Reusable by Epic B's planning skills.
- `README.md`: index documenting which sub-file the architect-foundation/dialogue phases load at which step; tags each sub-file silent vs. dialog

- `config-writes.md` (silent): sources A1's `plugins/dso/scripts/lib/strata-config-defaults.conf` (ships in plugin filesystem); writes `commands.*` keys per detected `STRATA_TEMPLATE_KIND`. Multi-template projects: union per A0's multi-valued schema. Append via normalize-then-write helper (split on `;`, dedupe, rejoin) to prevent semicolon corruption

- `arch-enforcement.md` (silent): appends Rails-Strata footguns from shared defaults to `.claude/ARCH_ENFORCEMENT.md` if `framework:strata-rails` is in stack array. Footgun idempotency keys on stable HTML-comment markers (e.g., `<!-- strata-footgun:rails:no-action-controller-api -->`), NOT raw rule text. Semantic overlap check before append: grep for keywords like `ActionController::API`, `belongs_to :case`; if found, emit `[A2 WARN] potential conflict: existing rule may overlap with Strata footgun '<title>'; review ARCH_ENFORCEMENT.md` and skip that footgun

- `posture-dialog.md` (dialog): one Socratic turn presenting STRATA_DETECTION_SOURCE, detected template(s), `_commit` pin(s), `_src_path`(s), and the upgrade hint as the dialog's pre-filled default. Four responses: `yes` / `edit` / `not Strata` / `[I no longer use Strata]`. `not Strata` cleanup removes Strata tags from in-memory stack array; comment in project-understanding.md notes "User declined Strata configuration on YYYY-MM-DD". Non-interactive context (no TTY): default to `yes` (proceed with detected defaults) with audit log; documented in README.md. Strata-removal 4th response (`[I no longer use Strata]`) removes Posture section + footguns + Strata commands.* values

- `posture-writer.md` (silent, runs after posture-dialog approval): atomic write via mktemp + mv -f. Writes approved `## Strata Posture` section to `project-understanding.md`. Idempotent (replaces existing section if present; otherwise appends)

- The relevant 136b-6758 phase files (architect-foundation, dialogue) gain phase-conditional Reads of these sub-files when `platform:strata` in stack array. Sequencing: config-writes during config emission step; arch-enforcement during enforcement scaffolding step; posture-dialog during dialogue/confirmation step; posture-writer after posture-dialog approval.

- `detect-strata.sh` wired into A0's detector-orchestration so its output unions into the unified `stack` array (NOT a separate config key). Documented in A0's `DETECTION-SCHEMA.md` as a worked example of "adding a sibling detector".

- New `--no-strata` flag for graceful skip on older plugin versions (when `prompts/strata/` subdirectory missing); explicit error if missing without flag: `[A2] requires prompts/strata/ from plugin v<min>+; update plugin or pass --no-strata`. Documented one-liner migration: `bash plugins/dso/scripts/detect-strata.sh && /dso:onboarding --resume=strata-only` re-runs detection + four sub-files without re-running other phases. STRATA_SKIP signal: `--no-strata` writes `strata.skip=true` to dso-config.conf; sprint/brainstorm/preplanning check this key for graceful degradation.
- Pre-commit hook `check-no-stack-case.sh` self-exclusion list covers the hook's own source, the synthetic-detector fixture, the schema doc's anti-pattern section.

- `dso:completion-verifier` validation on Strata-detected runs: (a) `commands.*` matches `strata-config-defaults.conf` for the detected variant, (b) all 5 Rails-Strata footguns present when `framework:strata-rails`, (c) `## Strata Posture` exists in `project-understanding.md`.

- `tests/scripts/test-detect-strata-fixtures.sh` against 7 fixtures (rails-with-marker, nextjs-with-marker, flask-with-marker, infra-with-marker, manual-gemfile-only, no-strata, multi-template-rails-and-infra)
- `tests/scripts/test-onboarding-strata-idempotency.sh` — fresh-from-A1 fixture: zero diffs in `commands.*`, `ARCH_ENFORCEMENT.md`, `## Strata Posture`

- `tests/scripts/test-onboarding-strata-fresh-detection.sh` — manual-adoption fixture (Gemfile fingerprint match, no markers): asserts Gemfile-fallback fires, posture-dialog notes detection-source, post-`yes` writes land

- Behavioral tests cover: not-Strata cleanup (asserts tags removed from stack array after dialog), non-interactive default (asserts dialog auto-yes when no TTY), version-skew error path (asserts clear error message + `--no-strata` skip works)
- Strata SDK planning context for brainstorm/preplanning/implementation-plan (Epic B)
- NextJS/Flask-specific footguns (v1 Rails-only; SDK is Rails-only)
- Multi-template disambiguation dialog (A0's multi-valued `commands.*` handles natively)
- Modifications to 136b-6758's phase mechanism — A2 consumes the mechanism as documented

1. Detection emits correct namespaced tags + facts artifact across 7 enumerated fixtures: (1) rails-with-marker (fresh A1 scaffold); (2) nextjs-with-marker; (3) flask-with-marker; (4) infra-only-with-marker; (5) manual-gemfile-only (Gemfile fingerprint match, no markers); (6) no-strata (negative case); (7) multi-template (Rails+infra). Each golden-master asserts emitted stack-array additions AND `strata-detection.env` contents. Malformed-marker case asserts non-zero exit + clear stderr naming the file.

2. Fresh-from-A1 idempotency: `/dso:onboarding` on A1-scaffolded project produces ZERO file diffs in `commands.*`, `ARCH_ENFORCEMENT.md`, `## Strata Posture`. Posture dialog presents detected facts; `yes` completes phase with no content changes. Confirmation receipt printed: "Strata detected — configured commands.* (test_runner=make test, lint=make lint-ci, ...), added 5 footguns to ARCH_ENFORCEMENT.md, wrote ## Strata Posture to project-understanding.md. No further Strata questions." Verified by behavioral test asserting (a) zero diffs (b) dialog-turn count = 1 (c) receipt content present.

3. Manual-adoption Gemfile-fallback: fixture with multiline-aware Gemfile fingerprint match and no markers triggers fallback. Two assertions: (a) `dso-config.conf` contains correct `commands.*` key-value pairs (unit assertion); (b) `validate.sh --ci` invokes the correct command string when run on the fixture (integration assertion).

4. Phase wiring + completion-verifier: `prompts/strata/README.md` documents sub-file/phase/step mapping; phase files Read sub-files at documented steps; `dso:completion-verifier` confirms (a) `commands.*` matches shared-defaults file, (b) all 5 footguns present (when Rails-Strata), (c) `## Strata Posture` exists. Behavioral tests cover not-Strata cleanup, non-interactive auto-yes, version-skew `--no-strata` skip, strata-removal 4th dialog response.
5. No Strata writes on non-Strata projects: `/dso:onboarding` on a non-Strata fixture produces zero `prompts/strata/*` Reads, zero Strata-specific writes, no Strata mention in any artifact.

6. Reviewer enforcement loop verified: A behavioral test submits a diff containing an `ActionController::API` subclass to a Strata-configured Rails project fixture; the code-reviewer agent returns at least one finding that references the ARCH_ENFORCEMENT.md footgun by keyword (e.g., contains `ActionController::API` or the footgun title). Test fails if findings list is empty OR if no finding references the footgun.

13 surviving scenarios from red/blue team filter (10 filtered). Mitigations folded into Robustness contract: silent-exit detection failures (explicit error + non-zero exit), ARTIFACTS_DIR creation (mkdir -p before write), multiline Gemfile (awk), not-Strata cleanup (tag removal from stack array), atomic writes (mktemp + mv), semicolon-corruption (normalize-then-write helper), monorepo (glob support), non-interactive default (auto-yes with audit log), KEY=VALUE injection (bash-quoted printf), posture-writer atomicity (mktemp + mv), version-skew (`--no-strata` flag + clear error), footgun text drift (HTML-comment markers as idempotency keys), footgun semantic overlap (warn rather than blind-append).

Layered detection (sibling `detect-strata.sh` to existing `detect-stack.sh`, output unioned into A0's array) plus tiered prompt sub-files in `prompts/strata/` directory loaded surgically by phase mechanism. Single Socratic dialog turn for posture confirmation; rest is silent application. Sources A1's shared defaults file for drift prevention. Robustness mitigations across 13 surviving scenarios.

At least one full strata-aware onboarding run produces a populated `## Strata Posture` section in `project-understanding.md` AND writes the strata-detection.env keys.

- The detect-strata.sh script's Socratic-confirm step is exercised (transcript shows the dialog OR `--non-interactive` mode is used with the result recorded).

| `strata.skip` (dso-config.conf) | `/dso:onboarding` writes false at project setup; operator can flip true to disable | Operator edit | detect-strata.sh; brainstorm/preplanning/impl-plan strata gates | N/A — persistent per-project |

| `STRATA_TEMPLATE_KIND` (strata-detection.env) | detect-strata.sh writes after detection + Socratic confirm | Re-detection on stack change; manual re-run of detect-strata.sh | Brainstorm, preplanning, impl-plan strata-aware gates; create-dso-app.sh | Implicit with `strata.skip=true` flip OR project teardown |

content.text: The current `scripts/create-dso-app.sh` clones a hardcoded fork of Strata's NextJS template with DSO infrastructure baked into the fork's files. The fork is NextJS-only (precluding Strata SDK access, which is Rails-first) and detached from `platform-cli`'s install/upgrade lifecycle, so it drifts from upstream Strata over time. There's no way for a non-technical user to scaffold a Strata Rails+SDK+USWDS prototype with one command. This epic rewrites the installer to invoke `nava-platform app install` against upstream Strata templates (Rails default, pinned to v1.0.0), apply a DSO overlay, and deprecate the fork — using a phased script structure with extracted overlay engine and pre-implementation feasibility spike (already executed and recorded as a baseline at `tests/audits/A1-feasibility-spike-results.md`).

- Restructure `scripts/create-dso-app.sh` into six explicit phases: `parse-args` → `check-prereqs` → `invoke-platform-cli` → `apply-overlay` → `rails-sdk-add` → `emit-summary`. Each phase is a bash function; failures emit `[A1] phase=<name>` tagged errors and a "what to do next" hint.

- New shared script `plugins/dso/scripts/apply-host-overlay.sh` (the overlay engine): walks `plugins/dso/templates/host-project/`, applies `{{PROJECT_NAME}}` substitution per the existing installer convention, copies into target, leaves a one-line audit comment in dso-config.conf. Reusable beyond create-dso-app.sh.

- New in-plugin overlay tree `plugins/dso/templates/host-project/`: canonical DSO files (CLAUDE.md template, dso-config.conf, .pre-commit-config.yaml, project-understanding.md skeleton, design-notes.md skeleton, ARCH_ENFORCEMENT.md skeleton) with `{{PROJECT_NAME}}` placeholders matching the installer's substitution patterns.

- Ship `plugins/dso/scripts/lib/strata-config-defaults.conf` — shared canonical definition file mapping each Strata template variant to its `commands.*` values, Rails-Strata ARCH_ENFORCEMENT footguns, and Strata Posture section template. Single source of truth — sourced by A1's `apply-overlay` phase AND by A2's `prompts/strata/config-writes.md` + `arch-enforcement.md`. A1 MUST NOT independently define `commands.*` keys — sources from this file. A1 writes the FULL Posture section (not a skeleton) using install-time-known `_commit` and `_src_path`, so A2's onboarding-time idempotency check produces zero diffs.
- Tickets orphan-branch creation post-overlay; explicit `git push origin tickets` exit-code check; remote conflict surfaced with clear error and exit non-zero.

- CLI flags: `--app-name=<name>` (positional kept for back-compat plus added as flag), `--port=<num>` (default 3000), `--template=rails|nextjs|flask` (default rails), `--no-sdk` (skips Rails SDK gem add), `--no-overlay` (skips DSO overlay), `--auto-install-prereqs`, `--help`. Phase-tagged errors and recovery hints.

- Defensive guard against unknown Copier vars: at `check-prereqs`, parse upstream `copier.yml` at pinned commit hash (via `gh api`) and diff required-var list (name + type + accepted-values for enums) against hardcoded list in `plugins/dso/scripts/lib/strata-template-vars.sh` (where copier.yml is the source of truth and the hardcoded list is the script's coverage map). content.text: DSO's `detect-stack.sh` emits a single string (`python-poetry`, `ruby-rails`, `node-npm`, etc.) that conflates orthogonal axes — language, package manager, framework, infrastructure, CI platform, platforms-on-top. The flat schema cannot honestly describe a real project (a Strata Rails app on Terraform AWS deployed via GitHub Actions reduces to `ruby-rails`), and each pending first-class-platform epic (Java 70d5-37ee, Terraform jira-dig-1582, Jenkins jira-dig-1583, .NET ee22-4785, Azure DevOps 622a-3955, Strata Epic A2) compounds case-explosion in consumers that switch on the singular value. Polyglot projects cannot be represented at all. This epic migrates the schema to a namespaced flat array, preserving every existing value as an array element for back-compat, in-place across all consumers, with auto-migration of existing project configs and explicit in-session safety nets to mitigate the big-bang risk profile.

- Rewrite `plugins/dso/scripts/detect-stack.sh` to emit comma-separated namespaced array. Existing values (`python-poetry`, `ruby-rails`, `node-npm`, `golang`, `rust-cargo`, `ruby-jekyll`, `convention-based`, `unknown`) preserved as elements; atomic decompositions added (`python`, `ruby`, `node`, `go`, `rust`, `bundler`, `cargo`, `npm`, `poetry`, `rails`, `jekyll`); namespaced forms added (`language:ruby`, `package_manager:bundler`, `framework:rails`). When a compound value is detected, the array always includes both the compound form for back-compat AND every namespaced decomposition; the compound form is never suppressed.

- Author `plugins/dso/docs/DETECTION-SCHEMA.md`: namespaced-tag convention; axis enum (`language`, `package_manager`, `framework`, `infrastructure`, `ci`, `platform`, `build_system` — extensible); legacy-compound preservation rules; consumer query patterns; whitespace-strip rules; empty-value to `unknown` semantics; trailing-empty-element-strip; multi-`stack=` rejection at parse time; detector authoring guide.
- Update `plugins/dso/docs/CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md` to v2: `stack` and `commands.*` schemas; v1 to v2 migration table; semicolon delimiter for `commands.*` documented.

- Migrate every legacy-pattern consumer in DSO from singular-equality to array-membership. Pre-migration inventory committed as `tests/audits/A0-stack-consumer-inventory.md` BEFORE any migration commit. Known consumers: `resolve-stack-adapter.sh:44`, `prefill-config.sh:138`, `project-detect.sh:346,348`. Inventory is the migration checklist; sprint stories sized one-per-consumer; `dso:completion-verifier` confirms checklist 100% before A0 closes.

- Add pre-commit hook `check-no-stack-case.sh` blocking future legacy patterns. Documented self-exclusion list covers the hook's own source, the synthetic-detector fixture, the schema doc's anti-pattern section; future tests use `# stack-case-exempt: <reason>` annotation.

- Auto-migrate existing project configs: when a v2-aware consumer reads `dso-config.conf` with legacy singular `stack=`, rewrite to v2 array using `flock` advisory file lock + `mktemp` + `mv` rename atomic write. Idempotent on v2 configs. Edge cases: missing trailing newline, malformed YAML rejected with named-line error, comments preserved, multiple `stack=` lines rejected, empty `stack=` migrated to single-element `unknown` array, read-only filesystem (EROFS) gracefully falls back to in-memory translation with `[DSO WARN]` log.

- Upgrade `commands.*` to multi-valued (semicolon `;` separator, NOT comma — chosen to avoid collision with comma-bearing command args like pytest `-k 'foo,bar'`): `commands.test_runner`, `commands.lint`, `commands.format`, `commands.format_check`, `commands.lint_ruff`, `commands.lint_mypy`. `commands.lint_ruff` and `commands.lint_mypy` are pre-existing single-valued keys being retrofitted; the polyglot fixture exercise is limited to `commands.test_runner` and `commands.lint`.
- Add `depends_on` link + one-line "blocked on A0" comment to each pending platform-integration epic: 70d5-37ee, jira-dig-1582, jira-dig-1583, ee22-4785, 622a-3955.

- Test fixtures (`tests/fixtures/stack-detection/`): one per existing stack value, two polyglot combinations (Python+JS, Ruby+Terraform), one Strata-anticipation fixture (`.template-application-rails/<name>.yml` with `_commit` + `_src_path`).
- Synthetic-detector behavioral test (`tests/fixtures/detect-fake.sh` + `tests/scripts/test-synthetic-detector.sh`): exercises new tag introduction AND collision case.

- Pre-cutover review checklist appended to the final commit's PR body for the deep-tier reviewer: audit clean, fixture tests green, round-trip tests green, smoke run green, inventory 100% checked, polyglot fixture executes both runners.
- Detector implementations for new platforms (Strata = Epic A2; Java, Terraform, Jenkins, .NET, Azure DevOps = the linked epics).
- Per-detection confidence scoring; per-detection source-file attribution; JSON/YAML detector output formats.
- Multi-runner CI orchestration logic; per-axis precedence rules at the detection layer.
- Renaming/restructuring `dso-config.conf` keys beyond the migration noted.
- Rollback escape hatch (env var) — declined; rollback is `git revert` of the release.
- CI cache invalidation logic for the mixed-state-during-partial-deploy scenario — release-notes guidance only.

1. Detection emits namespaced array per fixture, including Strata-anticipation. Running `detect-stack.sh` against each fixture in `tests/fixtures/stack-detection/` (eight existing stack values + two polyglot combinations + one Strata-anticipation fixture) produces a comma-separated array matching golden-master assertions in `DETECTION-SCHEMA.md`. The Strata-anticipation fixture (with `.template-application-rails/<name>.yml`) plus a stub Strata detector together produce an array containing `ruby,bundler,rails,ruby-rails,language:ruby,package_manager:bundler,framework:rails,framework:strata-rails,platform:strata`. End-to-end smoke test runs `validate.sh --ci` against the polyglot fixture (Python+JS) AND asserts the emitted stack array contains exactly `{python, ruby, poetry, bundler, python-poetry, ruby-rails, language:python, language:ruby, package_manager:poetry, package_manager:bundler, framework:rails}`. The multi-command iteration path through `commands.test_runner` is exercised (both `pytest` and `npm test` execute and report separately). Verified by `tests/scripts/test-detect-stack-fixtures.sh` passing in CI.

2. All consumers migrated; existing configs auto-migrate idempotently. Pre-migration inventory `tests/audits/A0-stack-consumer-inventory.md` enumerates every legacy-pattern hit before migration commits. Post-migration, the same audit script returns zero legacy-pattern matches across `plugins/` and `.claude/`. Pre-commit hook `check-no-stack-case.sh` blocks reintroduction with documented self-exclusion list. Round-trip tests cover (a) v1 to v2 rewrite on first read with audit comment using atomic write+flock, (b) v2 idempotency, (c) edge cases — missing trailing newline, malformed YAML rejected with file+line error, comments preserved, multiple `stack=` rejected, empty `stack=` to `unknown`, EROFS graceful fallback with warn-log.

3. `commands.*` keys are multi-valued; polyglot iteration verified. Schema documents semicolon-separated lists for the listed `commands.*` keys. SC3's exercise is bounded to `commands.test_runner` and `commands.lint`; other listed keys retrofitted but not fixture-exercised in this epic. The polyglot Python+JavaScript fixture demonstrates `commands.test_runner=pytest;npm test` with both runners executing during one `validate.sh --ci` run, both results reported separately, empty trailing list elements stripped.

4. Synthetic-detector and collision behavioral tests pass with specific outcomes. `tests/fixtures/detect-fake.sh` synthetic detector emits a new namespaced tag (`platform:fake`) AND a tag colliding with an existing compound (`ruby-rails` from a non-Ruby fixture). Test asserts: (a) the synthetic `platform:fake` tag is present in consumer output without error; (b) the colliding `ruby-rails` tag from the non-Ruby fixture is deduplicated to a single occurrence in the emitted array; (c) no gate exits non-zero solely due to the collision.

5. Detector author can implement a new detector using only the published contract; documentation and dependent epics linked. A detector author can implement `detect-terraform.sh` (or any pending platform-integration detector) using only the published `DETECTION-SCHEMA.md` contract, with no changes to shared consumer code; verified by the synthetic-detector behavioral test passing without modification to any consumer in `plugins/dso/scripts/`. `DETECTION-SCHEMA.md` and `CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md` v2 published; referenced from `CLAUDE.md`. Each of 70d5-37ee, jira-dig-1582, jira-dig-1583, ee22-4785, 622a-3955 has a `depends_on` link to A0 and a one-line "blocked on A0" comment.
10 surviving scenarios from red/blue team filter; mitigations folded into In Scope. 1 critical scenario (mixed-state partial deploy) declared OUT (release-notes guidance).
- Auto-migration concurrent race (high, runtime) — flock + atomic mktemp/mv
- commands.* embedded comma collision (high, runtime) — `;` separator
- Pre-commit hook self-trigger (high, deployment) — self-exclusion list
- Mixed state during partial deploy (critical, deployment) — OUT of scope; release-notes only
- Read-only CI checkout (high, deployment) — EROFS in-memory fallback
- Smoke run polyglot coverage (high, deployment) — SC1 explicit
- Empty `stack=` (high, configuration) — empty to unknown semantics
- Trailing empty list element (medium, configuration) — strip-empty rule
- Multiple `stack=` lines (high, configuration) — reject at migration time

Big-bang in-place migration in one epic with explicit in-session safety nets: pre-migration consumer audit committed as artifact; post-migration audit-gate enforcement (zero legacy patterns); pre-commit hook preventing reintroduction; fixture matrix covering all stack values plus polyglot plus Strata-anticipation; auto-migration round-trip tests with edge cases; synthetic-detector + collision behavioral tests; end-to-end smoke run; pre-cutover review checklist for deep-tier reviewer.

| v2 `stack` array (dso-config.conf) | Auto-migration script rewrites v1→v2 at first /dso:onboarding run post-upgrade; `/dso:onboarding` writes fresh on new projects | Operator edit; multi-stack project adds entries | All stack-aware scripts (detect-stack.sh, generate-semgrep-config.sh, polyglot test gate, polyglot kudos triggers, mutation-testing.yml) | N/A — persistent per-project; entries removed when stack uninstalled |

| Semicolon-delimited `commands.*` keys (multi-value support) | Auto-migration or onboarding write | Operator edit; APPEND-by-default, operator must explicitly clear to overwrite | Polyglot consumers parse on `;` | N/A — persistent |

| `verification:legacy`-style v2 migration sentinel | Migration script writes once at first v1→v2 conversion | Stable | /dso:onboarding skips re-migration on subsequent runs by reading the sentinel | **Removed after the v1→v2 migration window closes (operator manually unsets when v1 support is dropped from the plugin entirely).** The plugin maintains v1 read-compat for a documented N-version window; the sentinel is RETIRED at the version boundary when v1 read-compat is dropped. |

| `# stack-case-exempt` inline annotations (in dso-config.conf) | Operator manually adds when a stack name needs case preservation | Operator edit | Migration / detection scripts skip case-normalization for annotated lines | N/A — persistent per annotation; removed manually if no longer needed |

| Pre-commit hook self-exclusion list | Hook installation step writes the exclusion list (the hook excludes itself + the migration script from its own checks) | Re-installation rewrites; manual edit otherwise | The hook reads at every commit | Removed if the hook is uninstalled |

| `tests/audits/A0-stack-consumer-inventory.md` (consumer audit artifact) | Sprint that ships this epic writes the initial inventory | **UPDATE owner: each future epic that adds a new stack-consuming script is responsible for adding its consumer entry to this file** (preplanning-checklist item; CI grep test asserts that any new script under `plugins/dso/scripts/` matching `*stack*` has an entry in the inventory) | Operators reviewing stack-detection scope; future audits | N/A — persistent project artifact; closes the audit's "future consumer drift" gap by making each new consumer add itself |
- The added CI grep test (or its addition is filed as a preplanning task for the sprint) catches new stack-consumers missing from the inventory.

No upstream blockers. Downstream sequencing constraint: Epics A2 and B must NOT implement stack-keyed conditional logic until A0 is merged. Dependency chain enforces this (A2 lists A0 + 136b-6758; B depends on A0 + A2). If A2 or B implementation begins before A0 lands, they accept a second migration when A0's array schema activates. Soft coordination with 136b-6758 on the prompts/<topic>.md mechanism's contract — A0 records a one-line clarification comment confirming "a topic-prompt loads when its identifier appears in the stack array".

- OUT: Auto-update of pinned ref (manual ref bumps in v1).

content.text: Developers submitting PRs through CI receive review findings that may be invalid or overstated. PR-80's attribution review (closed bug d42d-8126) found 8 of 11 CI-produced findings were invalid or had overstated severity, causing developers to waste cycles resolving phantom issues and eroding trust in automated CI review. Two required schema fields — cited_excerpt (verbatim text from the cited file, >=5 chars) and reachability (>=20-char path-from-entrypoint sentence, required for {critical, important, fragile}) — were added on main (commit 729d2c2075) to force reviewers to ground findings in real code. Local /dso:review enforces these via validate-review-output.sh. The CI llm-review path (dso_ci_review/runner.py) bypasses that validator entirely — merged findings are written to disk at line 937 with no schema check in between. A future reviewer prompt change that adds a required field will silently regress in CI, putting developers back into the phantom-finding-resolution loop and undoing the calibration just landed.

- When CI llm-review produces a finding that violates the schema, the validation step detects it and triggers exactly one correction dispatch before findings are written to disk; if review.schema_correction_max_attempts=0 the correction step is skipped and the path goes directly to the synthetic-error path.

- When correction dispatch returns schema-valid findings with the same number of findings as the input AND byte-for-byte preservation of frozen fields (severity, category, description, file_path, line_range, finding_id), CI llm-review proceeds with the corrected findings and the job passes. If correction returns valid JSON but a different finding count or mutates any frozen field, correction is treated as failed and the synthetic-error path fires.

- When correction dispatch fails to produce valid findings (validation still fails, count drift, frozen-field mutation, exhausted retries, or max_attempts=0), a synthetic schema_error finding (severity: critical, type: "parse_error" — already recognized by validate-review-output.sh as exempt from cited_excerpt/reachability checks) is appended, the existing severity gate fires, and CI exits non-zero with a stderr diagnostic naming the specific schema errors. Verified by appending the synthetic and re-running validation — no infinite loop.

- The validation step shells out to validate-review-output.sh code-review-dispatch <tmpfile> with an explicit subprocess timeout (default 60s). When the validator binary is missing/non-executable, the subprocess times out, or returns an unrecognized exit code, runner.py emits a critical stderr diagnostic and exits non-zero — never silently skipped. Local /dso:review and CI enforce identical rules (zero drift).

- A new config key review.schema_correction_max_attempts (default: 1, documented intended range: 0–3, hard ceiling: 3 to prevent runaway LLM cost) is added to CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md and dso-config.conf; the runner clamps any value above the ceiling to the ceiling and logs a warning.

- Regression tests in tests/skills/dso_ci_review/test_runner_smoke.py cover: (a) valid findings pass through unchanged; (b) missing cited_excerpt → corrected → pass; (c) missing reachability on critical severity → corrected → pass; (d) repeated correction failure → synthetic schema_error → non-zero exit; (e) silent severity mutation during correction → treated as failure → synthetic schema_error. At least one test invokes validate-review-output.sh live (not mocked) to exercise the actual shell contract.
None — all upstream work (cited_excerpt + reachability schema enforcement; calibration approaches 1, 2, 4) landed on main via commits 729d2c2075 and 59a6671f97.

Insert schema validation between merge_findings() and _write_output() in dso_ci_review/runner.py (line 937 insertion point). Write merged findings to a mktemp file, invoke validate-review-output.sh code-review-dispatch <tmpfile> via subprocess with 60s timeout. On non-zero exit, parse stderr (line-prefixed format) for schema errors. Build dispatch_schema_correction() in dispatch.py wrapping existing dispatch_review() with a correction-mode prompt fragment (new file plugins/dso/docs/workflows/prompts/reviewer-schema-correction.md) containing the original findings + specific schema errors + frozen-field constraint. Max retries from review.schema_correction_max_attempts (default 1, ceiling 3). On persistent failure, append synthetic schema_error finding (severity: critical, type=parse_error — validator-recognized as exempt from cited_excerpt/reachability).
- subprocess timeout on large payloads (high, runtime) — mitigated by SC4 explicit timeout
- correction mutation causes second schema violation (high, runtime) — mitigated by SC2 count + frozen-field preservation, SC3 fail-closed
- validate-review-output.sh missing/non-executable (critical, deployment) — mitigated by SC4 fail-loud
- reviewer-schema-correction.md not bundled (high, deployment) — covered by SC4 fail-loud on missing resources
- max_attempts=0 silently skips synthetic (high, configuration) — mitigated by SC1+SC3 routing
- max_attempts large value cost (medium, configuration) — mitigated by SC5 hard ceiling
- stderr parsing unstable across error types (high, assumption) — stderr contract documented; SC6 live test asserts
- dispatch_review reuse → finding count or frozen-field drift (high, assumption) — mitigated by SC2 dual-check
- synthetic exemption not recognized by validator (critical, assumption) — mitigated by SC3 using validator-recognized parse_error type
- smoke tests miss live shell contract (medium, assumption) — mitigated by SC6 live-invocation requirement
The correction prompt fragment (plugins/dso/docs/workflows/prompts/reviewer-schema-correction.md) must address three behavioral risks surfaced by the bot-psychologist review:

- Behavioral review (Sonnet bot-psychologist): three failure modes identified when LLMs are asked to "correct your own output" — silent in-place mutation of fields the prompt only forbids in prose (Sycophancy); phantom cited_excerpt reconstruction from memory rather than file re-read (Phantom Capability); laundering of upstream quality failures by treating the original output as immutable ground truth (Confidence Calibration).
- Recommendations to apply in the prompt fragment during /dso:implementation-plan:

1. Frozen-field enumeration (positive constraint, not just prose negative): "The following fields are FROZEN — copy them byte-for-byte from the original: finding_id, severity, category, description, file_path, line_range. You may only write to: cited_excerpt, reachability."

2. Explicit read-then-copy for cited_excerpt with __UNREADABLE__ sentinel: "For each finding where cited_excerpt is missing: read the file at file_path at lines line_range; copy that exact text — do not paraphrase, summarize, or reconstruct from memory. If the file is not readable, set cited_excerpt to __UNREADABLE__ — do not invent content."

3. Schema-only scope preamble: "This correction call is SCHEMA-ONLY. You are not re-reviewing the code. You are not re-evaluating severities. You are not adding context. If you believe a finding is substantively wrong, that is out of scope here — write the schema fields as required and return."
- Coordination — 1de7-50d4 (Resolution/reporter enum): if it adds new schema fields, validator rules update once; shell-out inherits automatically (no spec coupling needed).
- Coordination — 3c01-3b89 (Per-sub-branch reviewed batches): depends on this epic (depends_on link already exists).
- Coordination — 84da-9ad3 (Hallucination detection): should run after schema validation when it lands (document the ordering in 84da preplanning).

- Validation signal: run the updated CI llm-review path against the PR-80 diff (the diff that produced 8/11 invalid findings in bug d42d-8126). Verified outcome: zero synthetic schema_error findings appended (the reviewer's output passes schema validation on the first attempt or after one successful correction), and 100% of real findings contain non-empty cited_excerpt and the required reachability sentence (when severity is critical, important, or fragile). Document the schema-compliance rate in the PR description as evidence that the calibration problem is closed.

Build a new `code-reviewer-verifier` sub-agent that runs unconditionally between every reviewer and `record-review.sh`, independently re-reading each cited file/excerpt to confirm the asserted defect is real, and emitting one of `confirm | downgrade-to-minor | drop` per finding before findings reach the PR or autonomous-resolution loop.

The existing `code-reviewer-arbiter` is a *post-defense* dispute adjudicator (trinary SUSTAIN / ACCEPT_DEFENSE / DOWNGRADE), invoked only on `ESCALATE_REVIEW` or `oscillation_no_arbiter_engagement` signals. It cannot catch the d42d failure modes (misread, hallucinated off-by-one, stale line ref) because invalid findings reach the PR untouched and consume autonomous-resolution attempts before any defense escalates them. A separate pre-surfacing verifier is needed.

PR-80 evidence: 8 of 11 round-2 findings invalid or overstated; an autonomous-resolution agent acting on them would have introduced complexity for non-bugs (flock wrapper for non-existent race in N3, refactored loops to fix non-existent off-by-one in N1).

2. Dispatch step in `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/runner.py` between reviewer dispatch and `record-review.sh`.
3. Schema for verifier ruling per finding; integration with the new `cited_excerpt` field (Approach 1) so verification is anchored.
4. Behavioral test fixtures: known-misread diff, known-hallucinated diff, known-valid diff.
5. Telemetry: drop/downgrade/confirm counts per cycle so we can measure the calibration delta.
- Approach 1 (`cited_excerpt` required field) lands first — verifier uses excerpts as the anchor for its file reads.

content.text: In a local Claude Code session with PR merge strategy, `merge-to-main.sh` should drive an interactive loop in which the session agent is the LLM dispatch engine for any work the script needs done. Specifically, the local-mode loop should:

1. **Detect and resolve git merge conflicts** — when the branch diverges from main during push (e.g., another PR landed first), surface the conflicts to the session agent, let the agent resolve them, then continue.
2. **Monitor the PR CI run** — poll `gh pr checks` until all required checks complete; identify failures (test failures, lint, llm-review findings, security gates, etc.).

3. **Dispatch failure resolution** — for each detected failure, hand the session agent a structured task describing the failure category and the artifacts it needs (failing test name + log, llm-review finding + diff context, lint error + path, conflict files). Agent does the fix in-session, pushes, the script re-enters monitoring.
4. **Loop until green or escalate** — repeat (2)-(3) until CI passes OR a bounded number of iterations elapses OR the agent escalates a specific item as unfixable.

The local-session loop should reach the same end state that the CI-only auto-merge loop reaches when `_LLM_DISPATCH_CMD` is wired in CI: PR merged (or queued to merge) without manual operator round-trips.
The script fails out on the first issue it cannot resolve itself, and the session agent has to do every step manually with no orchestration help from the script:

* **Issue 1 — Unresolved threads / CI findings**: `_phase_resolve_threads` checks `_LLM_DISPATCH_CMD` at line 1050. When unset (as it is in every local session — the helper was deleted in S3 with no shipped default), the script emits `ESCALATE: _LLM_DISPATCH_CMD not set` and returns 1. Even if `_LLM_DISPATCH_CMD` were set, the next layer (`_pr_dispatch_unresolved_batch` line 660) checks `_dso_is_ci_environment` and emits a local escalation when not in CI, regardless of the var. So local sessions cannot use this code path at all.

* **Issue 2 — CI-failure remediation**: `_dispatch_fix_agent` (line 1406) has the same shape: `_REMEDIATE_LLM_CMD` required, plus a CI-environment guard. Local sessions cannot trigger automated CI fix loops.

* **Issue 3 — Merge conflicts**: `_phase_resolve_conflicts` uses `_RESOLVE_CONFLICTS_LLM_CMD` (line 1271, same shape). When unset locally, conflict resolution can't run. Observed in this session: the script created PR #89, the user landed PR #88 in parallel which conflicted on `.test-index`, and I (the session agent) had to manually fetch main, merge it, hand-resolve the duplicate-key, push. The script provided zero orchestration for that work — it just exited with the push complete and the PR in `CONFLICTING` state.

The net result: in a local PR-merge-strategy session, the script does exactly the part that doesn't need LLM dispatch (branch push + PR open), then exits. Everything else — conflict resolution, CI monitoring, failure remediation, review-thread response — falls back to the session agent doing it free-hand with no shared state, no resume mechanism, no bounded loop.

The script's contract for LLM-driven steps is: invoke an external `<cmd> <prompt> <user-message> <tier>` helper, parse stdout for action markers. That contract assumes the helper exists OUT-OF-PROCESS and runs to completion non-interactively. It does NOT model the local-Claude-Code case where:
1. The LLM dispatch IS the calling agent (this session).
2. There is no separate dispatch process to invoke; the work happens between script invocations, not within one.

3. The right protocol is: the script emits a structured \"AGENT_TASK:...\" handoff describing what to do, then exits cleanly; the agent does the work and re-enters the script (e.g., via `--resume`); the script resumes monitoring; loop until the script declares done or escalates.

* Affected: every `/dso:end-session` / `/dso:commit` flow that ends in `merge-to-main.sh` against a `merge.strategy=pr` repo from a local session. Today that means every brainstorm/preplanning/sprint/fix-bug session that lands its work via PR.

* Adjacent: `/dso:fix-bug`, `/dso:debug-everything` — these are the agents that would actually do the failure-remediation work the loop hands off to, but they have no input contract from `merge-to-main-pr.sh` for inheriting \"here's the failure to fix, here's the artifact to read.\"

1. **Interactive-mode flag**: add `merge-to-main.sh --interactive` (or auto-detect when stdin is a TTY / outside CI) that switches the three LLM-dispatch phases into a structured handoff protocol. Each phase, when blocked, emits a single `AGENT_TASK:` line with category + payload, writes its checkpoint, and exits 10 (or some distinguished code). Session agent reads the line, does the work, re-runs `merge-to-main.sh --resume`. Script picks up the same phase from checkpoint.

2. **Local-dispatch shim**: ship a `merge-to-main-local-dispatch.sh` that wraps the `<cmd> <prompt> <user-message> <tier>` contract by writing the prompt + user message to a file in artifacts dir, exiting with a \"NEEDS_AGENT\" marker, and the agent invokes the script with `--resume-dispatch <task-id>` to feed the response back. Heavier; more moving parts.

3. **Separate phase commands**: split the loop into `merge-to-main.sh phase=poll-ci`, `phase=fix-failure`, `phase=resolve-threads`, etc. The session agent orchestrates the sequence and does the LLM work between phases. The script becomes a state machine kit, the agent becomes the loop driver. Cleanest separation of concerns; most refactoring.

4. **Sprint-style adoption**: wire `/dso:sprint` or a new `/dso:merge-to-main` skill to own the loop. The script becomes a passive helper; the skill is the orchestrator. Matches existing DSO patterns; aligns with the \"skill owns the workflow, scripts are kit\" architecture.

Path 4 (skill-orchestrated loop) is the most DSO-native and avoids retrofitting interactive semantics onto a script designed for non-interactive batch flow. A new `/dso:finalize-pr` skill (or extension to an existing one) would:
* Loop: `gh pr checks` poll → detect failures → for each failure category, dispatch named DSO agents (test-fixer, llm-review-responder, conflict-resolver). Re-push, repeat.
* Exit when PR is mergeable + green OR escalate a specific blocker to the user.
Filing this for design before implementation. The fix is non-trivial and the local UX of PR-mode is currently broken to the point of nullifying the value of `merge.strategy=pr` for local sessions.
