content.text: The calibration program lacks an empirical Tier-3 catch-power signal. Tests pass deterministic Tier-1/Tier-2 checks (assertion shape, intent articulation, manifest-claim breadth and header-source from 7f42) while sometimes failing to catch behavior-changing mutations on the code they claim to verify. Without mutation testing, the project has no empirical ground truth for "does this test catch a real regression?" — only structural proxies. The DSO maintainer, sprint orchestrators, and code-reviewer-test-quality have no visibility into per-PR kill-rate trends; the project cannot tell whether changes to test-writing prompts (d566, 69e8 graduations) are actually improving test catch-power.

This epic delivers per-PR mutation testing for the DSO plugin's first-class stacks (Python, Ruby, JS/TS, Flask, Go), runs in parallel with llm-review as a non-blocking CI job, ships calibration-first with a count-floor surfacing a maintainer-review story ticket, and after thresholds are committed enters enforcement mode where threshold breach auto-creates a bug ticket. Bash is out of scope due to the absence of mature mutation tooling in the bash ecosystem.

SC1: plugins/dso/docs/contracts/mutation-testing-findings.md published. Per-stack-result schema: {stack, mutation_tool, tool_version, total_mutants, mutants_generated (distinct field — zero indicates PR touched only non-mutable code), killed_mutants, surviving_mutants: [{file, line, operator, expected, actual}], kill_rate, runtime_seconds, runtime_exceeded (bool), exit_status}. Aggregate-result schema: {pr_number, schema_version=1, calibration_mode_active, per_stack_results: [...], aggregate_kill_rate}. Tooling MUST preserve unknown fields in passthrough for forward-compatibility.

SC2 (Phase 1 — Python pilot): plugins/dso/workflows/mutation-testing.yml shipped as plugin template. Triggered on pull_request (synchronize, opened). Concurrency group keyed to PR ref so new commits cancel in-flight runs. PR-label `skip-mutation-testing` opts a PR out entirely (cost-control escape hatch). When PR's mutable-stack file count exceeds `mutation.max_files_per_run` (default 100), workflow auto-skips with annotation suggesting label use or PR split. Python matrix job installs mutmut pinned to `mutation.python.tool_version` from dso-config.conf; on install failure, tries `mutation.python.fallback_versions` in order; final failure emits `TOOL_INSTALL_FAILED` annotation distinguishing tool-yank from mutation-failure. Runs mutmut incremental mode against diffed Python files. Writes findings JSON per SC1. Uploads as workflow artifact. Aggregate job upserts PR comment with marker `MUTATION_TESTING_FINDINGS_<pr-number>` (distinct from llm-review's marker — no race possible), writes GHA workflow summary, falls back to GHA-summary-only when comment-write is unavailable (fork PRs). Operates in calibration mode (no enforcement, no auto-bug-creation).

SC3 (Phase 2 — polyglot expansion): Ruby (mutant), JS/TS (Stryker `--incremental`), Go (go-gremlins) added as parallel matrix jobs alongside Python. Flask covered by Python. Each per-stack job installs its tool pinned to `mutation.<stack>.tool_version` with `mutation.<stack>.fallback_versions` chain. Per-stack runtime cap via `mutation.<stack>.timeout_seconds` (defaults: Stryker 600, mutmut 900, mutant 1200, gremlins 900). On timeout, partial-result emitted with `runtime_exceeded=true`. fail-fast: false across matrix entries. When ALL stacks return `runtime_exceeded=true`, PR comment surfaces prominent `ALL_STACKS_TIMEOUT` warning, no bug ticket created (even in threshold mode), `aggregate_kill_rate=null`. Aggregate job merges all stack findings into a single PR comment.

SC4 (Phase 3 — calibration auto-surfacing): CI workflow tracks accumulated telemetry. Floor: ≥20 PRs telemetry AND ≥4 weeks elapsed since first telemetry run AND no existing `mutation-calibration-review` tagged story ticket — all three conditions required. Workflow auto-creates story ticket titled "Review mutation testing telemetry and set per-stack thresholds". Body opens with: "Your observed kill rate is X%. What threshold fits your project's risk tolerance?" (number not headlined). Reference points table with p25 / median / p75 rows and a second column "Approximate alert frequency" showing what share of PRs would fire a threshold alert at that rate. Self-reflection prompt: "Does your calibration window include PRs that modified test files? If most PRs in the window were non-test, this kill rate may underestimate steady-state." Stable tag `mutation-calibration-review` prevents duplicate creation. Workflow emits config-consistency warning annotation when `mutation.threshold.<stack>.min_kill_rate` is set but `mutation.calibration.completed=false` (or vice versa).

SC5 (Phase 4 — threshold-mode enforcement): Workflow reads `mutation.calibration.completed` from dso-config.conf. When true AND per-stack `mutants_generated > 0`: per-stack kill rate compared against `mutation.threshold.<stack>.min_kill_rate`. On breach, bug ticket auto-created via `.claude/scripts/dso ticket create bug` pushing to the tickets orphan branch using the same CI auth pattern as the existing Jira bridge / outbound checkpoint. Retry-with-backoff (3 attempts); on final failure writes `TICKET_CREATE_FAILED` artifact to the workflow run plus a workflow-level annotation. Bug ticket includes a 4-field structured blurb (max 60 words total):
- WHAT — one sentence on what mutation testing caught
- THRESHOLD — specific threshold that fired plus current kill rate
- CONTEXT — link to behavioral-testing-standard.md Tier-3 rationale and 411b epic for background
- NEXT_STEP — instructs investigating agent: investigate surviving mutants; do NOT adjust the threshold

Content-hash deduplication tag `mutation-breach-<sha>` where sha is hash(stack, source_file, mutant_locations) — scoped per-stack-per-source-file, NOT per-PR-diff. Recurring root-causes dedup correctly across PRs; structurally-similar diffs in different files don't collide.

SC6 (Phase 5 — onboarding integration): The consolidated `/dso:onboarding` (delivered by dependency 136b-6758) gains a mutation-testing phase. LEADS WITH TRADEOFFS before per-stack questioning: estimated CI time cost, false-positive context, and one sentence on what the maintainer is asked to do when bugs fire. Detects in-scope stacks via manifest files (Python: pyproject.toml or setup.py; Ruby: Gemfile; JS/TS: package.json; Go: go.mod). Single-stack auto-default: detected single in-scope stack auto-enables with a one-line notice "Mutation testing defaulted ON for <stack> — run /dso:onboarding --mutation-off to disable". Multi-stack: per-stack Socratic-confirm after the tradeoff context block. Writes `mutation.<stack>.enabled` keys to dso-config.conf. Copies `mutation-testing.yml` to `.github/workflows/`. Ensures the tickets-branch push permission scope exists in CI auth configuration. Documents bash as unsupported in the dialogue with ecosystem-limitation rationale.

SC7 (Phase 5 — create-dso-app.sh setup-script integration): plugins/dso/scripts/create-dso-app.sh updated. When scaffolding a new DSO-using project, the script applies the same single-stack-auto-default + multi-stack-confirm pattern as SC6. Writes default `mutation.<stack>.enabled=true` for detected stacks. Copies mutation-testing.yml alongside other CI workflow templates. Adds tickets-branch push permission to CI auth section. Coordination via ticket comment on d765-a3b6-84bd-4816 noting 411b's setup-script touchpoints.
SC8 (out-of-scope documentation + scope-seal): mutation-testing.yml header contains an explicit scope-seal block:
# SCOPE-SEALED: bash mutation tooling is out of scope — see 411b epic; do not reopen.
# Rationale: no mature mutation testing tool exists in the bash ecosystem.

behavioral-testing-standard.md gains a Tier-3 addendum noting the supported stacks and the bash scope-seal with the 411b epic ID reference. plugins/dso/docs/contracts/mutation-testing-findings.md notes the scope decision. plugins/dso/docs/CI-INTEGRATION.md updated to document mutation-testing parallel job semantics, per-stack timeout handling, ALL_STACKS_TIMEOUT behavior, and TOOL_INSTALL_FAILED annotation. Reviewer assertion: code-reviewer-test-quality (or equivalent test-quality reviewer agent) flags any proposed bash-mutation-tooling additions as a scope violation.
SC9 (synthetic end-to-end test): Ten scenarios covering happy paths, adversarial paths, and post-calibration end-to-end loop:
(a) Phase 1 — PR with Python file changes triggers mutmut; PR comment posted with calibration-mode kill-rate telemetry.
(b) Phase 2 — PR with Python + JS + Go file changes produces aggregate PR comment with per-stack stats.

(c) Phase 3 — fixture with 20-PR telemetry + 4-week elapsed AND no existing mutation-calibration-review story produces exactly one calibration-review story ticket with all required fields. Re-running the same fixture produces no duplicate.

(d) Phase 4 — fixture with mutation.calibration.completed=true + per-stack threshold + synthetic breach produces a bug ticket with all required fields including 4-field blurb (max 60 words) and content-hash dedup tag. Re-running the same fixture produces no duplicate bug.

(e) Phase 5 — dispatch consolidated /dso:onboarding against a Python-only fixture project: mutation.python.enabled=true; mutation-testing.yml present in .github/workflows/; tickets-branch push permission scope present.
(f) skip-mutation-testing PR label opts out: workflow runs but no mutation jobs execute; PR comment surfaces opt-out confirmation.
(g) mutants_generated=0 produces no bug ticket (PR touched only non-mutable code).
(h) runtime_exceeded partial result is emitted in findings JSON when per-stack timeout fires.
(i) ALL_STACKS_TIMEOUT: all stacks return runtime_exceeded=true; PR comment surfaces warning; no bug ticket created even in threshold mode.

(j) Post-calibration end-to-end loop validation: PR with known-undertested function (mutant survives) against repo with mutation.calibration.completed=true AND per-stack threshold committed produces an auto-created bug ticket appearing in `ticket list --type=bug --status=open`. Same PR with added killing test produces no new bug ticket. Confirms the feedback loop is live end-to-end.

SC10 (validation signal): mutation-testing.yml referenced in CLAUDE.md Quick Reference table as the project's mutation-testing surface. mutation-testing-findings.md listed in plugins/dso/docs/contracts/ index. Both references link to 411b epic for context. Verify by: grep CLAUDE.md for "mutation-testing.yml" AND `ls plugins/dso/docs/contracts/` shows mutation-testing-findings.md.

SC11 (self-use): The 411b sprint deploys `mutation-testing.yml` to `.github/workflows/` in the host DSO repo before sprint close, and at least one 411b story-PR triggers a successful mutation-testing workflow run with a posted PR comment containing the `MUTATION_TESTING_FINDINGS_<pr-number>` marker. Dogfooding loop is proven end-to-end: the workflow ships AND fires on the very PRs that ship it. Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I): `test -f .github/workflows/mutation-testing.yml` returns 0; `gh pr view <411b-story-pr> --comments | grep -q "MUTATION_TESTING_FINDINGS_"` returns 0 on at least one 411b story PR.
5 sequential phases with an explicit interim release gate:
- Phase 1: SC1 (contract) + SC2 (Python pilot CI workflow)
Phases 1-2 (Python pilot + polyglot expansion) constitute a shippable informational-mode increment; Phases 3-5 follow in the same milestone:
- Phase 5: SC6 + SC7 (onboarding + create-dso-app.sh integration) + SC8 (scope-seal documentation)
SC9 + SC10 (synthetic + validation signal) verified across phases as each ships.

- Per-stack mutation runtime explosion on large PRs (critical/performance): partially mitigated by SC2 max_files_per_run auto-skip + SC3 per-stack timeout caps + ALL_STACKS_TIMEOUT handling; residual is the case where most-but-not-all stacks time out.

- CI compute cost budget at scale (critical/cost): partially mitigated by skip-mutation-testing PR label + concurrency group + per-stack runtime caps; no org-level monthly-minute budget guard; accepted as residual for first version.

- Tool version drift / pin yanking (important/reliability): partially mitigated by fallback_versions chain + TOOL_INSTALL_FAILED annotation; residual is the case where all fallback versions are also unavailable.

- Calibration thresholds become stale as codebase evolves (moderate/correctness): unmitigated; no automatic re-calibration trigger; accepted as residual — operator may flip mutation.calibration.completed=false manually to re-enter calibration mode.
- Calibration data poisoned by low-quality initial test suites (moderate/correctness): partially mitigated by SC4 self-reflection prompt; no automatic floor enforcement on observed median.
- Monorepo diff scoping failure in Python with shared package dependencies (moderate/correctness): unmitigated; documented limitation of incremental-mode mutmut on monorepos.
- Phase 5 blocked indefinitely if 136b-6758 slips (moderate/planning): unmitigated; no degraded-mode onboarding path specified; if 136b-6758 slips significantly, Phase 5 is rescoped at that time.
- Bash mutation testing — no mature ecosystem tool; SCOPE-SEALED with rationale documented in SC8.
- Promotion to merge-blocking gate — reserved for a future hybrid epic informed by calibration data; this epic ships warn-only / informational-only.
- Pre-commit mutation invocation — operationally untenable per the time-cost analysis (1–4 min added to every commit).
- Nightly batch runs — PR-time only in this version.
- Mutation testing within the llm-review job itself — separate parallel job per the architectural decision.

- Test-writer agent prompt modifications — 411b's feedback loop is indirect via auto-created bugs flowing through /dso:fix-bug and 69e8's negative-example graduation; 411b does not modify how tests are written.
- Project-side dependency-manifest modifications — no pyproject.toml / package.json / Gemfile / go.mod additions in host projects (CI-installs-on-demand).
- Org-level monthly-minute cost budget guard — not specified in first version; can be a follow-on if cost becomes a concern.
- Automatic threshold re-calibration trigger — not specified in first version; operator flips mutation.calibration.completed=false manually if recalibration is needed.
`plugins/dso/workflows/mutation-testing.yml` MUST follow the DSO repo trigger convention established by `ci.yml`:

| `pull_request` | `types: [synchronize, opened]`; no `branches:` filter | Covers per-story PRs whose base is a session branch, not `main` (bug 3914-0848-faad-4f6a). Restricting to `branches: [main]` would silently skip mutation testing on every story PR. |
| `pull_request_target` | Not used | Not needed — mutation testing reads only the PR diff and does not require fork-secret access. Avoids the known `pull_request_target` security pitfall. |
| `push` | Not used | Mutation testing is PR-time only by design (per Out-of-Scope: "nightly batch runs"). Push-trigger would duplicate cost on story-branch pushes that already have an open PR. |
`concurrency.group` keyed to `github.head_ref` (per SC2) already prevents in-flight duplication.

Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I): `grep -A 20 '^on:' plugins/dso/workflows/mutation-testing.yml` shows `pull_request` block with no `branches:` key, no `pull_request_target` block, and no `push` block.

| `mutation.<stack>.enabled` (dso-config.conf) | `/dso:onboarding` (SC6) or `create-dso-app.sh` (SC7) at setup | `/dso:onboarding --mutation-off`; operator edit | `mutation-testing.yml` matrix gate | Stack removed; operator |
| `mutation.<stack>.tool_version` | Template default; onboarding | Operator edit; `create-dso-app.sh` | `mutation-testing.yml` tool-install step | Stack disabled |
| `mutation.<stack>.fallback_versions` | Template default | Operator edit | `mutation-testing.yml` install-fallback chain | Stack disabled |
| `mutation.<stack>.timeout_seconds` | Template default (per SC3 values) | Operator edit | `mutation-testing.yml` per-stack timeout | Stack disabled |

| `mutation.threshold.<stack>.min_kill_rate` | Operator, AFTER `mutation-calibration-review` story closes (SC4 → SC5) | Operator edit | `mutation-testing.yml` Phase-4 enforcement | Stack disabled OR `mutation.calibration.completed=false` flip |

| `mutation.calibration.completed` | Operator, when committing thresholds (SC5) | Operator (flip-back to false to re-calibrate, per Out-of-Scope) | `mutation-testing.yml` Phase-4 gate; SC4 config-consistency annotation | N/A — persistent project-state key |
| `mutation.max_files_per_run` | Template default = 100 | Operator edit | `mutation-testing.yml` pre-flight skip-check | N/A — persistent |

| Accumulated PR telemetry | Each workflow run uploads findings JSON as GHA artifact (per SC2) | Append-only via GHA artifact retention | SC4 calibration-floor scan over recent runs | Governed by GitHub Actions artifact retention (repo setting; default 90d) — anchors telemetry to GHA artifacts, NOT the tickets branch |
| Story tag `mutation-calibration-review` | SC4 auto-creation flow | Stable | SC4 pre-flight dedup | Persists through story close; new instance per calibration cycle |
| Bug tag `mutation-breach-<sha>` | SC5 auto-bug-creation flow | Stable | SC5 pre-flight dedup | Persists on bug ticket; new instance per unique surviving-mutant hash |
- `grep -E '^mutation\.' .claude/dso-config.conf` enumerates every key listed above (defaults present).
Closes the audit's named gaps: telemetry CREATE/RETIRE owner = GHA artifacts + retention; `mutation.calibration.completed` RETIRE = N/A (persistent, with operator flip-back path).
### External-dependency verification — addressable touchpoints (Probe-6 partial remediation with explicit override, 2026-05-18 follow-up)

The 2026-05-16 audit flagged probe 6 over four external touchpoints. Three are in-session-verifiable via fixtures + CLIs; one (4-week wall-clock telemetry emergence) is genuinely external. Adding the structured block with explicit override on the time-elapsed touchpoint.

| SC2: workflow RUNS in real GHA on real PRs | Covered by SC11 (self-use) — the 411b sprint deploys mutation-testing.yml AND at least one sprint PR triggers a successful run with the MUTATION_TESTING_FINDINGS_ marker. | IN-SESSION ✓ |

| SC4: 4-week-elapsed real-time telemetry-floor gate | Verified via SC9(c) fixture: a pre-built 20-PR + 4-week-elapsed telemetry fixture is replayed during the sprint and the calibration-review story-ticket auto-creation logic is exercised end-to-end. The CAPABILITY (gating logic + auto-creation flow) is verifiable in-session; the EMERGENCE (4 real weeks of real telemetry) is operational and not gated. | IN-SESSION (capability) ✓ + OPERATIONAL RESIDUAL (real emergence) |

| SC6: consuming projects install Python/Ruby/JS/Go toolchains in CI | Verified via a per-stack fixture project at `tests/fixtures/consuming-project-<stack>/` containing the manifest file (pyproject.toml / Gemfile / package.json / go.mod) and a stub `.github/workflows/`. The sprint runs `/dso:onboarding --fixture=tests/fixtures/consuming-project-python/` (etc. for each stack) and asserts that mutation-testing.yml is copied AND the relevant `mutation.<stack>.enabled=true` key is written. Real consuming projects installing in real CI is operational. | IN-SESSION (per-stack fixtures) ✓ + OPERATIONAL RESIDUAL (real projects) |

| SC7: create-dso-app.sh scaffolding lands in a new project | Sprint runs `create-dso-app.sh --target=$(mktemp -d)` against a temp directory and asserts mutation-testing.yml + dso-config.conf keys are present in the scaffolded output. Real new-project adoption is operational. | IN-SESSION (scaffolder fixture) ✓ + OPERATIONAL RESIDUAL (real new projects) |

Three of four touchpoints are now fully in-session-verifiable via fixtures (SC2 via SC11; SC6 + SC7 via per-stack fixture projects + temp-dir scaffolder runs). The fourth (SC4's 4-week-elapsed real-time emergence) is genuinely external; the spec's existing SC9(c) fixture provides in-session verification of the GATING CAPABILITY, while the real-world telemetry accumulation is acknowledged as operational and not gated. This is the same "capability verified in-session; real-world emergence is operational" pattern documented for SC11's dogfooding loop and the workflow-trigger-filter enumeration. Sprint closure gates on the capability checks; the emergence is observed post-ship without gating.

The audit's "structured External Dependencies block" pattern is honored in substance with each row's ownership (operator who runs the check) and access (gh CLI / `/dso:onboarding` / `create-dso-app.sh`, all available in-session) implicit in the verification command. Override applied because the genuinely-external piece is bounded to a single time-elapsed gate whose capability is independently verified.

- 136b-6758-ba12-47fc (Consolidate project-setup skills into resume-aware /dso:onboarding) — required for SC6. Phase 5's onboarding integration consolidates onto the unified /dso:onboarding rather than fragmenting across /dso:onboarding + /dso:init separately. Phases 1-4 ship independently while 136b-6758 is implemented in parallel.
- a03c-d55e — closure-checks-aware verifier consumes 411b's auto-created bugs.
- 94ed-f55c — surviving-mutant findings can optionally map back to intent_id via the manifest for downstream analysis; not required for the core gate.
- d566-afa6 — indirect downstream consumer via 69e8's negative-example graduation.
- 69e8-af39 — auto-created bugs are 69e8's input signal; 69e8 extracts negative-example patterns from these bugs.

- d765-a3b6-84bd-4816 — create-dso-app.sh rewrite coordination. If d765-a3b6 ships first, 411b's additions integrate on top of its rewrite; if 411b ships first, d765-a3b6's rewrite must preserve 411b's mutation-testing hooks. Coordination via ticket comment on d765-a3b6 at Phase 3 ticket integration.

- Web research (Step 2): not triggered. Sufficient context inherited from d566-afa6 brainstorm's three-stream research synthesis (Meta TestGen-LLM 2025, Stryker --incremental, mutmut, PIT scmMutationCoverage, mull, go-gremlins, OOPSLA 2025 PBT evidence).

- Scenario analysis (Step 3): triggered (SCs >= 5); 20 red-team scenarios surfaced; 13 mitigated-by-spec after blue-team filter; 7 surviving (most partial-mitigations on inherent runtime/cost residuals and moderate-severity items deferred).
- Cross-epic scan (Step 2.25): 1 conflict (136b-6758 hard dep, expected); 2 considerations (d765-a3b6 coordination, 69e8 consumer); 3 benign.

- Bot-psychologist (Step 5): triggered (LLM-instruction signal — modifies /dso:onboarding via 136b-6758 consolidation, create-dso-app.sh, and adds LLM-consumed bug-blurb content). Five risks folded: anti-sycophancy tradeoffs-first onboarding (SC6), single-stack auto-default (SC6), p25 anti-anchor reference table with explicit column headers (SC4), bash scope-seal block + reviewer assertion (SC8), 4-field structured auto-bug blurb max 60 words (SC5).
- Fidelity review (Step 4): Agent Clarity (5, 4), Scope (4, 4, 4, 4), Value (4, 4). All dimensions >= 4 after one revision cycle.
- Scale context (Step 0): small-to-medium per-PR; mutation runs scoped to diffed lines only.
- Session-signal override for complexity routing: success_criteria_count = 10 (>= 7 threshold) — would route to /dso:preplanning full mode if invoked; preplanning explicitly deferred this session.
- Polyglot first-class for Python, Ruby, JS/TS (including NextJS), Flask, Go; bash explicitly out of scope due to ecosystem-tool absence.
- CI parallel with llm-review; not a required merge check.
- Calibration-first delivery; thresholds set by human after telemetry-floor auto-surfaces a review ticket.
- Threshold breach auto-creates a bug ticket with explanatory blurb context for the investigating agent.
- CI-installs-on-demand (no project-side dependency-manifest changes; no local-env weight).
- Onboarding-side integration consolidated onto 136b-6758's unified /dso:onboarding rather than fragmenting across init+onboarding separately.
- dso setup script (create-dso-app.sh) updated for new-project scaffolding to include mutation-testing configuration.

DIG-2218.summary: Test creation calibration (d): mutation-testing infrastructure for empirical test-catch-power verification

content.text: When bugs surface in production OR are caught by code review rather than by the test suite, the project today has no mechanism for the test-writing agents to learn from that miss. The same class of bug recurs. Test-writing sub-agents (red-test-writer, sprint task-execution, fix-bug RED-phase) operate against static guidance (behavioral-testing-standard.md) that doesn't grow from observed misses. This epic delivers a closed-loop feedback system: closed bugs with extractable lessons get `NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE:` JSON comments + `negative-example` tag during /dso:fix-bug Phase G; test-writing sub-agents consume retrieved examples via `negative-examples-lookup.sh` at task start; recurring patterns graduate to universal rules in `behavioral-testing-standard.md` via /dso:retro Graduation Phase with human approval. After this epic ships, test-writing agents see project-specific "Lessons from past bugs" alongside the universal 7-rule standard — where today they see only the standard.

Users affected: DSO maintainer, sprint orchestrators, test-writing sub-agents (red-test-writer, sprint task-execution, fix-bug RED-phase), code-reviewer-test-quality, completion-verifier, and downstream calibration consumers (411b-a047 mutation infrastructure, 7f42-e41f growth metrics, fb3e-b01b deeper signals).

SC1: plugins/dso/docs/contracts/negative-example-comment.md published. NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE comment schema: {schema_version=1, bug_type_slug (string; from 4911-c7ba taxonomy), intent_ids_if_applicable (array of intent_ids from 94ed manifest entries; values MUST reference real manifest entries OR be empty), missed_signal_summary (describes what FAILED to be detected — canonical example in contract showing correct polarity), what_test_would_have_caught_it, generalizable_lesson, related_files (array of paths), scope_claim ("this pattern applies to any agent that..."), falsification ("this would NOT apply when...")}. Contract document includes prompt-engineering guidance for sonnet extraction to avoid inverted-polarity drafts AND a consistent style guide for opus drafting graduation rules (matching the existing 7-rule standard's structure).

SC2: /dso:fix-bug Phase G extended. EXECUTES AFTER 4911-c7ba bug-type classification step (explicit ordering — Phase G runs after 4911 sets bug_type_<slug> tag). When a bug ticket is closed with reason="Fixed: ...":
(i) sonnet sub-agent evaluates extraction conditions: bug not caught by an existing test AND pattern generalizable;

(ii) MANDATORY pre-extraction redaction step: sonnet identifies and redacts credentials, tokens, keys, PII, customer/user identifiers, internal-only IDs from all string fields. If sonnet cannot confidently redact, MUST skip extraction;
(iii) output MUST include scope_claim AND falsification fields per SC1; if either is vacuous ("when the code is correct", "always applies"), skip extraction;
(iv) atomic write: NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE comment + negative-example tag applied as single unit (rollback if either fails);
(v) when 4911 classification failed (bug_type_<slug> not set on the ticket), use bug_type_slug="unclassified" and add `retro-needs-classification` tag;
(vi) SKIP_RECORD comment logged on every skip with {decision: "skip", skip_reason: <one sentence>} for audit trail;
(vii) intent_ids_if_applicable values validated at write time against 94ed manifest entries; invalid intent_ids cause write to fail OR values dropped with warning.
(a) reads task's file_impact + claimable_intent from ticket data;
(b) queries via existing ticket-CLI primitives: `ticket list --type=bug --status=closed --has-tag=negative-example --has-tag=bug-type-<slug>`;
(d) excludes stale examples: tickets whose related_files reference paths not present on disk (auto-staleness check);

(e) relevance ranking: narrower-scoped bugs (smaller related_files set) preferred, weight by recency. When two examples have identical relevance scores, deterministic tie-breaking via ticket-id lexical order;
(f) returns top-N=3 most relevant matches as JSON;
(g) output includes excluded_count field (signal for /dso:retro Graduation Phase when count is high);
(h) summary format per match: {slug, missed_signal_summary, generalizable_lesson} (concise, not full schema);

SC4: Three test-writing sub-agent prompts updated to invoke `negative-examples-lookup.sh` at task-start: plugins/dso/agents/red-test-writer.md, plugins/dso/skills/sprint/prompts/task-execution.md, and the fix-bug RED-phase prompt (concrete path under plugins/dso/skills/fix-bug/ resolved during implementation-plan). Retrieved examples are injected with explicit label "## Project-specific learned patterns (advisory; not universal Rule 1-7+ authority)" so the agent distinguishes project-specific learned guidance from universal Rule 1-7 standards. Cap at 3 examples per task. When 0 examples returned (e.g., cold-start), section omitted entirely (no empty block, no error).

SC5: /dso:retro extended with a Graduation Phase. Opus sub-agent reads all bugs with `negative-example` tag AND without `promoted-to-standard:*` tag via single CLI query. Identifies graduation candidates via two trigger paths:

(a) Frequency floor: ≥3 examples sharing the same bug_type_slug AND distinct root-cause fingerprints. Opus MUST verify <80% missed_signal_summary similarity across the group; groups whose examples are >=80% similar are collapsed as a single signal (treats as 1 example, not N).

(b) Cross-slug semantic match: opus identifies a pattern via SINGLE FALSIFIABLE PREDICATE naming a specific testable condition (e.g., "all four miss the case where X is empty"). Theme-level labels (e.g., "all four are about validation") are NOT permitted — predicate must name a specific input state or code path AND an expected observable outcome.
(1) 4-field draft rule matching the existing behavioral-testing-standard.md structure: {rule_statement, rationale, anti_pattern_example, correct_pattern_example};
(2) evidence_citations: ≥3 bug IDs with quoted missed_signal_summary from each;
(3) explicit provenance ("3 same-slug bugs" OR "opus cross-slug semantic match across N examples").

PRE-DRAFT VALIDATION: opus MUST check existing rules in behavioral-testing-standard.md; if proposed rule overlaps an existing rule, opus either revises to propose modification to existing rule OR justifies distinct coverage. Block surfacing if conflict is unresolved.

SYCOPHANCY GATE: on user acceptance, before PR is drafted, user must answer challenge: "Where does this rule add distinct coverage beyond existing Rules 1-N?" An empty answer OR an answer that restates the rule blocks the PR and marks the candidate as `challenged-rejected`.

SC6: Atomic graduation: on accepted candidate, PR is drafted FIRST (contains the standard amendment); contributing bug tickets get `promoted-to-standard:<rule-id>` tag ONLY after PR creation succeeds. If PR draft fails, no tags are applied — prevents phantom graduation records.

SC7: behavioral-testing-standard.md remains designated a safeguard file per a03c-d55e's SC2 / CLAUDE.md rule 22. /dso:retro Graduation Phase MUST surface candidates and draft rule text but MUST NOT auto-commit. Human approval to merge the PR remains required.

SC8: Lifecycle hook — status transition closed→open on a tagged bug automatically removes the negative-example tag (sentry on the ticket-transition hook). Verified by SC9(i) fixture: reopening a tagged bug removes the tag and the bug is excluded from subsequent lookup results.
SC9: Synthetic end-to-end test covering twelve scenarios:
(a) EXTRACTION + atomic write + audit trail: fixture bug with test-miss + generalizable pattern produces NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE comment + negative-example tag atomically.
(b) SKIP recorded: fixture bug where extraction conditions not met → SKIP_RECORD comment with decision and reason.
(c) PRIVACY redaction: fixture bug with token/credential in description → redaction confirmed in NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE comment OR extraction skipped.
(d) LOOKUP with stale-example exclusion: fixture bug whose related_files references a deleted path → excluded from lookup output.

(e) FREQUENCY graduation: 3 fixture bugs sharing bug_type_slug=X with distinct root-cause fingerprints → /dso:retro Graduation surfaces candidate with provenance "3 same-slug bugs"; user accepts; PR draft + promoted-to-standard:<rule-id> tagging.
(f) FREQUENCY COLLAPSE: 3 fixture bugs sharing bug_type_slug with >=80% missed_signal_summary similarity → collapsed as 1 signal, no candidate surfaced.

(g) CROSS-SLUG predicate graduation: 4 fixture bugs across 2 slugs sharing a falsifiable predicate ("all four miss the case where input array is empty") → candidate surfaced with provenance "opus cross-slug semantic match across 4 examples".
(h) THEME-only rejection: 4 fixture bugs share a theme ("all about validation") without a specific predicate → NOT surfaced.

(i) SYCOPHANCY challenge blocks empty response: user accepts candidate, then enters empty answer to "where does this rule add distinct coverage?" → PR is blocked, candidate marked challenged-rejected.

(j) COLD_START / EMPTY_CORPUS: fixture task in a project with zero closed bugs tagged negative-example → lookup returns empty result with excluded_count=0; test-writer prompt omits "Lessons from past bugs" section entirely (no error, no hang).
(k) RANKING_TIE: 2 fixture examples with identical relevance scores → lookup returns them in deterministic ticket-id lexical order.

(l) OPERATIONAL METRIC EMISSION: /dso:retro Graduation Phase emits structured telemetry to a RETRO_TELEMETRY: ticket comment OR a retro-telemetry-<timestamp>.json artifact with fields {examples_extracted_since_last_retro, examples_skipped_count, graduation_candidates_surfaced, candidates_accepted, sycophancy_rejections, candidates_rejected_predicate, candidates_rejected_frequency_collapse}.
Four sequential phases, each independently mergeable:
- Phase 1: SC1 (contract) + SC2 (recording with redaction, atomicity, audit trail, intent_ids validation).
- Phase 2: SC3 (lookup helper with relevance + staleness + tie-breaking) + SC4 (test-writer prompt integration).
- Phase 3: SC5 + SC6 + SC7 (graduation with predicate/distinct-root validation + sycophancy gate + atomic PR-first + safeguard preservation).
- Phase 4: SC8 + SC9 (lifecycle hooks + twelve-scenario end-to-end synthetic test).

- Sonnet over-extraction (high/extraction-quality): partially mitigated by SC2(i) generalizability check + SC2(iii) scope_claim/falsification requirement + SC2(vi) audit trail; residual is sonnet's self-assessment quality.
- Sonnet under-extraction (high/extraction-quality): partially mitigated by SC2(vi) SKIP_RECORD audit trail; residual is silent signal loss; /dso:retro can surface high-skip-rate trends.

- Cross-slug opus over-clustering (high/promotion-integrity): partially mitigated by SC5(b) single-falsifiable-predicate constraint + SYCOPHANCY gate + PRE-DRAFT conflict check; residual is opus's self-assessment of predicate quality.
- Standard amendment too narrow (medium/rule-quality): partially mitigated by SC2(iii) scope_claim/falsification + SYCOPHANCY gate; no minimum-breadth requirement.
- Standard amendment too broad (medium/rule-quality): partially mitigated by SC5 PRE-DRAFT conflict check; overlap is opus's semantic judgment.
- File-impact intersection false positive (high/retrieval-relevance): partially mitigated by SC3(e) narrower-scoped + recency ranking; no semantic relevance filter.
- Top-N cutoff silences critical examples (high/retrieval-coverage): partially mitigated by SC3(f) excluded_count signal in output; ranking heuristic is structural not semantic.
- Cross-epic standard amendment conflicts (high/rule-quality): partially mitigated by SC5 PRE-DRAFT check against committed state of standard; concurrent in-flight PRs not visible.
- intent_id schema mismatch (medium/schema-integrity): mitigated by SC2(vii) validation against 94ed manifest entries.

- Bug ticket comment bloat (medium/data-integrity): partially mitigated by SC8 reopening-removes-tag + SC2(iv) atomic write; deduplication of multiple NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE comments on same ticket not specified (acceptable — latest comment wins in retrieval implicitly).
- Strict ownership enforcement at the manifest layer (explicitly out per 94ed brainstorm).
- Concurrent /dso:retro telemetry write conflict (deferred — low probability; manageable via lock or merge-by-comment-id).
- Operational metric dashboards beyond raw telemetry emission (deferred to /dso:retro-stats or similar observability epic).
- Cross-PR amendment conflict detection (deferred — relies on committed state of standard; PR-review process catches conflicts).
### External-dependency verification — addressable touchpoints (Probe-6 partial remediation with explicit override)

The 2026-05-16 audit flagged probe 6 over three external touchpoints. Two are in-session-verifiable via the available CLIs; one is genuinely external and explicitly overridden as non-gating with a documented residual.

| SC5 sycophancy gate user response | If the gate fires during the 69e8 sprint, the user's response is captured in the same session transcript. Verification: `grep -E 'sycophancy.*(rejected\|accepted\|deferred)' <session-transcript-or-PIL>` returns ≥1 entry OR the absence is documented as "gate did not fire in this sprint window" — sprint cannot close without one of these states recorded. | IN-SESSION ✓ |

| SC6 atomic graduation depends on gh PR creation | `command -v gh && gh auth status \|\| gh auth login` runs at sprint Phase A; an atomic-graduation invocation during the sprint exercises the gh-PR-creation path against a synthetic fixture branch and asserts a successful PR creation + immediate close. Verification: `gh pr create --draft --base <fixture-base> --head <fixture-head> --title "atomic-graduation-dogfooding" --body "..."` returns a URL; `gh pr close <pr>` succeeds. | IN-SESSION ✓ |

| SC7 human-approval merge on the safeguard-file PR | Human reviewer approval and merge on the `behavioral-testing-standard.md` amendment PR is **genuinely external** — no in-session command can synthesize human review. | OPERATIONAL RESIDUAL (override) |
SC7's human-approval requirement is acknowledged as operationally external. Sprint closure does NOT gate on the PR being merged within the sprint; closure DOES require that:
- The amendment PR has been **opened** (`gh pr view <pr-number> --json state` returns `"OPEN"` or `"MERGED"`),
- The PR is **assigned to a human reviewer** (`gh pr view <pr-number> --json reviewRequests --jq 'length'` returns ≥1),
- The deferral of merge-approval is recorded as a sprint Phase I comment noting the outstanding human-action item.

This converts the audit's prose-only external dependency into structured in-session preflight + an explicit operational-residual carve-out. The audit's "structured External Dependencies block" pattern is honored in substance (ownership/handling/access/verification_command columns are implicit in the table) while respecting that human review is non-gating.

- a03c-d55e (Closure Checks schema migration) — required. SC7 enforces a03c's safeguard-file designation for behavioral-testing-standard.md; SC5's PRE-DRAFT validation reads the standard structure a03c established.

- 4911-c7ba (Bug-classification coverage registry) — required. SC2 executes after 4911's bug-type-<slug> classification; SC3 retrieval queries by 4911's slug taxonomy; SC5(a) frequency trigger groups by slug.

- 94ed-f55c (Plan-time intent allocation manifest) — required. SC1 intent_ids_if_applicable references 94ed manifest entries; SC2(vii) validates intent_ids at write time; SC3 reads task claimable_intent from manifest entries.

- d566-afa6 (Generation-time prevention) — required. SC4's test-writer prompts are the same files d566 modifies with Rule 6/7. Coordination: when both epics ship in overlapping sprints, merge-window protocol applies to those prompt files.
- Web research (Step 2): not triggered. Sufficient context inherited from prior calibration brainstorms.
- Scenario analysis (Step 3): triggered (SCs >= 5); 20 red-team scenarios surfaced; 10 mitigated-by-spec after blue-team filter; 10 surviving (most LLM-judgment residual, partial-mitigated).
- Cross-epic scan (Step 2.25): 2 conflicts (a03c safeguard, d566 same-prompts overlap — both managed), 2 considerations (4911 taxonomy, 94ed intent vocabulary), 3 benign (411b, 7f42, cf7b).

- Bot-psychologist (Step 5): triggered (LLM-instruction signal — modifies /dso:fix-bug Phase G, test-writer prompts, /dso:retro). Five risks folded: SCOPE_CLAIM + FALSIFICATION fields in extraction (SC2(iii)), SKIP_RECORD audit trail (SC2(vi)), structured graduation drafting with evidence_citations (SC5), single-falsifiable-predicate constraint for cross-slug (SC5(b)), sycophancy challenge gate (SC5).
- Fidelity review (Step 4): Agent Clarity (4, 4), Scope (4, 4, 4, 4), Value (4, 4). All dimensions >= 4 after one revision cycle.
- Scale context (Step 0): small-to-medium — dozens of bugs and review findings per quarter; LLM-based extraction is feasible per-event.
- Session-signal override for complexity routing: success_criteria_count = 9 (>= 7 threshold) — would route to /dso:preplanning full mode if invoked; preplanning explicitly deferred this session.

- User-directed design decisions during brainstorm: tickets-as-storage (no separate file) with `NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE:` JSON comments; `negative-example` tag set on extraction; `promoted-to-standard:<rule-id>` tag on graduation; recording in /dso:fix-bug (sonnet); promotion in /dso:retro (opus + human approval at safeguard boundary); hybrid promotion triggers (frequency floor ≥3 same-slug + opus cross-slug falsifiable predicate); top-3 retrieval cap with relevance + staleness exclusion; sycophancy challenge gate mirroring 94ed's challenge round pattern.

DIG-2232.summary: Test creation calibration (c): feedback loop from production bugs and review findings to test-creation prompts

content.text: Test creation calibration today has no signal for "did we add tests for new intent items?" Test-writing sub-agents can produce many tests that pass review but do not cover newly-introduced SC/DoD/AC entries — and the failure is invisible until production. Today there is no per-PR or per-epic metric that distinguishes "suite grew because behavior was added" from "suite grew due to test inflation." Users affected: DSO maintainer, sprint orchestrators, test-writing sub-agents, code-reviewer-test-quality, completion-verifier, and downstream calibration consumers (411b-a047 mutation infrastructure once brainstormed, 69e8-af39 feedback loop). After this epic ships, when a sprint agent closes a story that has an SC with no test_artifact registered in the manifest, the completion-verifier emits a non-empty "Intent Allocation Findings" section naming the uncovered SC — where today closure is silent.

This epic delivers the first version of suite-growth metrics: (a) manifest-claim breadth + (a+) header-vs-source import check, both implemented as deterministic scripts. Stronger signals (intent-anchored line coverage, manifest-claim depth) are deferred to fb3e-b01b at P4 until the simpler signals' real-world catch rate is known.

SC1: plugins/dso/docs/contracts/intent-coverage-findings.md published with a jsonschema. Seven finding types: intent_with_no_test, test_artifact_missing_on_disk, test_artifact_fails, header_source_mismatch, dynamic_import_inconclusive (fail-open, warn), source_files_unresolved (warn; both manifest entry's source_files field AND parent ticket file_impact absent/empty), file_impact_likely_stale (warn; source_files resolved from file_impact but referenced files don't exist on disk). Severities: warn (default), block (reserved for intent_with_no_test at closure-time only). contract_version=1. Each consumer validates incoming findings JSON against the published jsonschema before processing.

SC2: plugins/dso/scripts/intent-coverage-check.sh implements (a) — manifest-claim breadth. Reads the 94ed manifest via intent-allocation-read.sh. For each end-state intent_id: (i) entry presence in the merged manifest; (ii) test_artifact.path realpath() normalization THEN file existence on disk; (iii) test pass/fail. Pre-commit invocation runs ONLY steps (i)+(ii) — fast checks. Test-pass validation step (iii) runs in CI workflow OR at closure-time on ticket-transition — NOT on every commit, eliminating pre-commit latency. Findings written to file via `--output-file` flag (ARG_MAX-safe; not passed as command-line argument or env var). Exit codes: 0 = no findings; 1 = warn-only; 2 = at least one block-mode finding.

SC3: plugins/dso/scripts/intent-header-source-check.sh implements (a+) — header-vs-source import check. ONLY applies to test files that have an intent-claim header per d566-afa6 Rule 6; files without a header are skipped (header presence is d566's reviewer concern, not 7f42's). For each test file with a header: (i) extract intent_id; (ii) resolve source_files via manifest entry's source_files field if present → else parent ticket's file_impact array → else emit source_files_unresolved (warn, fail-open; skip check for that intent); when file_impact is used, additionally check disk presence of each referenced file and emit file_impact_likely_stale (warn) for missing entries; (iii) parse the test file with sg (ast-grep); when sg unavailable OR no parser for the test language, emit dynamic_import_inconclusive (warn, fail-open) — NO grep fallback (grep fallback produces false positives); (iv) emit header_source_mismatch when test file contains no reference to any source_files entry. Dynamic-import patterns detected for fail-open: Python importlib.import_module with variable arg; JavaScript eval/Function/dynamic require with computed string; Ruby send/public_send. Findings written via `--output-file` (ARG_MAX-safe).
SC4: Multi-surface consumption — three consumers, one published contract:

- (a) plugins/dso/hooks/pre-commit-intent-coverage-gate.sh invokes only the FAST checks (file existence + header parsing). NO test-runner invocation in pre-commit. Block-mode reserved for intent_with_no_test at closure-time only, detected via ticket-transition hook.

- (b) 94ed-f55c's manifest-aware default validator (already registered with a03c-d55e's pluggable end-state-item-validator hook) ingests the findings JSON. ALL seven finding types (intent_with_no_test, test_artifact_missing_on_disk, test_artifact_fails, header_source_mismatch, dynamic_import_inconclusive, source_files_unresolved, file_impact_likely_stale) are explicitly enumerated as a contract requirement for 94ed's validator output mapping — the validator must register each type for rendering in the completion-verifier "Intent Allocation Findings" section.

- (c) .github/workflows/intent-coverage.yml invokes both scripts AND the (a)-step-iii test-pass validation step at CI time. Posts findings as PR comment via upsert-by-marker pattern: finds prior bot comment by the stable marker `COVERAGE_FINDINGS_<epic-id>` and edits it in place; if absent, posts new. One comment per PR, never a thread. Fallback when comment-write is unavailable (e.g., fork PRs with read-only GITHUB_TOKEN): write findings to the GHA job summary so the signal is not silently dropped.
SC5: Multi-language synthetic end-to-end test covering nine fixture scenarios:
- (a) HAPPY PATH: Python + bash test fixtures with valid intent-claim headers and manifest entries pointing at them. Both scripts return zero findings.

- (b) INTENT_WITH_NO_TEST: fixture epic with 2 SCs, only one has a manifest entry. intent-coverage-check.sh surfaces intent_with_no_test for the uncovered SC. completion-verifier dispatch produces a non-empty "Intent Allocation Findings" section naming it.

- (c) HEADER_SOURCE_MISMATCH: fixture Python test + fixture bash test both with valid intent-claim headers but no source-file symbol references. intent-header-source-check.sh surfaces header_source_mismatch for each.

- (d) SOURCE_FILES_UNRESOLVED: intent_id whose manifest entry has no source_files field AND whose parent ticket file_impact is empty. intent-header-source-check.sh surfaces source_files_unresolved (warn, fail-open) and skips the (a+) check for that intent.

- (e) FILE_IMPACT_LIKELY_STALE: parent ticket file_impact references a path that doesn't exist on disk. intent-header-source-check.sh surfaces file_impact_likely_stale (warn) but still attempts source-symbol matching against the surviving file_impact entries.
- (f) DEFERRED_TEST OVERRIDE: manifest entry with deferred_test: true set. Closure attempt on the parent ticket does NOT block on intent_with_no_test for that intent.

- (g) MISSING_SG: simulate sg absence on the runtime PATH. intent-header-source-check.sh emits dynamic_import_inconclusive (warn) for all test files; NO grep fallback is executed; pre-commit does NOT block.

- (h) BACKWARD_COMPAT_94ED_LEGACY: manifest entry without source_files field AND without deferred_test field (pre-extension legacy schema). Scripts handle gracefully: source_files resolution falls back to parent ticket file_impact; absent deferred_test treated as false. Verifies the additive 94ed schema extension preserves backward compatibility for existing consumers.

SC6: Dynamic-import fail-open verification per language. Python importlib.import_module with variable arg; JavaScript eval/Function/dynamic require with computed string; Ruby send/public_send. Each emits dynamic_import_inconclusive (warn); pre-commit does NOT block; completion-verifier surfaces as informational finding (not blocking closure).
Four sequential phases, each independently mergeable:
- Phase 1: SC1 (findings jsonschema contract) + SC2 (intent-coverage-check.sh; manifest-claim breadth check).
- Phase 2: SC3 (intent-header-source-check.sh; header-vs-source via sg) + SC6 (dynamic-import fail-open pattern detection per language).
- Phase 3: SC4 (multi-surface wiring — fast-only pre-commit hook, 94ed validator finding-type mapping, CI workflow upsert-by-marker with GHA-summary fallback).
- Phase 4: SC5 (nine-scenario multi-language synthetic end-to-end test).

7f42's sg usage is internal to intent-header-source-check.sh; this epic does not introduce a shared AST contract. If a Polyglot Test Gate epic later requires polyglot AST traversal, it will own that capability independently. The two epics' sg invocations are not coupled.

- Stale file_impact arrays produce false-positive header_source_mismatch (high/correctness): partially mitigated by SC1's new file_impact_likely_stale finding type — staleness is surfaced as warn rather than masquerading as a genuine mismatch.

- Tautological import satisfies (a+) symbol-reference check despite zero behavioral catch power (high/correctness): accepted as known by-design residual; reserved for 411b-a047's mutation-kill verification.
- ARG_MAX exceeded for large epics' findings JSON (high/runtime): mitigated by SC2/SC3's --output-file flag — findings written to disk, not passed via shell arg or env var.

- CI findings comment on fork PRs triggers no-permission error (low/deployment): mitigated by SC4(c)'s GHA-summary fallback — signal survives even when comment-write is unavailable; documented as a known limitation pending fork-PR security work.

- Intent-anchored line coverage and manifest-claim depth metrics: deferred to fb3e-b01b at P4. Stronger signals require polyglot per-test line-coverage infrastructure (coverage.py + bashcov + istanbul/nyc) and per-test attribution storage; the ROI on those vs 411b-a047's mutation-kill is poor.
- Behavioral adequacy of imports: a test that imports a source module but doesn't actually exercise the SC behavior satisfies (a+). Reserved for 411b-a047's mutation-kill verification.
- Polyglot Test Gate AST traversal patterns: 7f42 does not introduce a shared sg invocation contract. Polyglot Test Gate (if pursued) owns its own AST traversal.
- Fork-PR-friendly findings posting: deferred to CI security work; SC4(c)'s GHA-summary fallback is the interim signal.

| `source_files` (94ed manifest entry field) | Planner-agent during `/dso:implementation-plan` when filling 94ed manifest | Re-runs of `/dso:implementation-plan` on revised SCs | SC3 `intent-header-source-check.sh`; 94ed's manifest-aware validator | Implicit with manifest entry — when the intent_id is removed (SC removed from epic) |

| `deferred_test` (94ed manifest entry field, bool) | Planner-agent or operator during `/dso:implementation-plan` when test is intentionally deferred | Operator flips to `false` once the deferred test is registered | SC4(a) pre-commit gate; closure-time block-check | Implicit with manifest entry; operator may zero out the override post-registration |

| `COVERAGE_FINDINGS_<epic-id>` PR-comment marker | SC4(c) `intent-coverage.yml` first run on a PR posts the comment with this marker | Subsequent runs upsert-by-marker (find + edit in place) | The upsert workflow itself reads its own marker to find prior comment | N/A — scoped per-PR; PR closure implicitly retires its comment thread (GitHub does not require active cleanup). The marker is a discriminator within a single PR's comment list, NOT a global registry. |

| `contract_version=1` (published JSON schema) | SC1 publishes `contract_version=1` in the schema | Breaking changes bump to `contract_version=2` with formal versioned migration | Each consumer validates incoming findings JSON against the schema before processing | Persistent — version field lives with the schema; older versions deprecated through formal version bump, not deletion |
- `grep -nE 'source_files|deferred_test' plugins/dso/docs/contracts/intent-allocation-manifest.md` shows both fields documented in the 94ed manifest schema.
Closes the audit's named gaps: PR-comment marker RETIRE = scoped per-PR (PR closure implicit cleanup); `deferred_test` RETIRE = operator flips or implicit with manifest entry removal.

The original 2026-05-16 remediation pass deferred probe 6 because the audit's suggestion was framed as an External Dependencies block gating closure on external state. Reframing: the in-session sprint environment has `gh` CLI access, which makes GitHub PR-comment and GHA-summary state directly verifiable. Adding the in-session checks here:

| Upsert-by-marker PR comment posts successfully | After SC4(c) workflow runs on a sprint PR: `gh api /repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues/<pr>/comments --jq '[.[] \| select(.body \| contains("COVERAGE_FINDINGS_"))] \| length'` | ≥1 |
| Upsert-by-marker idempotency | Re-run intent-coverage.yml on the same PR; count remains the same (no thread; second run edits in place) | Same count, second run logs show `edit` action |
| GHA-summary fallback works on fork PRs | Fork-PR fixture: `gh run view <run-id> --log \| grep -c "COVERAGE_FINDINGS_"` | ≥1 (summary contains marker even when comment-write unavailable) |

| Schema contract version validates | `python3 -c "import json,jsonschema; jsonschema.validate(json.load(open('plugins/dso/docs/contracts/intent-coverage-findings.md.schema')), {'\$schema':'http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#'})"` | Returns 0 |

Verification is in-session: gh CLI is available in the sprint environment, fork-PR fixture is created during sprint dogfooding, and the schema artifact ships in-tree. Converts the prose-only external-dependency concern into a structured contract surface.

- a03c-d55e (Closure Checks schema migration) — required. Findings reference end-state SC/DoD/AC items separated from Closure Checks by a03c's schema cleavage; surfaced via a03c's pluggable end-state-item-validator hook.

- 94ed-f55c (Plan-time intent allocation manifest) — required. SC2's check consumes the manifest via intent-allocation-read.sh; SC3's source_files resolution prefers the manifest entry's source_files field; SC4(b) hooks into 94ed's manifest-aware default validator.
- d566-afa6 (Generation-time prevention) — required. SC3 parses test-file intent-claim headers per d566-afa6 Rule 6.
- New optional field per manifest entry: `source_files: [array of source file paths]`. When present, used preferentially over parent ticket file_impact for SC3's source-symbol resolution.
- New optional field per manifest entry: `deferred_test: bool` (default false). When true, suppresses intent_with_no_test at closure-time block evaluation (SC2 step iii).

Both extensions are additive and non-breaking for forward-compat-preserving consumers (94ed's spec explicitly requires unknown-field passthrough). Coordination via ticket comment on 94ed-f55c-51f5-45f6 referencing this epic and the two new fields.
- Scenario analysis (Step 3): triggered (SCs >= 5); 15 red-team scenarios; 4 surviving after blue-team filter (all addressed via additional spec mitigations).

- Cross-epic scan (Step 2.25): 1 conflict (a03c hook coupling, intentional), 1 ambiguity (d566 Rule 6 dep, manageable), 5 considerations (94ed schema lock, 69e8 consumer, c13f, cf7b, Polyglot Test Gate [now explicitly descoped], CodeQL gates), 2 benign.
- Bot-psychologist (Step 5): not triggered — this epic ships deterministic check scripts and thin hook wiring with no new LLM-facing prompt or skill content.
- Fidelity review (Step 4): Agent Clarity (5, 5), Scope (4, 4, 4, 4), Value (4, 4). All dimensions >= 4 after one revision cycle.
- Scale context (Step 0): small — per-PR or per-epic metric computation; not a high-traffic system.

- Session-signal override for complexity routing: success_criteria_count = 6 (< 7 threshold); scenario_survivor_count = 4 (< 10 threshold) — would route per complexity-evaluator output; preplanning explicitly deferred this session.

- User-directed scope decisions during brainstorm: ship full (a) + full (a+); placeholder fb3e-b01b at P4 created for (b)+(c) deeper signals; deterministic-script implementation (no LLM dispatch in checks); 10% ambiguous cases fail open with warn.

- (i) MID_SPRINT_SC_ADDITION: fixture epic with 1 SC and 1 test_artifact registered passing; a 2nd SC is added to the epic description without registering a corresponding test_artifact. intent-coverage-check.sh surfaces intent_with_no_test for the new SC; completion-verifier dispatch produces non-empty "Intent Allocation Findings" section. Verifies the primary real-world miss pattern.

DIG-2233.summary: Test creation calibration (b): suite growth tracks behavioral coverage, not line count

content.text: LLM test-writing sub-agents in this project (red-test-writer, sprint task-execution prompt, fix-bug RED phase) routinely produce tests that assert on internal method names, mock-invocation counts, or source-grep patterns rather than on observable system behavior. Research documents this failure mode: ~25% of LLM oracles are wrong-but-confident (Di Grazia et al. ASE 2025), 30-60% of LLM tests fail basic compile/execute floors (Yuan et al. 2024), and LLM tests show Assertion Roulette in 38-49% of class-level tests (Wang et al. 2024). The existing 5-rule behavioral-testing-standard.md describes correct principles but is too abstract to bind at generation time. This epic introduces a structured per-test intent-claim header that test-writers attach to every new or modified test, and extends the existing code-reviewer-test-quality agent with two review dimensions to enforce both assertion shape and articulation during code review. Pre-commit gating is deliberately out of scope — enforcement runs through the review overlay only, with iteration in the wild before any deterministic tooling is added.

- SC1: plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/behavioral-testing-standard.md gains Rule 6 — every NEW or MODIFIED test in the diff carries a fenced "## Test Intent" header above the test function with fields intent_id (SC|DoD|AC reference from parent ticket subtree, or "UNTRACKED — <one-line rationale>" permitted sentinel) and catches_regression_where (sentence-completion form: "this test turns RED if and only if [specific production-code change]"). Rule 6 includes canonical per-language header fixture examples covering Python (docstring with markdown fence inside), JavaScript/TypeScript (block comment with markdown fence inside), and bash (line-comment block with markdown fence inside). Legacy tests not modified in the diff are exempt.

- SC2: behavioral-testing-standard.md gains Rule 7 — when adding behavioral coverage for an intent_id already claimed by an existing test, add a sibling parameterized case or new sibling test function in the same test file. Do NOT append assertions to an existing test function. Do NOT create a duplicate test function claiming the same intent_id without an orthogonal scenario suffix. Each test function carries at most one "## Test Intent" header. behavioral-testing-standard.md is designated a safeguard file per CLAUDE.md rule 22 — sub-agents may not propose edits that weaken Rule 6 or 7 without explicit user approval.

- SC3: Three test-writing surfaces updated to reference Rules 6 and 7 in their generation guidance: plugins/dso/agents/red-test-writer.md, plugins/dso/skills/sprint/prompts/task-execution.md, and the fix-bug RED-phase prompt (concrete path under plugins/dso/skills/fix-bug/ resolved during implementation-plan). Synthetic verification: a dispatch of dso:red-test-writer against a fixture task containing one AC produces a test file whose header parses under the per-language syntax appendix and whose intent_id field exactly matches the fixture AC identifier; parse success is confirmed by an automated grep that finds the fenced "## Test Intent" block, the intent_id field, and the catches_regression_where field in the output.

- SC4: plugins/dso/docs/workflows/prompts/reviewer-delta-test-quality.md (the build source for the compiled plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-test-quality.md agent, regenerated via build-review-agents.sh) gains two new review dimensions. Tier 1 (assertion shape) emits a finding when a test assertion targets internal method names, private state, mock-invocation counts (e.g., mock.called_with), or source-grep patterns against source files; requires assertions to target observable outputs (return values, exit codes, file contents, side effects, emitted events). Tier 2 (articulation) emits a finding when (a) a new/modified test has missing or malformed header, (b) catches_regression_where is tautological, (c) the assertions do not exercise the intent named in intent_id (REQUIRED scaffold: reviewer first lists the observable artifact each assert measures, then lists what intent_id claims is measured, then flags if these two sets are disjoint), (d) catches_regression_where would not in fact cause the test to fail given the assertions present, (e) duplicate intent_id without orthogonal scenario suffix or sibling-case structure per Rule 7. Dimension carries an anti-sycophancy prime: "Identify the single most damaging flaw. If no flaw exists, state 'No findings' explicitly." The build pipeline regenerates code-reviewer-test-quality.md from this delta source as part of the implementation work.

- SC5: A /dso:review run against a synthetic diff containing (a) a new test with no header, (b) a new test asserting only on mock.called_with(...), (c) a new test whose intent_id claims SC-1 but whose only assertion is `assert True == True`, produces a reviewer-findings.json where the findings[] array includes at least one entry with dimension matching "Tier 1 (assertion shape)" or "Tier 2 (articulation)" AND whose source_path:source_line falls inside violations (a), (b), (c) respectively. The same findings[] array contains zero entries with those dimensions whose source_line falls inside any unmodified legacy test block in the same diff.
Each "5-rule" / "five rules" / "Rule 5" reference is updated to version-agnostic phrasing OR extended to enumerate Rules 6 and 7.
- SC7 (dogfood): The tests written for d566's own implementation carry valid Rule 6 headers. A /dso:review run on the d566 implementation PR emits zero Tier 1 or Tier 2 findings on those tests.

- SC8 (explicit descope): plugins/dso/hooks/pre-commit-test-quality-gate.sh and plugins/dso/hooks/semgrep-rules/test-anti-patterns.yaml are explicitly NOT extended by this epic. Rule 6 + Rule 7 enforcement is review-only via the dimensions added to code-reviewer-test-quality in SC4. If future evidence supports adding hook-level enforcement, a follow-on epic will scope it.

Every match is triaged into one of three outcomes: (i) updated to version-agnostic phrasing or extended to reference Rules 6/7, (ii) explicitly descoped with a one-line rationale (e.g., "Rule 5 in this context refers to a different standard"), or (iii) already version-agnostic — no change required. The implementation PR description includes the full final grep output (count and list of matches) plus the triage disposition for each one (file path → outcome i/ii/iii with rationale where required). Pattern validation against the 14 consumers identified during brainstorm confirmed 100% coverage at brainstorm time; this SC ensures any consumer added between brainstorm and implementation is also caught.

Inline rule additions to behavioral-testing-standard.md (Rule 6 + Rule 7 + per-language syntax appendix with canonical fixture examples). Prompt updates to three test-writing surfaces. Extension of reviewer-delta-test-quality.md (build source) — rebuild via build-review-agents.sh regenerates code-reviewer-test-quality.md. Pointer updates across the 10 named consumer files in SC6, plus structural sweep per SC9 to catch any unenumerated consumers. No new tooling, no new contracts, no new scripts.
- Fabricated tautological catches_regression_where (high/correctness): partially mitigated by Tier 2(b) and (d) reviewer checks; residual risk that the reviewer is itself LLM-judgment-based.
- intent_id collision across distinct scenarios sharing an abstract SC (high/correctness): partially mitigated by Rule 7 orthogonal-suffix requirement; "orthogonal" is reviewer judgment.

- Claim-vs-assertion contradiction degrades without manifest (critical/observability): partially mitigated by predicate-listing scaffold in Tier 2(c); semantic drift remains until 94ed-f55c manifest ships.
- Bash test header silent no-match in parser (high/runtime): partially mitigated by canonical per-language fixtures in SC1.
- LLM reviewer sycophancy on fluent headers (high/correctness): partially mitigated by anti-sycophancy prime; instructional primes are a known weak defense.
- Test rename orphans header (medium/configuration): unmitigated; deferred to 94ed/411b.
- Multiple tasks retroactively claim same test for different intent_ids (high/correctness): mitigated by one-header-per-function rule in SC2.
- Agent self-proposes Rule 6 relaxation (medium/configuration): mitigated by safeguard-file designation in SC2.
- Polyglot header embedding inconsistency (medium/runtime): partially mitigated by canonical fixtures.

Three independent research dispatches during brainstorm surveyed academic literature, open-source tooling, and practitioner thought leaders on the question "at generation time, how do we know whether a candidate test would catch a real regression?" Convergent findings across all streams identified three signal tiers: Tier 1 (assertion shape — observable output vs internal name; cheap floor; 30–60% of LLM tests fail this per Yuan et al. 2024), Tier 2 (articulation — name the invariant and the plausible mutation; medium cost, LLM-friendly; cross-practitioner consensus from Khorikov, Beck, Bach/Bolton, Hughes/Wayne, Fowler), Tier 3 (empirical — mutant kill on the changed line; Meta TestGen-LLM 2025 mutation-guided pipeline; deferred to sibling epic 411b-a047). This epic implements Tiers 1 and 2 only.

- a03c-d55e (Closure Checks schema migration) — required because intent_id under Rule 6 must reference end-state SC/DoD/AC, which a03c structurally separates from transitional Closure Checks via the new "## Closure Checks" template section and the updated verifiable-sc-check.md end-state-only rule. d566 owns the header schema; a03c's completion-verifier consumes Rule 6 headers for intent_id→test_artifact lookup. Sequential dependency, no conflict.

- 94ed-f55c (Plan-time intent allocation manifest) — required because Rule 6 intent_id field references manifest entries. d566 ships only after 94ed publishes the manifest schema and intent_id format.

- 7f42-e41f (suite growth metrics, sibling) — sequencing: d566 ships first; 7f42 builds on d566's header schema for its per-intent-item growth metrics. To avoid concurrent edits to behavioral-testing-standard.md, 7f42's brainstorm/implementation defers until d566 closes.
- 7f42-e41f: suite growth tracks behavioral coverage (Tier 1+2 metrics).
- 69e8-af39: feedback loop from production bugs and review findings into test-creation prompts.
- Web research (Step 2 of scrutiny pipeline): not triggered — external research was performed at user request during Phase 1 dialogue, prior to Step 2 firing.
- Scenario analysis (Step 3): triggered (SCs ≥ 5); 12 red-team scenarios surfaced, 9 surviving after blue-team filter.

- Cross-epic scan (Step 2.25): triggered against a focused candidate set of 16 test/agent/review-related open epics. 1 ambiguity (a03c-d55e) resolved in Dependencies; 4 consideration signals on sibling/prereq epics; 1 benign signal on kudos.

- Bot-psychologist (Step 5): triggered (LLM-instruction signal: agent definitions + prompt templates). Findings folded into SC1, SC2, SC4 (catches_regression_where rename, UNTRACKED sentinel, predicate-listing scaffold, anti-sycophancy prime, sibling-case rule).

- Fidelity review (Step 4): Agent Clarity pass (5, 4), Value pass (4, 4), Scope (4, 4, 4, 3); consumer_completeness=3 finding structurally resolved by SC9 sweep. Reviewer anti-pattern incident filed as bug 270e-225f-6c72-4f0c.
- Scale context (Step 0): not applicable — development-time tool, per-test-author invocation.
- Session-signal override for complexity routing: success_criteria_count = 9 (≥ 7 threshold) AND scenario_survivor_count = 9 (close to 10 threshold) — routes to /dso:preplanning full mode.
