DIG-2234.summary: Test creation calibration (a): generation-time prevention of change-detector tests

content.text: Test-writing sub-agents, the test-quality reviewer (d566-afa6), and the completion verifier (post-a03c-d55e) today have no canonical artifact that maps end-state intent items (SC/DoD/AC entries) to the tickets that own their test coverage. Concrete failure modes: duplicate test coverage emerges when parallel sprint sub-agents work against the same parent SC; orphan intent items (SCs no task ever covers) go undetected; the a03c-d55e pluggable validator hook has nothing to validate against when checking "does this end-state item have covering tests?". After this epic ships, when a sprint agent writes a test for SC2 the manifest validator will surface a duplicate-coverage warning at task closure; sprint orchestrators will see a distinct "Intent Allocation Findings" section in completion-verifier output where today they see silent pass-through.

- a03c-d55e provides a pluggable end-state-item-validator hook (contract_version=1; input {item_text, item_source_ticket_id, closure_timestamp}; output {valid, reason, severity: "block" or "warn"}). 94ed registers a manifest-aware default validator with this hook.
- d566-afa6 reads intent_id from the manifest to deduplicate test-quality reviewer suggestions; requires the stable slug-format intent_id this epic defines.
- 411b-a047 reads the manifest's intent_id-to-test_artifact mapping (manifest entry field `test_artifact.path`) to associate mutation findings with specific intent items.
- 7f42-e41f reads the manifest for per-intent-item growth metrics aggregation.
- 69e8-af39 mutates manifest entries to retroactively attribute production bug fixes back to intent items.

SC1: plugins/dso/docs/contracts/intent-allocation-manifest.md published. Per-entry schema: {intent_id (STABLE — slug or UUID; normative slug format `[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+){2,5}` derived deterministically from {epic_id_prefix, item_index, first_5_words_kebab_case}; never ordinal-derived; minted at item creation), owner_ticket (full ticket ID), test_artifact: {path: string, kind: "new"|"existing"}, deferred: bool (default false), lightweight: bool (default false; set by /dso:preplanning --lightweight when an item is not reassigned), shared_infra: optional epic-ID (explicit cross-epic owner_ticket sentinel), confidence: optional "high"|"medium"|"low" (assistant-emitted), rationale: optional string}. Manifest-level: contract_version=1. Tooling MUST preserve unknown entry fields in passthrough for forward-compatibility. Validator acceptance rule: entry is valid when intent_id matches the slug regex, owner_ticket resolves to a real ticket in the epic subtree (or shared_infra is set), and (kind="new" with path being a future path) OR (kind="existing" with the path file existing on disk).

SC2: /dso:brainstorm Phase 3 emits INTENT_ALLOCATION_BRAINSTORM: JSON ticket comment on the epic via plugins/dso/scripts/ticket-comment-from-file.sh (temp-file write to avoid ARG_MAX). Each end-state SC drafted gets an entry; intent_id minted by plugins/dso/scripts/intent-id-mint.sh from {epic_id, sc_index, first_5_words(sc_text)}; deferred=true; owner_ticket=epic-itself.

SC3: /dso:preplanning emits INTENT_ALLOCATION_PREPLANNING: JSON ticket comment on the parent epic (temp-file write). For each story DoD, mint stable intent_id. When reassigning an epic SC to a story, preserve the existing intent_id and set deferred=false. When running --lightweight, still emit the comment; unreassigned items get lightweight=true (default unset, only set in --lightweight mode) and deferred=true — this distinguishes intentional placeholders from genuine orphans.

SC4: /dso:implementation-plan emits INTENT_ALLOCATION_IMPLPLAN: JSON ticket comment on the parent story (temp-file write). For each task AC, mint stable intent_id. When reassigning a story DoD to a task, preserve intent_id and set deferred=false. test_artifact populated with the task's proposed test path (kind=new) OR an existing test path (kind=existing) for retroactive attribution.

SC5: plugins/dso/scripts/intent-allocation-read.sh <epic-id> walks the epic subtree, reads all INTENT_ALLOCATION_<STAGE>: comments, merges by stable intent_id. Stage precedence: brainstorm < preplanning < implementation-plan. Within-stage tiebreaker: most-recent timestamp. Same-stage same-timestamp tiebreaker: comment UUID lexical order (deterministic). _conflicts array surfaces equal-stage duplicates AND interleaved-stage anomalies (e.g., implementation-plan timestamp predates a late preplanning write). Output preserves unknown fields.

- orphan_intent: an intent_id present in any INTENT_ALLOCATION_<STAGE>: comment but with no resolved manifest entry after stage-precedence merge (seeded but never reassigned, never resolved by a downstream stage).
- unresolved_ambiguity: entry with merge-conflict that the merge rule could not resolve.
- stale_entry: entry whose intent_id no longer matches any current ticket text in the epic subtree.
- lightweight_pending: lightweight=true; actionable, distinct from orphan; surfaces items that --lightweight preplanning explicitly flagged for follow-up.
- cross_epic_reference: owner_ticket resolves outside the epic subtree AND shared_infra field is unset.
Output supports --summary-mode flag for high-volume epics (groups findings by type with count-only output). Exit 0 on no actionable findings; non-zero with count when issues present.

SC7: a03c-d55e's pluggable end-state-item-validator hook is augmented with the manifest-aware default validator (registered when 94ed ships). Returns {valid: false, severity: "warn", reason: <finding_type>} for orphan_intent, unresolved_ambiguity, cross_epic_reference; {valid: true} for clean entries; ignores pending_intent and lightweight_pending (informational only). Falls back to a03c's basic default ("present and well-formed text") when the manifest is absent (legacy or pre-94ed tickets). The completion-verifier output template is updated to include a distinct "Intent Allocation Findings" section that surfaces warn-severity findings prominently (not buried in general output).

SC8: plugins/dso/agents/intent-allocation-assistant.md (opus-tier). Dispatched by /dso:preplanning and /dso:implementation-plan ONLY when count(unassigned-or-deferred intent items) > 0. Input: full decomposition tree as structured JSON (ticket IDs + types + scope summaries), unassigned intent items, parent's existing manifest entries. Output: per-item {intent_id, proposed_owner_ticket, proposed_test_artifact, rationale referencing specific ticket attributes (e.g., "task T3 owns AC-2 because T3's scope is the only one that touches the auth layer"), confidence: high|medium|low}. Confidence as ROUTING SIGNAL: high suggestions are pre-accepted (planner can reject any one); low suggestions are mandatory review (no batch-skip); medium suggestions follow per-item flow ("each suggestion presented individually; planner must explicitly accept, edit, or reject before the next is shown"). After all suggestions are presented, planner must identify 1-2 least-confident assignments (challenge round) before proceeding.
SC9: Cross-epic coordination with a03c-d55e. Three deliverables:

(i) a03c's haiku migration of brainstorm:complete-tagged epics is extended (in a03c's migration script) to ALSO emit INTENT_ALLOCATION_BRAINSTORM with deferred=true entries per item classified as end-state.
(ii) A ticket comment is posted to a03c-d55e-1393-4f27 referencing 94ed-f55c-51f5-45f6 and SC9, documenting the cross-epic dependency.
(iii) a03c-d55e's epic description is amended (via PR) to add a sub-bullet under its migration SC referencing the manifest backfill step.

Pass criterion: a fixture epic with 2 SCs in its description, post-a03c-migration, produces exactly 2 INTENT_ALLOCATION_BRAINSTORM entries with deferred=true and valid intent_ids matching the SC1 slug regex.
SC10: Synthetic end-to-end test covering three scenarios:

(a) HAPPY PATH: /dso:brainstorm dispatch produces 3-SC epic; INTENT_ALLOCATION_BRAINSTORM written with stable IDs + deferred=true. /dso:preplanning produces stories; INTENT_ALLOCATION_PREPLANNING extends manifest; SC entries reassigned with deferred=false. /dso:implementation-plan produces tasks; INTENT_ALLOCATION_IMPLPLAN extends manifest. read.sh returns merged manifest with zero _conflicts. validate.sh returns zero orphan_intent + zero lightweight_pending.

(b) PARALLEL-SPRINT DUPLICATE-DETECTION: simulate two sprint dispatches each registering a test_artifact entry against the same intent_id. BOTH signals must fire: validate.sh surfaces unresolved_ambiguity AND the test-quality reviewer (d566 integration once shipped, or a stand-in synthetic invocation) surfaces a dedup warning. Test pass requires both.

(c) ORPHAN-DETECTION: fixture epic with 1 SC and preplanning but no implementation-plan stage. With --lightweight preplanning the SC's manifest entry must have lightweight=true and deferred=true (default behavior of --lightweight, defined here). validate.sh surfaces lightweight_pending; completion-verifier dispatch produces a non-empty "Intent Allocation Findings" section naming the unresolved SC.

SC11: Assistant validation. Fixture preplanning dispatch with a 5-SC, 3-story epic triggers intent-allocation-assistant. Output includes at least one suggestion at each confidence tier (high, medium, low). Challenge round exercised (planner identifies 1-2 low-confidence items). Per-item acknowledge log records accept, edit, and reject paths at least once each.
Five sequential phases, each independently mergeable:
- Phase 1: SC1 (contract) + SC2/SC3/SC4 (brainstorm/preplanning/implementation-plan emit INTENT_ALLOCATION_<STAGE>: comments) + stable-id helper.
- Phase 2: SC5 (read helper with stage-precedence + UUID tiebreaker) + SC6 (validate with 6 finding types + --summary-mode).
- Phase 3: SC7 (a03c hook integration + visible "Intent Allocation Findings" output section) + SC9 (cross-epic coordination — a03c migration backfill).
- Phase 4: SC8 (auto-population assistant with confidence-as-routing + challenge round) + SC11 (assistant validation).
- Interleaved multi-stage writes break most-recent-wins (critical/correctness): partially mitigated by stage-precedence + UUID tiebreaker in SC5; residual risk in clock-skew across worktrees.
- Concurrent preplanning worktrees emit conflicting comments (critical/correctness): partially mitigated by _conflicts array surfacing in SC5; no automated resolution; manual reconciliation required.
- owner_ticket=epic sentinel never reassigned in --lightweight (high/correctness): mitigated by SC3 lightweight=true flag and SC6 lightweight_pending finding type (distinct from orphan).

- False test attribution: kind=existing path references a test that doesn't actually verify the intent (high/correctness): unmitigated; this is an LLM-judgment edge that no static check can resolve without semantic introspection of the test code.
- a03c hook warn severity silently masked (medium/observability): mitigated by SC7 distinct "Intent Allocation Findings" section in completion-verifier output.

- Assistant proposes owner=current-task generically (medium/adoption): partially mitigated by SC8 decomposition-tree-as-structured-input + rationale-must-reference-specific-ticket-attribute requirement.
- Cross-epic owner_ticket reference (medium/correctness): mitigated by SC1 shared_infra field + SC6 cross_epic_reference finding type.
- Per-item acknowledge UI fatigue (medium/adoption): partially mitigated by SC8 confidence-as-routing (high pre-accepted, low mandatory) + challenge round; residual risk on medium-tier volume.
- Epic closure leaves manifest entries as permanent orphans (medium/correctness): unmitigated; deferred to ticket-system observability work outside this epic's scope.
- Equal-timestamp merge non-deterministic (low/correctness): mitigated by SC5 UUID tiebreaker.

Cross-stream synthesis from d566-afa6's brainstorm research dispatches identified intent-claim articulation (Tier 2) as the strongest LLM-friendly catch-power signal. This epic delivers the manifest infrastructure that the Tier 2 articulation references — without a stable shared intent_id vocabulary, Tier 2 claims devolve into free-text drift.
### State Lifecycle — RETIRE owner for INTENT_ALLOCATION_<STAGE> manifest comment streams (Probe-3 remediation)

CREATE / UPDATE / CONSUME owners for the `INTENT_ALLOCATION_<STAGE>` ticket-comment manifest stream are already named in SC2 / SC3 / SC4 (brainstorm / preplanning / implementation-plan emitters) and SC5 / SC6 / SC7 (read.sh, validate.sh, a03c hook + downstream consumers). The audit identified the missing RETIRE owner — surfaced as deferred in SC10's blue-team analysis. Resolving here:

Manifest comment streams remain on their parent ticket indefinitely as durable historical record, consistent with ticket-system-v3 event-sourcing semantics (comments are append-only; the CLI exposes no `ticket comment-delete` operation in standard use). Comments are retired only when the parent ticket itself is deleted via `.claude/scripts/dso ticket delete <id> --user-approved` (a human-approved terminal operation), which cascades to remove all associated comments.

This converts SC10's "deferred" blue-team item into a documented design choice: the manifest is intentionally persistent so downstream consumers (d566 / 411b / 7f42 / 69e8) can audit historical intent allocations on closed epics. "Orphan" status is reframed as "archival" — orphans are the desired end-state for closed epics, not a hygiene problem.
- `.claude/scripts/dso ticket comment --help 2>&1 | grep -ci 'delete\|remove'` returns 0 (CLI has no comment-deletion operation in standard use; only ticket-delete cascades).
- The 94ed epic description's State Lifecycle / Operational Constraints section explicitly names "N/A — persistent by design; cascade-deleted with parent ticket" as the RETIRE owner.

- a03c-d55e (Closure Checks schema migration) — required. Provides the end-state SC/DoD/AC separation that this epic's intent_id format references; provides the pluggable end-state-item-validator hook that SC7 registers a manifest-aware validator with.

Implicit downstream coupling: this epic amends d566-afa6's Rule 6 (in behavioral-testing-standard.md) to use stable slug-format intent_id rather than ordinal references (SC-1, DoD-2.a). Recoverable since d566 has not yet been preplanned or implemented. The amendment is recorded as a ticket comment on d566.
- Web research (Step 2): not triggered. Sufficient context inherited from d566 brainstorm research dispatches.
- Scenario analysis (Step 3): triggered (SCs >= 5); 16 red-team scenarios surfaced; 10 surviving after blue-team filter.

- Cross-epic scan (Step 2.25): 1 conflict (a03c, intentional hook coupling), 1 ambiguity (d566 intent_id vocabulary resolved via Dependencies amendment note), 3 considerations (411b/7f42/69e8 downstream consumers), 2 benign.

- Bot-psychologist (Step 5): triggered (LLM-instruction signal — modifies brainstorm/preplanning/implementation-plan skills + new opus assistant agent). Five risks identified; all folded into SC1 (stable intent_id), SC2 (deferred flag default), SC8 (confidence-as-routing, challenge round, structured decomposition tree), SC6 (lightweight_pending finding type).
- Fidelity review (Step 4): Agent Clarity (4, 4), Scope (4, 5, 4, 4), Value (5, 5). All dimensions >= 4.
- Scale context (Step 0): small — per-epic artifact, dozens of entries max per manifest. Not volume-sensitive at runtime.
- Session-signal override for complexity routing: success_criteria_count = 11 (>= 7 threshold) — would route to /dso:preplanning full mode if invoked; preplanning explicitly deferred this session.
- User-directed scope additions: ship all three approach options (A + B + C) — minimal infrastructure + validation tool + auto-population assistant.

DIG-2251.summary: Plan-time intent allocation: assign owner_ticket + test_artifact to every end-state intent item before implementation begins

content.text: LLM sub-agents (brainstorm, preplanning, sprint task-execution, completion-verifier) treat every SC/DoD/AC item identically today, conflating durable system properties with one-time sprint achievements. Concrete failure modes: the completion verifier produces false-positive closures when transitional tasks masquerade as durable SCs; brainstorm authors write change-detector-style transitional items into SC sections that downstream test-generation systems then treat as test targets; the entire calibration program (d566-afa6, 94ed-f55c, 411b-a047, 7f42-e41f, 69e8-af39) is blocked until this distinction is structural. This epic delivers the schema cleavage as root prerequisite. Ships in four sequential phases — templates, verifier, audit, migration — with a multi-opus coherence walk-through gate before migration cutover.

- SC1: Epic/story/task templates (plugins/dso/skills/brainstorm/phases/epic-description-template.md and equivalents in preplanning, implementation-plan) include "## Closure Checks" section after end-state sections. Required at epic level; optional at story/task with per-level granularity guidance in template comments.

- SC2: plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/verifiable-sc-check.md gains an end-state-only rule with canonical litmus test: "Could this item be false before the sprint began and true only because of this sprint's specific work? If yes, route to Closure Checks." Rule includes accept/reject example list covering past-tense durable invariants (accept: "the system supports OAuth"; accept: "the legacy adapter is absent from imports"; reject: "OAuth has been migrated"; reject: "legacy adapter has been removed"). Brainstorm refusal copy added: "This SC describes a one-time transition rather than a durable system property — moving it to Closure Checks. To keep it as an SC, reframe it as ongoing system behavior."
(a) reads "## Closure Checks" separately from end-state items;
(b) validates each Closure Check one-shot at closure;

(c) walks descendant subtree via parent_id ONLY (not relates_to or depends_on, avoiding shared-descendant fan-out blocking); skips descendants in closed/deleted status; treats blocked as open unless all blockers terminal; emits WARN (not BLOCK) on open descendants without Closure Checks;
(d) handles tickets without "## Closure Checks" section gracefully (treat as zero checks = pass, preserving legacy compatibility);

(e) exposes end-state-item-validator hook at plugins/dso/docs/contracts/end-state-item-validator.md with contract_version=1, input={item_text, item_source_ticket_id, closure_timestamp}, output={valid: bool, reason: string, severity: "block"|"warn"}. Default validator returns {valid: true, severity: "warn"} on present and well-formed items. Contract document includes one worked example of a custom validator.
Outcome: verifier no longer produces false-positive closures on tickets containing mixed Closure Check and SC items.

- SC4: plugins/dso/scripts/audit-closure-checks-migration.sh implements combined methodology over .md, .sh, .py, .yaml, .yml files in plugins/, tests/, docs/. Pattern sweep includes variable-interpolation hints (e.g., $VAR='Closure Checks'), aliases (closure-chk, cc-items), and section-name regex. Reverse-dependency enumeration follows static imports AND flags dynamic loads (importlib.import_module with variable, $PLUGIN_ROOT-rooted sourcing). Six classification buckets: section-name-reference, file-path-reference, semantic-consumer, test-asserting-on-structure, user-facing-copy, migration-in-progress. Output: structured JSON to plugins/dso/.audit-output/closure-checks-migration-<timestamp>.json. Reconciliation pass terminates after max 5 iterations with remaining flags surfaced as RECONCILIATION_INCOMPLETE.

- SC5: Pointer updates land per bucket recipe across consumer files identified by SC4. Re-running the audit script returns zero unflagged matches OR an explicit RECONCILIATION_INCOMPLETE block listing residuals (steady state).

- SC6: plugins/dso/scripts/migrate-closure-checks.sh dispatches a haiku classifier per SC/DoD/AC item on every brainstorm:complete-tagged epic. Classifier returns {label: end-state|transitional|uncertain, ranking: 1-5, rationale: string}. Escalate to user on label=uncertain OR ranking <= 3. Migration review batches capped at 25 items per batch; per-item explicit acknowledge required (no batch-approve button). Migration is snapshot-based and idempotent — re-runs pick up tickets edited during prior passes. Audit comment per ticket records {snapshot_timestamp, original_text, classification, ranking, rationale}.

- SC7: Synthetic end-to-end test. A /dso:brainstorm dispatch with one end-state SC ("the system supports OAuth") and one transitional SC ("OAuth migration is complete") routes the transitional SC to "## Closure Checks". A /dso:completion-verifier dispatch on an epic with one unresolved Closure Check and all end-state items passing returns refused-closure with a finding naming the unresolved Closure Check.

- SC8: plugins/dso/scripts/audit-closure-checks-migration.sh header contains the verbatim sentence "use sparingly — for simple field renames, targeted grep + one-pass update is sufficient." AND the script name appears in the CLAUDE.md Quick Reference table. Verified by grep against both files.

- SC9: Closure Checks template description requires each item to be one-shot verifiable (a command, a state check, or a reference to a specific named artifact). Standalone synthetic test: a /dso:brainstorm dispatch where a proposed Closure Check phrased as "team has reviewed the design" is submitted produces a rejection message referencing the one-shot-verifiable requirement.

- SC10: Multi-opus-agent workflow coherence walk-through gated between Phase 3 (audit and pointer updates complete) and Phase 4 (migration). content.text: The existing kudos system (Epics 3e9b-afee and 71df-5bd8) includes 5 triggers that silently skip on non-Python stacks. T7 uses Python ast.NodeVisitor. T9 uses ruff (Python-only). T12 uses Python-anchored regexes. T13 and T4 use Python ast.dump() subtree hashing. Ruby and JavaScript developers receive zero kudos from these 5 triggers. This epic replaces them with polyglot equivalents so kudos fires across all supported stacks.
- T7 uses lizard -ENS instead of Python ast.NodeVisitor; supports Python, JS/TS, Ruby, Java; 30s timeout; --exclude for test dirs; when lizard absent: TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal
- T9 reads commands.lint (from Epic B); when absent: TRIGGER_SKIPPED; when present, fires on zero-violation result
- T12 uses line-start-anchored regexes covering Python, JS/TS, Ruby, Java syntax for commented-out code detection
- T13 and T4 use jscpd (JSON reporter to temp dir, 30s timeout, exit code parsing); when jscpd absent: TRIGGER_SKIPPED
- All five triggers emit machine-readable TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal conforming to the signal format established by Kudos Epic 2 (71df-5bd8); no shared library imported from Kudos Epic 2

| `commands.lint` (dso-config.conf, written by Epic B / 3818-310d) | `/dso:onboarding` writes per detected stack at project setup | Operator edit; re-onboarding APPENDS new stacks, never overwrites existing | T9 trigger reads at evaluation time | N/A — persistent per-stack config; key removed only if stack itself is removed from project |

| `TRIGGER_SKIPPED` signal format (shared with Kudos Epic 2) | Each polyglot trigger emits this format when its tool is absent (per the spec) | Format is versioned via `schema_version` field; breaking changes bump version + migration | Kudos Epic 2's aggregator consumes and surfaces in retro | N/A — wire-format protocol; retired only via formal schema version bump with consumer migration |
- `grep -E '^commands\.lint=' .claude/dso-config.conf` shows the key with a sensible default OR an empty value that's documented as "stack-specific, set by /dso:onboarding".
- `grep -nE 'TRIGGER_SKIPPED|schema_version' <plugin-kudos-trigger-scripts>` confirms the signal format is emitted with explicit version field.

- Validation: sprint acceptance test environment has lizard and jscpd installed; test matrix covers all 5 triggers before/after on non-Python files; before: no kudos for Ruby file; after: kudos fires for quality improvement; Kudos Epic 1 must be present in CI or dispatch_kudos_trigger() mocked
- Epic B (3818-310d): T9 reads commands.lint; without Epic B, T9 always emits TRIGGER_SKIPPED
- Kudos Epic 1 (3e9b-afee): T13 and T7 call the kudos dispatch function delivered by Kudos Epic 1; runtime blocking dependency (blocks relationship in ticket system)
- Kudos Epic 2 (71df-5bd8): runtime consumer dependency — Epic C conforms to TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal format so the existing event emitter can handle it

Replace each of the 5 Python-specific trigger implementations with polyglot equivalents: lizard for AST-based nesting analysis (T7), jscpd for duplicate block detection (T13/T4), language-neutral regexes for commented-out code (T12), and commands.lint config key for lint-clean detection (T9). All triggers emit TRIGGER_SKIPPED when required tooling or config is absent.
- External integration (lizard): -ENS flags emit nesting/size metrics; supports Python, JS/TS, Ruby, Java, C/C++; `command -v lizard` absence detection; 30s subprocess timeout required

- External integration (jscpd): JSON reporter to temp dir (`--reporters json --output <dir>`); exit code 0 = no duplicates, 1 = duplicates found; parse via `cat <dir>/jscpd-report.json` (file-based, not stdout); 30s subprocess timeout required
- Dependency (commands.lint from Epic B 3818-310d): polyglot lint config key; absent → TRIGGER_SKIPPED; present → fires on zero-violation exit
- Signal format (TRIGGER_SKIPPED): conforms to Kudos Epic 2 (71df-5bd8) signal format independently — schema duplicated, not imported, to preserve epic independence
- lizard binary absent in CI (high, deployment): T7 voids awards; TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal emitted per Kudos Epic 2 schema; document or accept skip as designed
- jscpd binary absent in CI (high, deployment): T13/T4 void awards; TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal emitted per Kudos Epic 2 schema; document or accept skip as designed
- commands.lint key absent from dso-config.conf (high, configuration): T9 always emits TRIGGER_SKIPPED; onboarding/architect-foundation must populate this key per detected stack
- lizard/jscpd subprocess exceeds 30s timeout (medium, runtime): kill and treat as TRIGGER_SKIPPED; explicit timeout handling required with SIGKILL after grace period

- TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal format drift from Kudos Epic 2 schema (high, integration): format validated independently per epic; schema change in Epic 2 silently breaks Epic C signals — add schema conformance test in this epic
- T12 regex false-positive on language-specific block comments (medium, correctness): Python `"""`, Ruby `=begin/=end`, JS `/** */` need language-aware anchors beyond simple line-start matching
- Testing (03d4-062a, 988f-933e): External binaries need subprocess mocking

content.text: **What**: Replace the Python-specific ast.NodeVisitor implementation of T7 with a lizard-based approach using `lizard -ENS` to measure cognitive complexity (nesting depth) across all supported stacks. Emit TRIGGER_SKIPPED when lizard is not on PATH.

**Why**: T7 today can only measure nesting depth in Python files. Ruby and JavaScript developers who reduce deeply-nested code receive zero kudos. Lizard supports Python, JS/TS, Ruby, and Java, making it the natural polyglot replacement.

- IN: `lizard -ENS` subprocess with 30s timeout; `--exclude` flag for test directories; compare before/after nesting depth from git diff; TRIGGER_SKIPPED when `lizard` not on PATH; TRIGGER_SKIPPED on non-zero lizard exit; award kudos when nesting depth decreases
- OUT: Installing lizard in CI (covered by SC6 / Story E); T9, T12, T13, T4
- When this story is complete, T7 fires and awards kudos on a JS/TS file where nesting depth decreased (measured by lizard), and does NOT fire on a file where nesting depth increased or stayed flat
← Satisfies: "T7 uses lizard -ENS instead of Python ast.NodeVisitor; supports Python, JS/TS, Ruby, Java"
- When this story is complete, T7 emits a machine-readable TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal (not an exception) when `lizard` is not found on PATH
- When this story is complete, T7 does not hang — subprocess call enforces 30s timeout; timeout → TRIGGER_SKIPPED
- When this story is complete, test directories are excluded from lizard analysis (`--exclude` passed for dirs matching test/spec patterns)
- When this story is complete, the TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal fields conform to Kudos Epic 2 (71df-5bd8) schema; no shared library imported from Kudos Epic 2
← Satisfies: "All five triggers emit machine-readable TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal"

- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for: PATH-absent case (TRIGGER_SKIPPED), timeout case (TRIGGER_SKIPPED), nesting-decrease case (award), nesting-flat/increase case (no award)
- [Testing] Mock `subprocess.run` (or equivalent) to avoid requiring lizard binary in test environment; test PATH-absent, timeout, zero-exit-code-with-no-decrease, and award-path cases
- [Maintainability] TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal format: reference Kudos Epic 2 (71df-5bd8) for the required field schema; implement independently (no import from Kudos Epic 2 modules)
- [Reliability] dispatch_kudos_trigger() from Kudos Epic 1 (3e9b-afee) must be mocked in unit tests
- [Reliability] Timeout handling: subprocess timeout=30 must be caught and converted to TRIGGER_SKIPPED, not propagated as an exception

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

content.text: Context: The /dso:roadmap skill reads design-notes.md for project archetypes and golden paths but never writes captured design intent back to the file. When a non-engineer runs /dso:roadmap immediately after the bootstrap installer, design-notes.md contains template stubs (vision: 'TBD', archetypes: []). Roadmap captures vision and archetype information during Phase 0 intake but discards it; downstream skills (/dso:brainstorm, /dso:sprint) then operate on stale stubs rather than actual project intent. This epic adds a write-back step to /dso:roadmap Phase 0 that persists captured design intent into design-notes.md.

Approach: Modify /dso:roadmap SKILL.md to add a Phase 0 write-back step immediately after intake completes. Stub detection rule (authoritative definition): a field value is a stub if it matches '' (empty string), 'TBD', 'TODO', 'PLACEHOLDER', null, or [] (empty array). Non-stub values are preserved unchanged. Also update check-onboarding.sh to evaluate design field content against the stub detection rule (not just file existence). Cross-skill schema dependency: design-notes.md schema is co-owned by /dso:onboarding; any future onboarding field additions must be reflected in the write-back logic — document this coupling in plugins/dso/docs/SCHEMA-COUPLING.md.

1. After a roadmap session where the user provides a vision statement, design-notes.md is updated with the captured vision value; for projects with no UI component (no src/app/ or pages/ directory present), the archetypes field is not required and may remain at its existing value.
2. A non-stub value already present in design-notes.md (any value not matching the stub detection rule) is not overwritten when roadmap runs the write-back step.
3. A stub value (matching the stub detection rule: '', 'TBD', 'TODO', 'PLACEHOLDER', null, or []) in design-notes.md is replaced with the roadmap-captured value after Phase 0 completes.

4. check-onboarding.sh is updated (as part of this epic) to evaluate design fields for non-stub content — a design-notes.md with all stub values returns design_onboarding.pass == false; a design-notes.md with real values (as written by roadmap write-back) returns design_onboarding.pass == true.

5. A new integration test at tests/integration/test_roadmap_writeback.sh exists and passes green; the test: (a) simulates a roadmap Phase 0 session capturing a vision value by invoking the write-back step directly with a fixture input (vision string + archetype list) bypassing interactive intake, (b) asserts design-notes.md is written with that value, (c) asserts a pre-existing non-stub value is not overwritten, (d) asserts a stub value is overwritten; this test is written RED-first before any implementation.
Scenario Analysis (5 surviving red team scenarios):
- Stub detection false positive on intentionally short values (medium, runtime): project acronym 'TBD' classified as stub and overwritten
- Write-back fails silently when design-notes.md is read-only (high, runtime): must surface as hard stop, not silent continue
- Schema mismatch on bootstrapped repos with different field layout (medium, deployment): renamed/nested fields cause silent no-op merge
- Single-element stub array bypasses empty-array rule (medium, configuration): archetypes: ['TBD'] is non-empty, preserved as real content
- Multi-line vision string breaks YAML serialization (high, configuration): must use YAML-aware serialization, not string interpolation

Prompt Alignment: LLM-specific risks — value hallucination (LLM fills stubs with plausible-but-wrong values; SKILL.md must anchor each written value to intake transcript); over-eager stub detection (TODO-as-note values must be protected by non-empty sentence guard). Add read-back verification step after write.

Dependencies: 'DSO NextJS Starter: one-command bootstrap for non-engineer prototyping' (primary epic) must complete first — it establishes the stub-initialized design-notes.md in the installed template. check-onboarding.sh content update is scoped into this epic (not a prerequisite).
Priority: Value=3 (Measurable — removes re-prompt friction for non-engineer persona), Effort=3 (Moderate — SKILL.md modification + check-onboarding.sh update + integration test) -> P2

content.text: Agents running design-review, ui-designer, brainstorm, preplanning, and sprint workflows currently operate without a shared corpus of UI/UX design knowledge. Each session starts without government-specific anti-patterns, USWDS component guidance, WCAG 2.2 compliance patterns, or established design principles, causing inconsistent and incomplete guidance. This epic establishes the foundational reference library — schema, corpus structure, full initial content, retrieval infrastructure, and source provenance tracking — that five subsequent epics will integrate into specific agent workflows. It absorbs the government anti-pattern catalog from epic 17de-a47a, seeds the full corpus from permissively licensed sources and Nava-internal reference sources identified during research, and establishes the retrieval contract (ref-query.sh) that all downstream integration epics depend on.

- A corpus directory at plugins/dso/data/ui-reference/ with domain-partitioned Markdown files (each ≤500 lines), YAML frontmatter per entry (id, title, domain[], component[], action[], compliance[], severity, story_type[], coverage, source, license), and three Markdown resolution tiers per entry (### Summary, ### Detail, ### Implementation). A _schema.yaml + check-corpus-schema.sh pre-commit hook enforce tag vocabulary across six dimensions: domain, component, action, compliance, severity, story_type. Domain vocabulary includes gov-benefit-flows (government benefit application form patterns from tested real-world projects). License vocabulary includes internal-nava (paraphrased from internal sources; not for external distribution).

- A _index.yaml manifest committed to the repository (not generated at build time), listing every entry with six-dimension tags, one-liner, file path, coverage tier, source, and license. Full inventory readable without loading any corpus file. Regenerated and recommitted on corpus changes.

- A plugins/dso/scripts/ref-query.sh retrieval script using stdlib Python BM25 (self-contained, no external deps); bm25s used as optional performance accelerator if installed, falls back with stderr notice if not. Flags: --top-n (default 8), --tier=summary|detail|implementation, --session-hash dedup, zero-result stderr signal ([ref-query: no results for query: "..." with filters: ...]), completes within 10 seconds.

- Initial corpus covers: (a) public permissive-license sources — government anti-patterns (all 48 from 17de-a47a at Detail tier; Implementation stretch), USWDS component and token guidance, WCAG 2.2 AAA patterns cross-referenced to Section 508/OMB M-24-08, Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics, Don Norman's principles, GOV.UK Government Design Principles, 18F UX Guide principles, digital.gov federal requirements, Inclusive Design Principles, cognitive load and defensive design checklists, Brignull dark pattern taxonomy, SageSELab AidUI 27-class taxonomy, and representative entries from benbrignell/principles.design; (b) navapbc Apache 2.0 GitHub sources committed directly — navapbc/wic-participant-recertification-portal docs/participant/pages/ (multi-step form flow, minimal PII philosophy, conditional document requirements, skip logic patterns; ~15–25 entries) and docs/decisions/ ADRs (10 ADRs covering Remix for multi-step wizards, Zod validation with custom error codes, UX scoping principles; ~8–12 entries); navapbc/template-application-nextjs docs/decisions/ ADRs on USWDS selection rationale and react-uswds trade-offs (~5–8 entries); (c) Nava-internal Confluence sources, paraphrase-only with license: internal-nava — Nava Pattern Library PL space (Design patterns for online applications: question page and 7 sub-patterns one-question-per-page/repeatable-items/stacking/looping/people-list/someone-else/I-dont-know/grouping; task list; review page; validation and error messages; status page; document upload; mobile responsiveness; confirmation; e-signature; SSN collection; draft/resume; people composition; rights and responsibilities; ~48–68 entries tagged domain: [gov-benefit-flows]); SNAP Policy Requirements and State Options PM3 space (full SNAP lifecycle, state options, unhappy-path client flows; ~20–30 entries); Accessibility Test Checklist AAN space (7-category WCAG/508 checklist; ~25–35 entries); Trauma-Informed Design Practice Guide DOH space (SAMHSA 6 principles applied to government digital services with Grants.gov case study; ~12–15 entries); Lessons Learned from CA EDD/NJ UI/USDOL NUI space (cross-project UX anti-patterns; ~15–20 entries); Agentic Design Patterns for Government Services NL space (multi-level transparency, human-in-the-loop, plain language do/don't pairs for AI caseworker tools; ~10–12 entries). Summary + Detail required for all entries; Implementation is stretch.

- Integration test at tests/integration/test-ref-library.sh (REPO_ROOT-based paths): (a) session-timeout query returns entry tagged auth/forms or containing "session timeout" in Summary; (b) --tier=summary output has ### Summary, no ### Implementation; (c) manifest integrity — every _index.yaml entry resolves to a file at its declared path; (d) no corpus file exceeds 500 lines; (e) precision sub-test — three representative queries ("USWDS form validation", "WCAG 2.2 keyboard navigation", "government authentication anti-pattern") each return a top result whose frontmatter tags match a predefined expected-tag mapping; (f) completes within 10 seconds.
- ref-query.sh registered as dso ref-query shim; check-shim-refs.sh does not block downstream skill file references.

- A docs/ui-reference-sources.yaml file at the project root tracks each reference source with fields: name, url, type (github-repo|github-repo-private|confluence-page|confluence-space|google-doc|web-spec|website), access (public|internal-nava), credentials_required (bool), pinned version/commit (where applicable), last-synced date, license, and which corpus domains it populates. Internal sources (Confluence, Google Docs, private GitHub repos) are supported first-class — url holds the full internal URL; credentials_required: true signals that access requires provisioned credentials. navapbc/benefits-delivery-system is registered as type: github-repo-private, credentials_required: true, with an implementation note that it is expected to be a rich source of benefits delivery design and implementation context pending credentials provisioning. This is the provenance record for all corpus entries, public and internal.

- Initial corpus includes federal-style-canon entries for government UI copy editing — covering USWDS forms, GOV.UK error/form patterns and Service Manual writing for user interfaces, VA.gov Content Style Guide (error anatomy, capitalization, punctuation), 18F Plain Language guide, Federal Plain Language Guidelines (Plain Writing Act of 2010), and CDC reading-level guidance. Each entry carries a stable rule ID, a prior-art citation, and a precedence field. Required by depending epic f360-3a5b-b8f3-4f86 (gov-copy-writer sub-agent).
- bm25s corpus load time timeout (high, runtime): addressed by SC3 10s target and SC5f timing check
- Tag pre-filter zero matches silently (high, runtime): addressed by SC3 zero-result stderr signal and SC1 vocabulary enforcement
- Missing _index.yaml on fresh checkout (critical, deployment): addressed by SC2 committed-not-generated requirement
- Integration test paths break in worktree sessions (high, deployment): addressed by SC5 REPO_ROOT-based path resolution
- Pre-commit integrity blocks downstream skill refs before merge (high, deployment): addressed by Dependencies merge-ordering note
- shim-exempt not applied to ref-query.sh (medium, deployment): addressed by SC6 shim registration
- YAML vocabulary drift causes silent retrieval gaps (high, configuration): addressed by SC1 schema file and check-corpus-schema.sh
- Internal Confluence source inaccessible in CI (medium, deployment): paraphrase-only approach means corpus content is committed to repo; Confluence access not required at runtime or in CI

- Private GitHub repo (BDS) inaccessible without credentials (medium, deployment): addressed by credentials_required flag in ui-reference-sources.yaml; corpus seeding from BDS deferred to a contributor with provisioned access

content.text: **What**: Orchestrator logic for the accept action handler: dispatches a general-purpose fix sub-agent to implement the change requested in the comment, commits and pushes the result, and replies to the comment thread with the commit SHA.
**Why**: Accepting an engineer's change request is the highest-value response — it directly implements feedback and closes the comment loop without manual intervention.

- IN: Receive a pre-classified accept comment (with normalized JSON including path/position fields); dispatch a general-purpose fix sub-agent with the comment body, the file identified by path (and nearby context), and the current PR diff as context; handle failure cases: if sub-agent signals multi-file scope, returns no changes, or reports a conflict — revert ALL partial working-tree changes (including staged changes, unstaged edits, and any new files) before reclassifying to defer per Story 4; handle non-fast-forward push (branch head moved) as a conflict → revert and reclassify to defer; on clean success, commit and push to PR branch, then use the shared reply-posting function from Story 1 to post a thread reply with the commit SHA; all reply bodies begin with <!-- dso-agent-reply -->
- OUT: Comment classification (Story 5); comment fetching and schema (Story 1); comments not classified as accept
- When this story is complete, an accept-classified comment causes a fix sub-agent to apply the requested change, and the handler commits and pushes the result to the PR branch
← Satisfies: "a general-purpose fix sub-agent receives the comment body, relevant source files, and current diff" (SC2)

- When this story is complete, if the fix sub-agent signals multi-file scope, returns no changes, or reports a conflict, ALL partial working-tree changes are completely reverted and the comment is reclassified to defer (no leftover staged or unstaged changes after revert)
← Satisfies: "orchestrator reverts any partial working-tree changes and reclassifies to defer per SC4" (SC2)
- When this story is complete, a non-fast-forward push failure (branch head moved) also triggers revert and reclassify to defer
- When this story is complete, the thread reply includes the commit SHA of the applied fix and begins with <!-- dso-agent-reply -->

MOTIVATION: V1 kudos system is fully mechanical (no LLM judgment, no human input). User-awarded points would add a human oversight layer and cover quality behaviors that are observable to humans but not structurally verifiable from git diff alone.
- User explicitly recognizes a design decision during interactive session ('that was a great approach')
- User approves a particularly well-reasoned implementation-plan proposal
- User notes that an explanation or doc update was especially clear
- Post-session retro: human rates session quality and awards bonus points
- Mechanism: CLI command or slash command for human to award (e.g., /dso:kudos award <points> <reason>)
- Integrity: human-awarded points should be stored separately from mechanical awards in .kudos/ ledger (different trigger_id prefix) to maintain audit trail
- Anti-gaming: human-awarded points should have a session cap independent of mechanical cap to prevent solicitation behavior
- Solicitation disqualifier: agent explicitly asking for kudos points should disqualify the session from human awards
- Goodhart risk: higher risk than mechanical triggers since human judgment is more gameable (agents could optimize for human approval rather than quality)
- Attribution: human-awarded points carry session ID of the human session, not agent session
- Should human awards propagate to sub-agent framing in subsequent sessions?
- Slack/comment integration: award via PR comment or Slack reaction?
- Cross-session visibility: should human awards be visible in the running total display?
- Social recognition systems in software teams (peer recognition vs. manager recognition)
- Gamification research on human-in-the-loop reward systems
- Whether human awards reinforce or undermine mechanical award signal

content.text: DSO is currently Claude Code-only. Add a cross-runtime compatibility layer so DSO skills, hooks, and workflows can function across multiple AI coding tool runtimes.

everything-claude-code (131k stars) achieves cross-runtime parity across 4 runtimes via an adapter.js that normalizes each harness's stdin event format into a shared format, then routes to shared scripts/hooks/*.js:

This DRY architecture means adding a new hook behavior touches one file regardless of how many runtimes are supported. An AGENTS.md file at the repo root serves as the universal cross-tool routing file read by all harnesses.
1. **Adapter layer** — create a runtime adapter that normalizes event formats from different AI coding tools into DSO's internal event model

4. **Hook portability** — identify which hooks map to equivalent events in other runtimes (pre-commit hooks are git-level and already portable; PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks are Claude-specific)
5. **Graceful degradation** — when running on a less-capable runtime, DSO should degrade gracefully (e.g., skip sub-agent dispatch, fall back to single-agent workflows) rather than fail
- The agentskills.io open standard (SKILL.md format) is already portable across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini CLI — DSO skills already use this format

content.text: **What**: A new shell script (pr-comment-response.sh) that fetches all unresolved comments from a GitHub PR — both inline review comments and top-level conversation comments — and writes them to a normalized JSON file for downstream action handlers.

**Why**: All three response handlers (accept, defend, defer) require a consistent, pre-processed view of unresolved PR comments. This script is the data foundation for the entire comment-response pipeline.

- IN: Paginated fetch of inline review comments (via GitHub pull request review comments API) and top-level conversation comments (via GitHub issues comments API); API layer probe at startup — use GitHub MCP server tools (v0.31.0+) if configured and responsive; fallback to gh api --paginate on any MCP failure (401, 403, tool-not-found, timeout); normalization to JSON schema {comment_id, root_comment_id, thread_url, body, author, is_inline, already_replied, defense_comment_id, path, position} where path is the file being commented on (for inline comments) and position is the line number; root_comment_id resolution by walking in_reply_to_id chain to null (the true thread root) — guard against cycles with max-depth limit; deduplication: threads where any reply begins with <!-- dso-agent-reply --> are excluded from the output (already_replied=true); API probe logic implemented as a shared reusable function usable by the standalone skill; empty result: {"comments": [], "skipped_count": <N>}; non-zero exit with "ERROR: <message>" on API failure; gh CLI minimum version check at startup with clear error if below minimum; rate-limit response detection with backoff on paginated fetch; shared thread-reply posting function (is_inline-aware endpoint routing: inline → POST /pulls/{n}/comments/{root_comment_id}/replies; top-level → POST /issues/{n}/comments) for use by all action handlers
- OUT: Comment classification (handled by standalone skill, Story 5); action handler logic; MCP server configuration or installation

- When this story is complete, running pr-comment-response.sh against a test PR produces a normalized JSON file matching the schema {comment_id, root_comment_id, thread_url, body, author, is_inline, already_replied, defense_comment_id, path, position}
← Satisfies: SC1 schema specification (extended with path/position per adversarial review RT-2)
- When this story is complete, root_comment_id for any reply comment is the true thread root (walked to null), and the walk terminates even for malformed/circular references (max-depth guard)
← Satisfies: "root_comment_id is the top-level comment in the thread (resolved by walking in_reply_to_id to the true root for replies)" (SC1)
- When this story is complete, threads that already contain a reply beginning with <!-- dso-agent-reply --> are excluded from output
← Satisfies: "comments are excluded when the thread contains a reply beginning with <!-- dso-agent-reply -->" (SC1)
- When this story is complete, the script exits 0 and writes {"comments": [], "skipped_count": N} when no unresolved comments exist
← Satisfies: "when no unresolved comments exist, exits 0 and writes..." (SC1)
- When this story is complete, the script exits non-zero with "ERROR: <message>" when the GitHub API call fails
← Satisfies: "exits non-zero with ERROR: on API failure" (SC1)
- When this story is complete, the script includes a shared thread-reply posting function with is_inline-aware endpoint routing, used by all three action handlers to avoid duplicated reply logic
← Satisfies: adversarial review finding RT-1 (shared reply posting utility)
- When this story is complete, unit tests are written and passing for all new or modified logic
- [Security] GITHUB_TOKEN accessed in this script — ensure it never appears in script output, debug messages, or error traces (A02:2021 Cryptographic Failures)
- [Reliability] root_comment_id chain walk must terminate — implement max-depth guard (e.g., 50 iterations) or visited-set to prevent infinite loop on malformed circular references

content.text: Epic 1 of 2. Establishes the full kudos ledger infrastructure and 10 primary quality triggers for the process-reward tracking system.

CONTEXT: Engineering teams adopting AI coding agents need a feedback system that reinforces quality behaviors at commit time. Without explicit recognition, agents optimize for task completion over quality practices. This epic delivers the ledger, anti-gaming stack, and 10 triggers so that every commit produces an auditable record of recognized behaviors.

APPROACH: Implement ledger, award formula, anti-gaming controls, and 10 triggers as pure shell + Python stdlib anchored to commit-validate.sh in the existing commit workflow. Spikes S0/S1 de-risk sg pattern matching and Python AST clone detection before those triggers ship.

SPRINT SCOPE RATIONALE: Infrastructure without triggers produces zero awards. All 10 triggers share one user goal (recognizing quality behaviors at commit time) and depend on the same anti-gaming stack. Spike tasks are investigation prerequisites, not sprint work items.

SC-E1-1: .kudos/ledger.jsonl (append-only JSONL) — fields: session_id, trigger_id, diff_hash, artifact_sha, verification_method, workflow_phase, message, points (int >= 1), jitter_factor (float in [0.8,1.2]), timestamp (ISO-8601 UTC); all string fields JSON-escaped; .kudos/ in .gitignore
SC-E1-2: Award formula: Award(n) = round(BasePoints x (1/(n+1)) x jitter), jitter in [0.8,1.2] uniform random, min 1 point, floating-point division; n = prior session ledger entries for trigger_id
SC-E1-3: Deduplication: one award per (trigger_id, diff_hash) per session
SC-E1-4: Session ceiling: kudos.session_ceiling from dso-config.conf (default 100, validated >0; absent key uses default); awards blocked when reached, prohibition-block message shown
SC-E1-5: kudos-write-guard.sh PreToolUse hook blocks Edit/Write to .kudos/** (exit 2); jq-free parse_json_field; registered via onboarding/architect-foundation
SC-E1-6: commit-validate.sh integrated into COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md before commit gate; creates .kudos/ on first run; fails-open (any detection error skips with log, never aborts commit)
SC-E1-7: Session identity UUID written to .kudos/session-id at worktree creation; commit-validate.sh reads from file (fails-open with fresh UUID if absent)
SC-E1-8: Contributor rank displayed per commit: Contributor (0-25), Consistent (26-75), Distinguished (76-150), Exemplary (151-300), Principal Contributor (301+)
SC-E1-9: CLAUDE.md Kudos section: overview, prohibition block (listed before rewards), jitter disclosure (+/-20% random), Goodhart's Law disclosure, rank table

SC-E1-10: diff-to-sg-scope.sh wrapper: command -v sg pre-check (exit 2 if absent); checks HEAD~1 existence (exit 2 if first commit); git diff --name-only HEAD~1; sg run --pattern

--json=stream per file; parses NDJSON

SC-E1-12: Spike S1 implements/tests Python AST subtree hashing prototype (hashlib.sha256(ast.dump(node).encode())); measures false-positive rate; confirms jscpd file-output integration (cat $OUTPUT_DIR/jscpd-report.json, not stdout) if selected as fallback

content.text: ## PR Size Limits as Proactive Guidance

Activate sets a clear 400-line PR size guideline. DSO's review workflow has 300/600 line thresholds for model escalation/rejection, but doesn't guide PR sizing proactively. PR size is only surfaced reactively at review time — by then the work is already done and splitting is costly.
Surface PR size guidance earlier in the workflow — during implementation planning, not just at review time:
- Implementation-plan should estimate diff size per task and flag tasks likely to exceed the 300-line threshold
- Tasks exceeding the estimate should be split proactively during planning, not at review time
- Preplanning should consider PR size when slicing stories — vertical slices should produce reviewable PRs
- Sprint batching should be aware of cumulative diff size per commit/PR
- The 300/600 line thresholds from the review workflow should be referenced as planning constraints, not just review triggers

content.text: **What**: Orchestrator logic for the defend action handler: receives a pre-classified defend comment along with a defense argument generated by the classification step, posts a new PR review comment (not an inline source code comment) with the justification, and replies to the original thread linking to that review comment.

**Why**: Engineers deserve a substantive response when the workflow maintains a design decision. A PR review comment is the appropriate venue for design justifications — it keeps source code clean and surfaces the rationale in the PR conversation.

- IN: Receive a pre-classified defend comment with generated defense argument text (produced by Story 5's classification prompt — not generated here); post a new PR review comment via the correct endpoint: inline (is_inline=true) → POST /pulls/{n}/comments/{root_comment_id}/replies; top-level (is_inline=false) → POST /issues/{n}/comments; write the returned comment ID to defense_comment_id in the normalized JSON file BEFORE posting the thread reply; use the shared reply-posting function from Story 1 to post a thread reply linking to the posted review comment; retry idempotency: if defense_comment_id is already non-null in the JSON, skip step 1 (post review comment) and proceed directly to step 2 (post thread reply); fallback: if inline reply returns 422, fall back to POST /issues/{n}/comments; all reply bodies begin with <!-- dso-agent-reply -->
- OUT: Defense argument text generation (Story 5's classification prompt produces this); source code modification; REVIEW-DEFENSE: inline source code comments; comment classification
- When this story is complete, a defend-classified comment results in a new PR review comment posted via the correct GitHub API endpoint based on the is_inline field in the normalized JSON

← Satisfies: "post a new PR review comment (not a # REVIEW-DEFENSE: source code comment) via the correct endpoint (inline: POST /pulls/{n}/comments/{root_comment_id}/replies; top-level: POST /issues/{n}/comments)" (SC3)
- When this story is complete, the returned review comment ID is written to defense_comment_id in the normalized JSON file before the thread reply is posted
← Satisfies: "write the returned comment ID to defense_comment_id in the normalized JSON" (SC3)
- When this story is complete, if defense_comment_id is already non-null (retry case), step 1 (post review comment) is skipped and only the thread reply is posted
← Satisfies: "on retry, defense_comment_id being non-null skips step 1 and proceeds directly to step 2" (SC3)
- When this story is complete, if the inline reply endpoint returns 422, the handler falls back to POST /issues/{n}/comments without failing
← Satisfies: "Fallback to POST /issues/{n}/comments when inline reply returns 422" (epic Scenario Analysis)
- When this story is complete, the thread reply links to the posted review comment and begins with <!-- dso-agent-reply -->
← Satisfies: "reply to the originating thread linking to that review comment; all reply bodies begin with <!-- dso-agent-reply -->" (SC3)
- When this story is complete, unit tests are written and passing for all new or modified logic

- [Reliability] Two-step defend is non-atomic — defense_comment_id persistence after step 1 before step 2 is the sole idempotency mechanism; test must cover the case where step 2 fails and retry correctly skips step 1
- [Reliability] Comment on a deleted file may return 422 from the inline reply endpoint — fallback to POST /issues/{n}/comments is required; test must cover the 422 fallback path
- [Testing] Test must cover both is_inline=true and is_inline=false endpoint routing paths independently
- [Maintainability] Use the shared thread-reply posting function from Story 1 for the thread reply call — do not reimplement is_inline endpoint routing for the thread reply step

content.text: Replace file-impact-only coordination between parallel agents with explicit interface contracts at stream boundaries, and extend this coordination model to multiple parallel sessions.
wshobson/agents (33k stars) requires explicit interface contracts between parallel agents before spawning workers. The agent-teams plugin uses a team-lead agent that:
- Assigns strict file ownership (never duplicate assignments)
- **Defines interface contracts at agent stream boundaries** — what data format agent A will produce that agent B will consume

This is more structured than DSO's current approach of static file impact analysis and shared blackboard, which only prevents file-level conflicts but doesn't verify that parallel agents produce compatible outputs.
DSO currently coordinates parallel agents via:
1. **Static file impact analysis** — identifies which files each agent will touch
2. **Shared blackboard** — publishes file ownership per agent to prevent conflicts
This prevents two agents from editing the same file, but does NOT prevent:
- Agent A creating a function with signature `get_user(id: int) -> User` while Agent B calls `get_user(user_id: str) -> dict`
- Agent A creating a database migration that Agent B's code depends on but hasn't run
- Agent A defining an API response format that Agent B's frontend code doesn't match
- Two parallel sessions making incompatible changes to shared interfaces
Before spawning parallel agents, the orchestrator must declare interface contracts at boundaries:
Response: { token: string, user: { id: int, name: string } }
When agents report at CHECKPOINT 4/6 (implementation complete), the orchestrator verifies:
- Producer's implementation matches the declared interface
- Consumer's code calls the interface with the correct format
- Any deviations are flagged before the next batch starts
When multiple Claude Code sessions work on the same repo in parallel (worktree-based):
- Each session declares its interface contracts in a shared location (e.g., .claude/contracts/ or ticket comments)
- Before implementation, each session checks for existing contracts that overlap with its planned changes
- Semantic conflict detection: not just "same file" but "same interface" across different files
- Contract registry is append-only during a session; conflicts detected at commit/merge time
- **Blackboard extension** — add an `interfaces` section to the blackboard alongside file ownership
- **Implementation-plan** — task generation should identify interface boundaries between tasks and declare contracts
- **Sprint orchestrator** — verify contracts between batches, not just file conflicts
- **Completion verifier** — check that all declared contracts are satisfied (maps to the key_links concept from the must_haves epic)
- **merge-to-main** — contract validation as a merge gate for multi-session coordination
- Not a full API contract testing framework (like Pact) — it's lightweight declarations verified by the orchestrator
- Not a replacement for file impact analysis — contracts complement file ownership, they don't replace it
- Not blocking for single-agent tasks — contracts only apply when parallel agents or sessions share boundaries

content.text: The Pull (API + Merge) epic gives the implementation agent a structured, merged manifest reflecting designer revisions. After implementation, there is no automated way to verify the implemented UI matches the Figma design. This epic adds post-implementation fidelity validation: Figma frames exported as PNG via REST API, Playwright screenshots of implemented routes, perceptual diff scoring to quantify visual match.
1. Validation exports Figma frame as PNG via REST API (GET /v1/images/:key, scale=1), using rate-limit-aware client (check lastModified before re-exporting, 3-5s delay between requests)
2. Playwright captures screenshot at same viewport as Figma export (default 1440x900, configurable via design.figma_viewport), with networkidle + 500ms settle delay
3. Perceptual diff (pixelmatch, threshold 0.1) produces Design Fidelity Score (matching pixels / total pixels x 100); score and highlighted diff image written to design artifacts directory
4. Score below threshold (design.figma_fidelity_threshold, default 85) → story tagged design:fidelity_gap and surfaced in sprint reports; score at or above → tagged design:fidelity_verified
5. If Playwright not installed or REST API returns 429, logs warning with remediation guidance and skips scoring; creates advisory ticket to track skipped validation; never blocks story closure

Derived from Pull epic's 16 surviving scenarios. Key validation-specific risks: Playwright screenshot timing (mitigation: networkidle + settle delay), resolution mismatch (mitigation: normalize viewport), threshold miscalibration (mitigation: configurable per project, default 85), silent fidelity skip in CI (mitigation: advisory ticket created).
| `design.figma_viewport` (dso-config.conf) | `/dso:onboarding` design step at project setup | Operator edit | Figma pull validation script | N/A — persistent per-project config |
| `design.figma_fidelity_threshold` (dso-config.conf) | Same | Same | Pixelmatch comparison gate | N/A — persistent |

| Design artifacts directory (typically `docs/designs/` or configured path) | First Figma pull writes; `/dso:onboarding` creates the directory | Each design-pull operation writes new artifacts; never auto-deletes prior | Visual diff reviewer; design-review skill | **Operator-managed cleanup**: old artifacts are retained as historical record; operator manually archives or deletes when design system version changes. Closes the audit's gap. |
| Fidelity tags on visual-diff results | Figma-pull validation writes per comparison | Stable per result | Reviewer + design-review skill | Implicit with design-artifact ticket / commit lifecycle |
| Figma REST API reachable | `curl -sf -H "X-Figma-Token: $FIGMA_TOKEN" https://api.figma.com/v1/me` | 200 OK + JSON response |
| FIGMA_TOKEN env / repo secret present | `gh secret list --repo "$OWNER/$REPO" \| grep -c FIGMA_TOKEN` OR `test -n "$FIGMA_TOKEN"` | ≥1 |
| Playwright runtime present | `npx playwright --version` OR `command -v playwright` | Returns 0 |
| pixelmatch present | `command -v pixelmatch \|\| npm list -g pixelmatch \|\| jq -r '.devDependencies."pixelmatch"' package.json` | Returns version |
| Skip-when-absent fallback works | Synthetic test: unset playwright; verify SC5 fallback emits structured warning and exits 0 (informational, not blocking) | Confirmed before sprint close |
Converts the audit's prose-only external dependencies into structured in-session checks.
- Figma PAT with file_content:read scope (same as Pull API+Merge)

content.text: The story completion verifier (dso:completion-verifier) and epic completion verifier should validate that any UI changes conform to the corresponding UI designs before allowing closure.

Currently, the completion verifier checks that acceptance criteria are met and tests pass, but does not verify that UI implementation matches the approved design artifacts (DESIGN.md, wireframes, design system, approved.json). A story can close with all tests green but the UI looking nothing like what was designed.

1. **Design artifact detection** — at story/epic closure, the verifier should check whether the story involved UI changes (detect modified template/component/view files) and whether corresponding design artifacts exist
2. **Design conformance check** — when design artifacts exist (DESIGN.md, wireframes, component specs), the verifier should compare the implementation against them:
- Color values match the design system palette
- Spacing follows the design system's spacing scale (4/8px rhythm)
- Interactive states (hover, focus, active, disabled) are implemented per spec
3. **Missing design artifact warning** — if UI files were modified but no design artifacts exist, flag this as a gap (UI changes without an approved design)
4. **Design drift detection** — if the design artifact was last modified before the implementation began, flag potential drift between design and code
5. **Integration with design review** — the verifier should reference any prior /dso:design-review findings and verify they were addressed
- This should not block non-UI stories — only activate when UI files are detected in the changeset
- Design artifact paths should be configurable via dso-config.conf (e.g., design.artifacts_dir=designs/)
- The check should be pragmatic — exact pixel matching is not feasible, but structural conformance (correct components, correct hierarchy, correct color tokens) is checkable

content.text: Add an integrated observability layer to DSO that tracks context usage, cost, skill/agent performance, and review quality — with log rotation to prevent runaway disk usage.

The awesome-claude-code list (36k stars) identifies observability as the clearest gap in the Claude Code ecosystem. Existing tools (claude-devtools, ccflare) are external read-only viewers. DSO has the opportunity to build observability directly into its orchestration layer, where the data is richest.
- Context window utilization per phase (brainstorm, preplanning, implementation-plan, sprint batch, review, commit)
- Context at compaction trigger points (when did 70% threshold hit?)
- Sub-agent context consumption per dispatch (how much of the 200k window did each sub-agent use?)
- Compaction events: voluntary vs. involuntary, what was lost
- Token usage (input + output) per skill invocation
- Aggregated cost per story, per epic, per sprint
- Model tier usage breakdown (haiku vs. sonnet vs. opus tokens)
- Cost efficiency: tokens per task completed, tokens per line of code changed
- Sub-agent dispatch count, success rate, and checkpoint completion rate (1/6 through 6/6)
- Model escalation frequency (how often does haiku→sonnet→opus escalation occur?)
- Dispatch failure rate and recovery method used
- Review score averages per dimension (correctness, verification, hygiene, design, maintainability)
- Autonomous resolution success rate and attempt distribution
- False positive rate (findings dismissed or downgraded)
- RED test lifecycle (time from RED marker added to marker removed)
- Average time from open to closed per ticket type
- Bug discovery rate (bugs found per sprint)
- Structured JSON lines (.jsonl) — one event per line, each with timestamp, event_type, and payload
- Stored at .claude/telemetry/ (or configurable via dso-config.conf telemetry.dir)
- Separate files per category: context.jsonl, cost.jsonl, agents.jsonl, reviews.jsonl, tests.jsonl, tickets.jsonl
- **Size-based rotation** — rotate when a log file exceeds configurable max size (default 5MB)
- **Retention policy** — keep N rotated files (default 10), delete oldest

- **Compaction** — when rotating, compact the old file into a summary record (totals, averages, min/max per metric) before archiving. Raw events are discarded; summary is appended to a persistent summaries.jsonl
- **Disk budget** — configurable max total telemetry size (default 50MB). If exceeded, oldest rotated files are pruned first, then summaries are compacted further.
- **.gitignore** — telemetry directory must be gitignored (contains session-specific data, not project artifacts)
- The retro skill should consume telemetry data as a primary input alongside its existing git/ticket analysis
- Retro should surface: cost trends, context efficiency, agent success rates, review score trends, test health
- A /dso:telemetry or /dso:stats skill that summarizes current session and historical telemetry
- Output: structured summary with sparkline-style trends where applicable
- /dso:end session close should include a telemetry summary: total tokens used, cost estimate, sub-agents dispatched, review scores, tests run

content.text: Enhance the completion verifier to distinguish between task completion and goal achievement, and ensure planning workflows produce verifiable goal declarations.
get-shit-done (47k stars) separates verification into three distinct categories:
- **truths** — observable user-facing behaviors (not task completion). "The user can log in with email and password" not "Login endpoint was created."
- **artifacts** — files with real implementation (not stubs, not TODOs)
- **key_links** — critical connections between artifacts (the login form submits to the auth endpoint, the auth endpoint writes to the session store)
This separation catches the gap where all tasks ran successfully but the feature doesn't actually work end-to-end.

DSO's completion verifier currently checks that acceptance criteria are met and tests pass. But acceptance criteria are often written at the task level ("create the endpoint", "add the migration"), not at the goal level ("the user can complete the workflow end-to-end"). A story can close with all tasks green but the feature broken because the pieces don't connect.

- **Brainstorm** — epic success criteria should be written as observable user-facing truths, not implementation milestones. The gap analysis should flag criteria that describe implementation actions rather than user outcomes.
- **Preplanning** — each story's done definition should include at least one truth (user-observable outcome), the key artifacts expected, and any key_links between components.

- **Implementation-plan** — task acceptance criteria remain implementation-level (they should be), but the plan must also declare story-level must_haves that the completion verifier will check after all tasks complete.
At story closure, the verifier should check three layers:
1. **Task completion** (existing) — all tasks done, tests pass
2. **Truths verification** (new) — each declared truth is demonstrably true. Not "the endpoint exists" but "a request to /login with valid credentials returns a session token"
3. **Key_links verification** (new) — declared connections between artifacts are functional. The form actually submits to the endpoint. The endpoint actually writes to the database.
At epic closure, the verifier should additionally check:
- All story-level truths roll up to epic-level success criteria
- No epic success criterion is unaddressed by story truths
