- Check docs/adr/ for highest existing number (currently 0013-verifier-severity-authority.md)
- Follow exact format of existing ADRs: Status / Deciders / Date / Context and Problem Statement / Decision Drivers / Considered Options / Decision Outcome / Consequences / Links sections

- Context: DSO historically used two independent keys — merge.strategy (direct|pr) and enforcement.strategy (local|ci|both) — plus DSO_CI_MODE, DSO_SPRINT_MODE, DSO_MERGE_STRATEGY environment variables. This fragmentation required operators to set multiple keys whose interaction was non-obvious (e.g., merge.strategy=pr + enforcement.strategy=ci is the canonical CI-PR mode).

- Decision: Consolidate into a single dso.workflow key with values: local (default — merge.strategy=direct + enforcement.strategy=local), ci-pr (merge.strategy=pr + enforcement.strategy=ci), ci-local (merge.strategy=direct + enforcement.strategy=ci). Implement via hybrid shim (read-config.sh resolves dso.workflow to legacy values for backward compat) + idempotent migrator (rewrites existing dso-config.conf). Legacy keys remain functional via shim until migration sentinel exists; after sentinel, legacy-key reads are rejected.

- Considered options: (A) hard cutover — replace all legacy key reads immediately (breaks existing configs, high blast radius); (B) shim-only, no migration — keep shim indefinitely (perpetuates confusion); (C) hybrid shim + idempotent migrator — chosen approach (gradual migration, operator control, rejection gate after sentinel)

- Consequences: operators on old configs transparently continue working; new projects use canonical dso.workflow; migration is operator-initiated via migrator script; rejection gate prevents post-migration drift
Gate fired: 4 (decision rationale — why, not what)

content.text: # External-integration verification gate for /dso:fix-bug (in_review status + closure loop)

/dso:fix-bug front-loads investigation discipline — intent gate, feature-request gate, hypothesis testing, TDD RED-before-GREEN — but Phase E Step 4 only checks `$TEST_CMD`, `$LINT_CMD`, `$FORMAT_CHECK_CMD` before transitioning the bug to `closed`. For bugs whose symptom lives in an external integration (Jira bridge, GitHub Actions, hosted service) or a deployed environment (staging, production), a green local suite does not prove the symptom is gone. The Jira-bridge fix history shows ≥7 commits across multiple bug tickets, each shipped green, each followed by symptom recurrence; today's session almost shipped the 8th (bug 76d2-e46f) — the GitHub Actions workflow YAML hardcoded `ref: main` so the fix wouldn't run until merged, but unit tests had no way to surface that.

Each recurrence costs the on-call engineer 30–90 minutes of re-triage, re-filing, and context-reconstruction for the same root symptom — a sunk cost that compounds across the cluster. This epic closes the loop by introducing a new `in_review` ticket status, capturing a bug-reporter-owned Verification Plan in the create-bug template, and gating closure of external-integration bugs on observed evidence — captured in-session when possible, or via a recorded verification command run manually post-merge.

**Haiku-classifier contract.** /dso:fix-bug Phase A dispatches a haiku-tier classifier sub-agent that returns a structured response: `{"unreachable": bool, "reason": "<one-sentence>", "local_repro_step_present": bool}`. The bug is treated as requiring external verification when `unreachable=true AND local_repro_step_present=false`. When `reason` is empty or under 5 words, the orchestrator deterministically re-dispatches with sonnet (the "classifier=yes" shorthand used elsewhere in this spec means "requires external verification per this rule").

**Post-ship signal (not a sprint SC).** Zero unverified-closure recurrence events across the next 5 external-integration bug fixes is the long-term health target — audited at the end of the following debug session as a retrospective signal, NOT a gate on this sprint. The 9 numbered SCs below constitute the sprint's definition of done; this paragraph is a forward-looking monitoring note only.

1. **Routing to `in_review`**: A bug whose Phase A haiku classifier (or sonnet re-dispatch) returns `unreachable=true AND local_repro_step_present=false` (the external-verification predicate as defined in the Haiku-classifier contract in Context) AND for which Phase C/G emitted `VERIFICATION_STATUS != local_verified` transitions to `in_review` — not `closed` — at /dso:fix-bug Phase H. Verified by `dso ticket show <id> | jq -r '.status' == "in_review"` against a synthetic test bug.

2. **Verification metadata recorded**: The `in_review` ticket exposes `verification_command` and `verification_target_env` fields populated from the original bug's Verification Plan section, observable via `dso ticket show`. Both fields are non-empty strings (or the explicit ZIR placeholder `"unknown at filing time — to be defined before Phase C"` is treated as "missing" by Phase A's gate).

3. **Parent-close guard**: `dso ticket transition <epic-id> in_progress closed` exits non-zero when any direct child has status `in_review`. The error message names the `in_review` children and recommends `dso ticket reparent <bug-id> none` (using the command shipped by epic `5efb-06ea-0a65-4e96`). Until `5efb-06ea` ships, the message documents `--force` as the interim escape. The existing open-children-guard ALREADY treats new non-`CLOSED_STATUSES` values as open, so this SC is structural-message-content only — no new guard logic.

4. **`/dso:verify-fix` three-layer check**: `/dso:verify-fix <ticket-id>` runs the recorded `verification_command` (refusing to exec when the command appears to be a natural-language plan — heuristic: no leading executable token + contains spaces without shell metacharacters → prompts user to run manually instead), applies a three-layer pass/fail check (exit code + configurable stdout/stderr failure-pattern grep, default `error|fail|fatal` case-insensitive + NL-plan detection), and captures a TRUNCATED ticket-comment artifact (stdout+stderr capped at 8 KiB total per the existing comment-size guidance) including all three layer results. Transitions: all-three-layers-pass → `closed` with `--reason="Verified: <one-line>"`; any-layer-fails → `in_progress` with `--reason` recording the failing layer. `VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` config key, default 120s; on timeout, transition to `in_progress` with reason `"Verification timed out — manual verification required."`

5. **`/dso:end-session` sweep — single A/B choice**: At session close, /dso:end-session lists every `in_review` bug in session-scope with its recorded `verification_command` and `verification_target_env`, then asks the user a SINGLE choice: (A) defer all to next session (each ticket gets a comment recording the deferral) OR (B) run `/dso:verify-fix` non-interactively against each in sequence. Per-bug interactive "paste evidence inline" is REMOVED from the sweep — that flow routes through standalone `/dso:verify-fix <ticket-id> --evidence="..."` invocations outside the sweep.

6. **Phase A Verification Plan gate**: `/dso:fix-bug` Phase A applies a two-prong field-level checklist to the bug's Verification Plan before dispatching Phase C investigation: (a) `verification_command` is non-empty AND starts with a shell-executable token OR contains backtick-wrapped named binary/tool/endpoint; AND (b) `verification_target_env` is non-empty AND not in the deny-list `["TBD", "N/A", "unknown", ""]`. When either check fails, Phase A pauses inline and presents a fixed structured form for the user to complete; the user's structured response is parsed and written to the ticket as `EDIT` events on the Verification Plan fields before Phase C dispatches. (Pre-existing bug tickets filed before this epic ships are exempted via a grace-period tag `verification:legacy` which Phase A respects but logs; tickets tagged `verification:legacy` are surfaced in /dso:end-session sweeps as deferred-by-default.)
7. **Bridge mapping and Jira workflow probe**: Three checks performed together as a single SC:
- **Outbound code**: `_LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` in `plugins/dso/scripts/acli-integration.py` contains `"in_review": "In Review"`. Verified by grep.
- **Inbound config**: `gh variable get INBOUND_STATUS_MAPPING` returns JSON containing `"In Review":"in_review"`. Verified by `gh variable get` parse.

- **Jira workflow probe (automated)**: A test fixture invokes `acli jira workitem search --jql 'project = $JIRA_PROJECT AND status = "In Review"' --limit 1` and asserts exit 0, contrasted against the same query with a known-invalid status name asserting exit 1. The fixture lives in `tests/` and runs in the test gate — not a one-time manual check. If the probe fails in CI, the bridge mapping change is rolled back and a BRIDGE_ALERT is filed.

8. **In-session dogfooding (validation signal)**: Before the epic's parent slice can be marked complete, a synthetic bug ticket is created via the updated `/dso:create-bug` flow with `verification_target_env: "staging"` (or equivalent non-local value). The synthetic bug is advanced through /dso:fix-bug, transitions to `in_review`, and an attempt to close it (`dso ticket transition <synthetic-id> in_review closed`) is rejected by the gate until /dso:verify-fix is invoked with a passing command. The full sequence is demonstrated in-session before story closure and the demonstration is captured as a ticket comment.

9. **Historical-audit signal (in-session)**: Before the epic's parent slice is marked complete, one of the ≥7 previously-reopened Jira-bridge bug tickets identified in the motivating evidence is walked through in-session: the bug's prior closure event is compared against the Phase A two-prong checklist (SC6) and the SC1 routing rule, and the walk-through is recorded as a ticket comment demonstrating that the new gate would have blocked that closure. This audit is performed and captured within the sprint session — not deferred to after merge. Confirms the gate catches the historical class of failures.
Phased shipping in 3 slices, with an explicit contingency boundary between Slice 2 and Slice 3:

**Slice 1 — Infrastructure**: New `in_review` ticket status (event-sourced, like every other status: `ticket-transition.sh` allowlist extension; ticket-list filter default; `CLOSED_STATUSES` left unchanged so existing parent-close guard treats `in_review` as open; outbound mapping in `_LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA`; inbound mapping via `INBOUND_STATUS_MAPPING` repo variable). `/dso:create-bug` template grows a Verification Plan section with two fields. `ticket-transition.sh` open-children guard error message enhanced. **Independently shippable.**

**Slice 2 — Gate**: /dso:fix-bug Phase A two-prong Verification Plan checklist with structured-form pause; haiku classifier dispatch with structured 3-field output + deterministic sonnet re-dispatch trigger; Phase C/G emit explicit `VERIFICATION_STATUS` field into structured handoff artifact; Phase H reads that field and routes to `in_review` (never inferring from absence). **Depends on Slice 1.**

**Slice 3 — Loop**: `/dso:verify-fix` skill with three-layer check + `VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` + NL-plan detection; `/dso:end-session` A/B sweep; /dso:fix-bug opportunistic in-session verification when the target environment is reachable in the current session (e.g., post-merge `gh workflow run` — with pre-check that the target workflow declares `on: workflow_dispatch` and graceful skip when absent). **Depends on Slice 2.**

**Contingency**: If `/dso:end-session` coordination becomes blocked by the active end-session epic cluster (e7d6-8013, f27a-3c6a, fb32-215c, 71df-5bd8, f8b0-f816, e884-d0ad), Slices 1+2 ship independently and Slice 3 is deferred to a follow-on milestone. Slice 3 SCs (4, 5) are tagged `slice:3` for tracking; their deferral does not block parent-epic closure.

| `in_review` ticket status | SC1 transition rule at /dso:fix-bug Phase H | SC4 /dso:verify-fix transitions in_review→closed (pass) or in_progress (fail) | SC3 parent-close guard; SC5 end-session sweep; SC8 dogfooding | N/A — status enum value, persistent within ticket-system status taxonomy |

| `verification_command` (ticket field) | Written at bug filing via /dso:create-bug Verification Plan | SC6 Phase A inline EDIT events when checklist fails | SC4 /dso:verify-fix execution | Implicit with ticket close — field persists as historical record |
| `verification_target_env` (ticket field) | Same as `verification_command` | SC6 Phase A inline EDIT events; operator | SC4 execution context; SC5 sweep display | Implicit with ticket close |
| `VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (dso-config.conf key) | SC4 sets default 120s in template | Operator edit | SC4 timeout enforcement | N/A — persistent config key |

| `INBOUND_STATUS_MAPPING` (GitHub repo var, JSON) | SC7 operator-set via `gh variable set` | Operator updates when Jira workflow changes | inbound-bridge.yml mapping lookup | N/A — persistent; entries retire per-entry only when Jira workflow status is removed (operator action) |

| `verification:legacy` tag | SC6 backfill at epic ship — applied to all bug tickets filed BEFORE this epic shipped | Stable (no mutation) | SC6 Phase A grace-period gate; SC5 sweep deferred-by-default | Per-ticket retirement: removed via `dso ticket untag <id> verification:legacy` when (a) the ticket's `verification_command` and `verification_target_env` both pass SC6's two-prong checklist, AND (b) the user confirms via Phase A's gate dialog. Until then, the tag persists per-ticket; the tag-class itself has no global retirement. |

| `VERIFICATION_STATUS` (handoff field, Phase C/G → Phase H) | Phase C investigator or Phase G fix-applier writes on completion | Same writers update on re-investigation | SC1 Phase H routing decision | Implicit — reset at next ticket reopen or persisted as historical record on close |

- `.claude/scripts/dso ticket show <synthetic-bug-id>` (from SC8 dogfooding) shows `verification_command`, `verification_target_env` populated and `status=in_review`; post-/dso:verify-fix shows `status=closed`.
- `grep -nE 'in_review|VERIFICATION_STATUS|verification:legacy' plugins/dso/skills/fix-bug/SKILL.md` confirms every documented CONSUME reference resolves.
Closes the audit's named gap: `verification:legacy` RETIRE = per-ticket untag after Phase A two-prong pass + user confirm.
### External-dependency verification — Jira "In Review" workflow (Probe-6 remediation, 2026-05-18 follow-up)

The original 2026-05-16 pass deferred probe 6 because the audit framed it as requiring a closure-gating External Dependencies block over Jira workflow state. Reframing: `acli jira workitem search` is available in-session and SC7 already specifies an automated Jira workflow probe. Promoting SC7's probe to a structured external-dependency check:

| Jira "In Review" status exists in target project workflow | `acli jira workitem search --jql "project = $JIRA_PROJECT AND status = "In Review"" --limit 1` | Exit 0 (status name recognized by Jira workflow) |

| Negative-case sanity check | `acli jira workitem search --jql "project = $JIRA_PROJECT AND status = "NotARealStatus"" --limit 1` | Exit 1 (proves the positive check actually distinguishes valid vs invalid status names) |
| Outbound bridge mapping in code | `grep -E '"in_review":\s*"In Review"' plugins/dso/scripts/acli-integration.py` | Returns 0 |
| Inbound bridge mapping in repo var | `gh variable get INBOUND_STATUS_MAPPING \| jq -r '."In Review"'` | Returns `in_review` |

| BRIDGE_ALERT auto-files on Jira workflow mismatch | Synthetic test: run the SC7 fixture against a fake Jira project lacking "In Review"; assert the bridge raises a BRIDGE_ALERT ticket | Test pass before sprint close |

This converts SC7's prose into a structured verification surface. The Jira workflow itself remains externally owned by the Jira project administrator, but the dependency on its "In Review" status is detected and surfaced in-session before sprint closure rather than waiting for inbound-sync failures in production.

- `depends_on 5efb-06ea-0a65-4e96` (Add ticket reparent CLI command + bulk orphan remediation). SC3's full remedy text requires `dso ticket reparent <id> none` to exist; until that lands, the error message documents `--force` as the interim escape.
15 surviving scenarios from red+blue team filtering. Material risks the implementation must address (full list of mitigations in approach + SCs above):
- **Classifier timeout** (`runtime`, `high`): bounded by sonnet-redispatch + interactive-prompt fallback + non-interactive `INTERACTIVITY_DEFERRED` + fail-closed default.

- **Concurrent fix-bug sessions on same ticket** (`runtime`, `high`): event-sourced reducer treats STATUS events as append-only; second session sees in_review and exits Phase H idempotently. Field writes use last-write-wins (acceptable; same-classifier produces same answer).
- **Unbounded stdout in verification_command output** (`runtime`, `medium`): 8 KiB cap (SC4) + `VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (SC4).
- **End-session sweep blocks on unreachable env** (`runtime`, `medium`): A/B sweep + per-command timeout (SC5).

- **ticket-transition.sh callers unaware of `in_review`** (`deployment`, `high`): existing open-children guard treats non-CLOSED_STATUSES as open (already correct); explicit Slice 1 includes allowlist extension and ticket-list filter update.
- **Jira "In Review" status precondition** (`deployment`, `high`): SC7 automated CI probe + BRIDGE_ALERT on missing.
- **Pre-existing tickets without Verification Plan** (`deployment`, `high`): grace-period tag `verification:legacy` (SC6).
- **verification_command env context** (`configuration`, `high`): create-bug template guidance documents required env vars; verify-fix three-layer check surfaces missing-env errors clearly (SC4).
- **verification_target_env enum** (`configuration`, `medium`): deny-list at filing time + ZIR-compatible placeholder (SC6).
- **`in_review` not in ticket-list defaults** (`configuration`, `high`): Slice 1 explicitly updates ticket-list defaults.
- **Reporters writing actionable verification_command at filing** (`assumption`, `high`): ZIR placeholder + Phase A pause + structured-form re-entry (SC6).
- **"In-session evidence" undefined** (`assumption`, `high`): explicit `VERIFICATION_STATUS` field emitted by Phase C/G (Approach Slice 2).
- **Jira workflow guards on transitions** (`assumption`, `high`): SC7 automated probe + bridge-alert on transition failures; surface via existing BRIDGE_ALERT path.
- **Exit 0 ≠ symptom resolution** (`assumption`, `high`): three-layer pass/fail check (exit + failure-grep + NL-plan detection) (SC4).
Matched signal: skill file modifications + agent definitions (haiku classifier + new /dso:verify-fix skill).
Behavioral review (bot-psychologist) produced 6 prompt-tightening recommendations, all folded into the spec above:
- Haiku classifier emits structured 3-field output with deterministic tiebreaker (Context).
- Phase C/G emit explicit `VERIFICATION_STATUS` field; Phase H reads it (avoids agent negative-existential inference) (Approach Slice 2).
- /dso:verify-fix three-layer pass check + timeout + NL-plan detection (SC4).
- Phase A two-prong field-level checklist for "concrete" verification plan (SC6).
- create-bug ZIR-compatible explicit placeholder for verification_command (SC2, SC6).
- /dso:end-session sweep simplified to A/B; per-bug "paste evidence inline" removed from sweep flow (SC5).

No open-source framework reviewed has an identical post-fix async verification gate; `in_review` status is a novel construct. LangSmith's `EvaluationResult` schema (score+reasoning+key as separate fields) is the closest prior-art pattern and informs the three-layer check in SC4.

Step 2 web research was skipped. Rationale: no new third-party API (ACLI/Jira already integrated), no new dependency, no new auth/credential flow, no novel architectural pattern (status additions are an established codebase pattern; haiku classifier dispatch has in-codebase precedent at `dso:cross-epic-interaction-classifier`).

content.text: PR titles created by merge-to-main.sh (or whatever subroutine builds the title) should be descriptive of what the PR contains. Acceptable format:
[ticket-ID] short epic title or bug title
[dea8-3ca9] fix(sprint): add HARD GATE prohibiting plan-review substitution in Phase B Step 2b
The ticket ID and the human-readable purpose of the change should both be visible at a glance in the PR list, so reviewers and post-hoc spelunkers can identify the PR without opening it.
merge-to-main.sh is producing PR titles that are raw merge-commit subjects, for example:
- contains no description of the actual change
- is indistinguishable from any other merge-back PR
- defeats GitHub PR search / filter / triage
* /dso:fix-bug dea8-3ca9-110a-4f0d ran end-to-end; commit landed cleanly; merge-to-main.sh was invoked.
* The PR that merge-to-main.sh opened took its title from the auto-generated merge-back commit subject rather than from the feature commit subject or from the ticket title.
* **Known Workarounds:** Manually edit the PR title after creation (`gh pr edit <pr> --title "..."`). Not done autonomously per Rule 23 (route through merge-to-main.sh).
merge-to-main.sh should derive the PR title from one of, in order:
1. The latest non-merge commit subject on the branch (most descriptive of the change).
2. The branch's primary ticket ID (extracted from a DSO-Story / DSO-Task trailer, or from a leading [ticket-ID] in a commit subject) prefixed onto that subject if not already present.
3. Fallback: `[<branch-name>] <truncated-commit-subject>` — never the bare merge-back commit subject.

content.text: - **Affected file:** plugins/dso/skills/fix-bug/SKILL.md (Phase A Step 2.5 Worktree Ancestry Gate)

Ancestry gate should not hard-stop investigation when the affected code is still present on HEAD with the buggy pattern intact. The gate rationale ('affected code may not exist here') does not apply if the orchestrator can verify the affected file/pattern is present on HEAD.

Bug 4bf1-3198 was filed from a sprint-story branch (eb487f27, on branch 'story/e7f3-2b45-8d7d-4c68/1ef8-79c4-6195-4c98'). That commit is not an ancestor of main HEAD because the story branch has not merged. Phase A Step 2.5 fires `ANCESTOR_FAIL` and hard-stops the skill, even though:
- Line 35 still reads 'Batch into Groups of 20' (the exact buggy cap the ticket reports)
Hard-stopping here forces the user to manually override or re-queue, and creates friction whenever bugs are filed mid-sprint-story from worktrees forked off story branches.
User ran /dso:fix-bug 4bf1-3198. Ancestry check failed. User chose to override and file this meta-bug.
- **Affected workflow step:** /dso:fix-bug Phase A Step 2.5 (Worktree Ancestry Gate)

- **Proposed mitigation:** Before hard-stopping on ANCESTOR_FAIL, parse `file_impact` (if present) or affected-file hints from the bug description and check whether those files exist on HEAD. If they do, demote the failure to a warning comment and continue. Only hard-stop if no affected files can be located on HEAD. Alternatively, exempt bugs filed with the CLI_user tag from the hard-stop (treat as user-acknowledged scope).

content.text: * **Scenario Type:** CI tooling defect — blocks autonomous-resolution merge path.

When the cycle-2 reviewer needs to fix its own output to satisfy the findings schema (severity normalization, finding_id format, cited_lines format), the schema-correction pass should either (a) coerce the output cleanly and continue, or (b) drop the malformed finding with a warning. It should NOT emit a synthetic `category: schema_error` finding with `severity: critical` that blocks the PR — that turns an internal pipeline issue into a false code reviewer signal.
PR #139 cycle-2 llm-review (run 25953280369, re-run) succeeded in dropping the cycle-1 hallucinations (defended via PR comment) but emitted a synthetic finding:

"description": "Schema correction failed after 2 attempt(s): frozen field 'cited_lines' mutated at index 0: original=['plugins/dso/scripts/ticket-edit.sh:134', 'plugins/dso/scripts/ticket-edit.sh:138'], corrected=['plugins/dso/scripts/ticket-edit.sh:134-138']",

The summary line shows: "Schema correction applied: changed severity from 'suggestion' to 'minor' (valid enum value), fixed cited_lines ranges to match diff line numbers, generated valid finding_ids in f-<8hex> format, removed deprecated 'scores' key, and populated cited_excerpt with verbatim code from diff."

The pipeline detected that one of its own corrections mutated a frozen field — it expanded a two-element list of line refs into a single range string — and then failed-loud as a critical finding rather than reverting or dropping the offending finding.
1. PR #139 cycle 1: 4 critical false-positive findings (all alleged-undefined functions). Defense comment posted with line-number evidence at <PR>#issuecomment-4465917893.
2. Re-ran failed llm-review (cycle 2). Defense consulted — all 4 false positives dropped.
3. Cycle 2 emits only 2 minor findings about code style + 1 critical synthetic schema_error.

Trigger any llm-review cycle that needs schema correction on a finding's `cited_lines` field — specifically when the LLM produces `['<path>:<line1>', '<path>:<line2>']` and the corrector wants to collapse to `['<path>:<line1>-<line2>']`.
* plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/ (or wherever the schema-correction pass lives — likely `runner.py` post-process step)
* PR-blocking impact: any cycle-2+ review where the LLM emits multi-element cited_lines for a finding becomes an unmergeable PR until human override.
* Autonomous resolution (R5) requires cycles 2+ to consult defenses. The schema-correction failure overrides that, turning a successful R5 cycle into a manual-intervention case.
* Compounds with intermittent reviewer hallucinations — when the model recovers from a cycle-1 hallucination, the cycle-2 self-correction is a fresh failure mode rather than a success.
* Drop synthetic schema_error findings with severity≥important when the underlying real findings (post-correction) are all minor/none.
* Or: treat schema_error as `important` severity (eligible for resolution / defense) rather than `critical`.
* Or: when frozen-field mutation is detected, revert the field to the LLM's original value, log a warning, and continue rather than fail.

content.text: \`DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0\` (and the analogous \`.sprint-active\` rename trick) silently disable the per-branch CI review architecture for the commit at hand. No justification is required, no audit trail is written, no warning is emitted. As a result, an orchestrator under pressure (e.g., hitting a chain-enforcement failure because a sub-agent forgot a DSO-Story trailer) can rationalize repeated use, accumulating un-provenanced commits on the session branch.

This manifested in sprint d076-d35e-55db-4843 where the orchestrator (Claude) used the escape hatch 20+ times after S1's sub-agents committed without trailers, leading to PR #140 with all sprint output landed directly on the session branch.
When the orchestrator sets \`DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0\` (or renames \`.sprint-active\`), require one of:
1. Inline justification string (e.g., \`DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE_BYPASS_REASON=\"sub-agent missing trailer; chain repair\"\`)
2. Audit comment posted to the epic ticket: \`SESSION_BYPASS: commit=<sha> reason=<text> timestamp=<ts>\`
3. Hard counter: max N bypasses per session before halting (forces orchestrator to address root cause)
Without one of these, the pre-commit hook should refuse the bypass.
- Companion bug: redistribute-session-commits.sh missing recovery mechanism (separate ticket)
- The escape hatch is documented in CLAUDE.md as legitimate; this ticket is about adding friction, not removing the escape entirely

The shipped architecture detected this correctly — \`verify-session-provenance.sh\` marks those commits as un-provenanced, and \`ci.yml\`'s narrow integration review unions un-provenanced SHAs into the LLM review scope. So the entire sprint output ended up routed through a single integration review on PR #140. The LLM reviewer hit a ~1095-line diff and produced cycle-3 findings that included 4/4 critical false positives ("file X does not exist" hallucinations against files that demonstrably do exist).
2. Sub-agents work in worktree-isolated environments but commit directly to the session branch using \`DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0\` (escape hatch documented in CLAUDE.md)
5. CI runs \`per-branch-review.yml\` (per-story review) on the WHOLE diff because the session branch is effectively the story branch
6. LLM review produces unreliable findings on the oversized diff
There is no recovery mechanism to retroactively split bypassed commits into per-story sub-branch PRs after the fact. The shipped architecture *detects* the bypass but cannot *remediate* it.
- Groups commits by story-id (auto), surfaces untagged commits for user classification (interactive)
- Preserves merge commits (they represent integration history)
- For each story-id: creates \`story/<epic-id>/<story-id>\` from main, cherry-picks the commits in order, pushes, opens PR with \`base=<session-branch>\`
- Result: per-story PRs each trigger per-branch-review.yml on scoped diffs; the session->main PR's narrow integration review shrinks to only true cross-branch concerns

content.text: Line 42 of tests/scripts/test-verify-session-provenance.sh uses 'fname="file_$(date +%s%N).txt"'. The %N (nanoseconds) format specifier is a GNU coreutils extension; BSD date (older macOS, FreeBSD) does not support it. Modern macOS (Big Sur+) may support it depending on installed coreutils.
Currently passes on CI (Linux runner) and on the dev machine (modern macOS), but the test suite would fail in environments where %N is not supported.
Flagged by Per-Story LLM Review on PR #145.
- 'date +%s_$$' — epoch seconds plus PID for uniqueness within a process
Priority 3 — affects test portability but does not impact production code or CI. Easy fix.

content.text: Subagents dispatched under the worktree-isolation protocol (see plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/worktree-dispatch.md) are observed writing to the session worktrees working directory instead of their own isolated sandbox worktree. This breaks the core isolation invariant the protocol is supposed to guarantee: each sub-agent should receive a sandboxed working directory independent of the orchestrators directory, and the orchestrator is solely responsible for merging back via single-agent-integrate.md / harvest-worktree.sh.
When the invariant fails, sub-agent edits land directly on the session branch without going through:
This can corrupt the session branch, bypass review, and leave orphaned in-flight changes from concurrent sub-agents racing on the same files.

User reports observing the violation across multiple sessions and across multiple skills (fix-bug single-agent dispatch, sprint multi-agent dispatch, debug-everything). No single deterministic reproduction is in hand; the symptom appears intermittently.

Per worktree-dispatch.md Step 2: every Agent/Task dispatch passes isolation: "worktree" and the sub-agents Git Root Verification check (SUB_AGENT_ROOT vs ORCHESTRATOR_ROOT) HARD-FAILS (exit 1) if they match. The invariant should be: it is impossible for a sub-agent to write to the orchestrators worktree because (a) the Agent tool gives it a distinct cwd, and (b) the sub-agent itself verifies and exits 1 on mismatch.
Sub-agent edits are landing in the session worktree path. Possible mechanisms (to be confirmed by investigation):
1. Dispatch sites that omit isolation: "worktree" from the Agent tool parameters
2. Dispatch sites that omit ORCHESTRATOR_ROOT injection in the prompt, allowing the sub-agents own guard to short-circuit
3. Sub-agents that do not run the Git Root Verification snippet as their first action
4. A Claude Code Agent tool behavior where isolation: "worktree" silently degrades to shared cwd
5. Sub-agents using absolute paths back into the orchestrator root (path injection escape)

To be determined by investigation. User has no concrete log/commit evidence; investigation should start by auditing all Agent/Task dispatch sites in the dso plugin against the worktree-dispatch.md contract, then construct a probe that detects whether isolation is actually in effect at runtime.

High: this is a load-bearing safety invariant. When it fails, the session branch can receive un-reviewed, un-tested writes; review-gate hashes can be invalidated mid-batch; concurrent sub-agents can race on the same files in the session worktree.

content.text: Discovered during workflow scenario validation of bug 85f3-8301-c1b0-479d's fix (PR #145, now merged). Line 458 of plugins/dso/scripts/redistribute-session-commits.sh uses 'git checkout -q -B "$_branch" "$MAIN_REF"' to create per-story branches. The '-B' flag CREATES OR RESETS — if a local branch with that name already exists, it gets reset to MAIN_REF, destroying any commits that branch had.

Concretely, if the redistribute tool is run against the d076 epic where one story ID (2abb-11b6-37ca-49dc) happens to match the session branch's name (story/d076-d35e-55db-4843/2abb-11b6-37ca-49dc), running the tool would:
1. Reset the local session branch to origin/main (LOCAL DESTRUCTION)
2. Cherry-pick story commits onto the now-empty branch
4. Leave operator with broken local state
1. Detect collision: if any planned branch name matches SESSION_BRANCH (the source range's branch), SKIP that group — its commits already live on the session branch.
2. Replace '-B' with '-b' (create-only, refuses if exists), so the tool fails fast on unexpected name conflicts rather than silently overwriting.
3. Add behavioral tests covering: (a) collision with session branch is skipped with INFO message, (b) collision with pre-existing local branch produces a clear ERROR with no destruction.

Priority 1 because the bug could destroy local session-branch state including unpushed commits. Reachable in normal use when the redistribute tool is run against an epic where any story ID matches the session branch name pattern (e.g., any sprint whose Phase F created a story branch and then committed to it directly).
- Surfaced when planning to apply redistribute to PR #140

content.text: plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main-pr.sh line 57 has a hard assertion:
This requires MERGE_STRATEGY to be set externally as an env var. The script does NOT read the value from .claude/dso-config.conf (which already has merge.strategy=pr) or from dso.workflow=ci-pr.
The coupling is to merge-to-main.sh (the dispatcher), which reads the config and sets MERGE_STRATEGY before calling merge-to-main-pr.sh. Concretely, merge-to-main.sh lines 41-43:
1. Single source of truth violation: the config holds the strategy, but the implementation script ignores it and re-derives from an env var that may not be set.

2. Hidden dispatcher contract: any caller that uses merge-to-main-pr.sh directly (e.g., redistribute-session-commits.sh's PUBLISH phase) fails with a cryptic 'MERGE_STRATEGY must be set' error. The caller may not realize the strategy is already correctly set in config.

3. Discovered concretely when redistribute-session-commits.sh called merge-to-main-pr.sh in background-parallel for 8 redistributed story PRs — all 8 failed with this error despite the project's config having merge.strategy=pr (and dso.workflow=ci-pr).
Option A (preferred): merge-to-main-pr.sh reads the config itself.
Option B: change the assertion to a fail-safe default (preferred=pr when called for PR-mode, easily configurable via env). Document the dispatcher-only contract in the script header.

Callers other than merge-to-main.sh (e.g., redistribute-session-commits.sh PUBLISH phase, or any direct user invocation) must set MERGE_STRATEGY=pr before invocation. The redistribute tool's PUBLISH was reaching this code via background-parallel calls and silently failing — the workaround is to call gh pr create directly (bypassing the full pipeline), which is what I'm doing for PR #140's redistribute.

content.text: Bug c9df-0538 ("[worktree-dispatch protocol]: subagents using worktree isolation -> writes land in session worktree instead of isolated sandbox") was investigated at ADVANCED tier with two convergent root-cause findings:

1. **Guard coverage is 1 of 44 named agents.** Only `plugins/dso/agents/red-test-writer.md` carries the explicit `SUB_AGENT_ROOT` vs `ORCHESTRATOR_ROOT` verification + write-base warning. The other 43 named agents rely on the orchestrator pasting the guard snippet into the dispatch prompt as prose — LLM compliance with prose-only "first action" instructions is non-deterministic, which is the proven mechanism behind the bug's intermittent symptom.

2. **`isolation: "worktree"` is not a filesystem sandbox.** Empirically probed: from an isolated sub-agent worktree the write to `$ORCHESTRATOR_ROOT/<file>` succeeds and `cd $ORCHESTRATOR_ROOT` lands on the session branch with full git access. The platform-level PreToolUse guard that previously enforced isolation (`pre-agent.sh`, `worktree-isolation-guard.sh`) was deleted by commit 65ffaa449c (2026-04-08) addressing a different invariant, leaving prose as the sole barrier.
- Fix B: changed `single-agent-integrate.md` Step 1 from `exit 0` (silent downgrade) to `exit 1` + ticket-comment surface, so a breach when it occurs is now observable.

- Fix C: hardened `named-agent-dispatch.md` to mandate the four-parameter preamble (`isolation`, `ORCHESTRATOR_ROOT`, `SESSION_BRANCH`, `SESSION_HEAD`) and added a "NOT a filesystem sandbox" warning to `worktree-dispatch.md` Purpose section.
Fix A (this epic) closes the structural coverage gap.
Make worktree-isolation verification structural (executed unconditionally by every implementer-class sub-agent) rather than prose-prompt-dependent.

1. **Per-agent guard sweep** — embed the Git Root Verification snippet + write-base warning into every implementer-class named agent file under `plugins/dso/agents/` (~28 files lacking guard, plus the highest-risk fix-bug fix-implementer). Reviewer-family agents (12 agents) stay explicitly excluded — they intentionally write to the orchestrator-side `$WORKTREE_ARTIFACTS`.

2. **Named fix-implementer** — convert `fix-bug` Phase E Step 3's unnamed general-purpose fix sub-agent into a named `dso:fix-implementer` agent with the embedded guard and a concrete dispatch template. Currently this is the highest-risk single site in the plugin.

3. **Concrete prompt templates** — add `plugins/dso/skills/fix-bug/prompts/fix-dispatch.md` and similar files for any skill that currently dispatches implementer-class agents via prose-only "apply worktree-dispatch.md" references (sweep: fix-bug, sprint Phase E doc-writer site, debug-everything, update-docs, resolve-conflicts, preplanning).

4. **Build-side enforcement** — update `build-composed-agents.sh` (and equivalents for hand-written agents) to prepend a shared `_pre-flight.md` fragment containing the executable guard, so the guard is structurally first in every implementer-class agent's instruction set and cannot be regenerated away.

5. **(Stretch / optional)** Restore a PreToolUse Agent hook scoped *only* to checking `isolation` parameter presence on dispatches from a session worktree (the narrower invariant — different from what 65ffaa449c removed).
- SC1: `grep -L "ORCHESTRATOR_ROOT\|SUB_AGENT_ROOT" plugins/dso/agents/*.md | grep -v code-reviewer | grep -v huge-diff` returns empty (every non-reviewer agent has the guard).
- SC2: `fix-bug` Phase E Step 3 dispatches a named `dso:fix-implementer` agent with a concrete prompt template; the file exists and contains the four-parameter preamble template.

- SC3: An empirical probe similar to bug c9df-0538's test, run from any randomly chosen implementer-class agent in an isolated worktree, fails to write to `$ORCHESTRATOR_ROOT` (or at least logs an `ISOLATION_ERROR` ticket comment).
- SC4: A test in `tests/` verifies the structural presence of the guard heading in agent files (per behavioral-testing-standard rule 5 — structural boundary, not content string).
## Out of scope for this epic

- Filesystem-level sandbox enforcement (`sandbox-exec`/`bwrap`) — code-tracer flagged medium risk + reviewer-family collision; defer to a separate hardening epic if Fix A coverage proves insufficient.
- Reviewer family agent changes — they intentionally do not run isolated.

- Background commits: 1cb16e6958 (original wiring, 2026-04-06), 65ffaa449c (platform hook removal, 2026-04-08), ea4d021c36 (silent-downgrade introduction), a1d4fb7162 (protocol flattening, 2026-05-15).

content.text: Discovered during real-data application against PR #140 (epic d076-d35e-55db-4843). Cherry-pick failed on commit b7231a3783 when redistributing to story/d076.../5921-e956-b444-4b49 (S3 — rulesets).

The investigation for bug 85f3-8301-c1b0-479d (PR #145) specified Option C with five phases including a SPLIT phase: "For SPLIT commits, generate per-story sub-patches via git format-patch -1 <sha> filtered with git diff-tree --name-only intersected with each story's scope; emit synthetic commits with DSO-Origin-SHA trailer; cherry-pick uses git apply --3way of the filtered patch on the new story branch."

The implementation (committed in 73a89680f0 and refined in cc97bbc76a + 486f856a41) classifies commits as SPLIT correctly, but the PUBLISH phase performs a regular `git cherry-pick "$_s"` on the whole commit. There is no patch filtering, no synthetic commit generation, and no per-story sub-patch creation.
Concrete failure case from PR #140 redistribute:

- Commit 6def60b4c2 (trailer S3) creates plugins/dso/scripts/resolve-session-branch.sh (an S5 deliverable) AND plugins/dso/scripts/sprint/check-ruleset-preflight.sh (S3 deliverable). Cross-pollinated.
- Commit b7231a3783 (trailer S3) modifies tests/scripts/test-check-ruleset-preflight.sh — a test file CREATED by commit 964e7a6279 (trailer S5).
- When redistributing S3's group onto a clean main, b7231a3783 fails to apply because the test file doesn't exist (S5's commit creating it was not included in S3's group).
Implement the Option C SPLIT path as originally specified:
1. For each SPLIT commit, generate a per-story patch:
2. Apply the filtered patch on the story branch with `git apply --3way` to handle minor context differences.
3. If the filtered patch is empty (no files from this story in the commit), skip — the commit has nothing for this story.
4. Synthesize a new commit on the story branch with the original subject + a DSO-Origin-SHA trailer recording the source SHA.
5. Each story branch then contains ONLY its declared files; cross-story dependencies are avoided because each story owns its scope.
A helper script (filter-patch-by-paths.py or filter-patch-by-paths.sh) is needed for the patch-filtering step.
Until this is fixed, PR #140 cannot be fully redistributed. Options:
- Take the partial success (PR #151 for S1) as validation of the architecture for clean-cut stories.
- For SPLIT-heavy stories, defer to integration review (un-provenanced commits route into ci.yml's narrow scope).
- Manually patch-filter and cherry-pick per story (expensive, not autonomous).
- Surfaced after redistribute applied per user authorization
- Companion to cd29-0242-9df3-4118 (safety fix, P1, closed)
- Companion to 85f3-8301-c1b0-479d (recovery mechanism, closed but incomplete)

content.text: During /dso:brainstorm execution converting bug 7883-a502 into an epic, the orchestrator presented a 3-option choice that included 'Skip scrutiny pipeline, create epic minimally' as a path forward. Orchestrator emitted an AskUserQuestion containing option (c): 'Skip scrutiny pipeline, create epic minimally — Create the epic with the drafted spec, link to 5efb-06ea as depends_on, write Planning Intelligence Log marking scrutiny as orchestrator-confirmed only, tag and close. Faster but the brainstorm:complete tag may be rejected by the validator.' The framing acknowledged the gate but presented it as a user-choice tradeoff, exposing a bypass surface the brainstorm SKILL.md HARD-GATE explicitly prohibits.

Behavioral signal: orchestrator surfaced an option that contradicts the canonical pipeline HARD-GATE. The skill text itself does not authorize the option; the orchestrator constructed it. Suggests the existing HARD-GATE wording (which prohibits substitutions in the workflow execution path) does not explicitly cover the orchestrator presenting substitutions as user-facing choices. Strengthening could be: HARD-GATE addendum 'NEVER offer the user a choice that includes skipping the scrutiny pipeline. The pipeline is non-optional regardless of session context, time pressure, or context budget. The only valid scrutiny-skip is the placeholder-epic exception: when the epic is explicitly scoped as a scrutiny:pending stub requiring its own future brainstorm session.'

Hypothesized trigger: long-context brainstorm session where orchestrator faces remaining token budget pressure may rationalize scrutiny-skip as a save-progress tradeoff and surface it to the user. Validate by re-running a long brainstorm session and checking whether the same skip option re-emerges, OR by inspecting brainstorm SKILL.md to confirm the HARD-GATE text covers user-facing option presentation as well as orchestrator-internal substitution.

content.text: When merge-to-main.sh runs in PR mode and the PR auto-merges as a squash commit, the script's subsequent auto-bump phase commits a version bump (1.17.5→1.17.6) to **local** main, but the local main pointer is still at the pre-merge base. Origin/main has moved to the squash-merge commit (a different SHA from the local merge), so the bump commit is on a stale base and the push fails with non-fast-forward. Each --resume creates ANOTHER bump commit (1.17.6→1.17.7→…) on the same stale base instead of rebasing local main onto origin/main first, accumulating orphan commits indefinitely.
- Script bumped 1.17.5 → 1.17.6 on local main and tried to push → non-fast-forward
- --resume bumped 1.17.6 → 1.17.7 on the **same** stale base and tried to push → non-fast-forward again
- Local main now has two orphan bump commits not on origin

After PR auto-merge, the bump phase should fetch origin/main, reset/rebase local main onto it, then bump on top, then push. --resume should detect existing orphan bump commits and either rebase them onto fresh origin/main or discard and re-create.

merge-to-main.sh --help says '(no args) Run all phases sequentially (no version bump).' but invocation with no args produced 'INFO: --bump not specified — defaulting to patch (version.file_path configured).' Help text and behavior disagree. Pick one.

content.text: The DSO ticket system has accumulated 113 non-closed orphan story/task tickets (16 stories + 97 tasks) because skill files and sub-agent dispatch prompts do not reliably thread parent_id through ticket create calls. The 2026-05-12 audit reports a 1/5 health score with 106 warnings dominated by "orphan ticket: no epic parent". DSO maintainers cannot trust dependency graphs, sprint scoping, or epic completion semantics. Sprint orchestrators and sub-agents that consume the dependency graph to scope work and determine epic completion are also impaired — incorrect parent linkage causes misordered batches and premature epic closure. Hard-fail at ticket creation is rejected — capturing ticket data must take precedence over enforcing structure — so remediation is primarily structural: the orchestrator writes a literal --parent=<id> at every ticket create story|task call site (including literal injection into sub-agent dispatch prompts before dispatch), and a CI test enforces this structurally by scanning every SKILL.md and dispatch prompt. The existing bug-template enforcement pattern at ticket-create.sh lines 279-328 is retained as a backstop — the CLI exits 0 and emits a structured stderr ERROR with explicit "To fix:" command — with the stderr-capture+ticket edit --parent remediation snippet applied only at the orchestrator-context shell sites where bash stderr capture is reliable. The standalone ticket tag marks tickets that intentionally have no parent; standalone-tagged tickets are excluded from orphan warnings.

- validate-issues.sh --quick --terse reports 0 orphan story/task warnings AND no non-closed story/task in the live tracker has parent_id=null, EXCLUDING tickets tagged standalone (intentional opt-out) and tickets tagged defer or dso-cleanup-pending (owned by 7271-e463). Before/after diff produced inside the sprint session by running validate-issues.sh --quick --terse immediately after orphan-cleanup.sh completes.

- ticket-create.sh emits "ERROR: <type> ticket <id> created without --parent" to stderr followed by "To fix: ticket edit <id> --parent=<parent-id>" whenever a non-bug, non-standalone-tagged ticket is created without --parent; exit code remains 0 (shell unit test).

- ticket-link.sh retries up to 3 times with exponential backoff (configurable via ticket_link.retry_base_ms=250 and ticket_link.retry_max_ms=2000 with documented defaults), appends a structured JSON entry to the tracker link-failures log on persistent failure (fallback to ${REPO_ROOT}/.dso/link-failures.log when the tracker directory is absent), and emits structured ERROR to stderr (shell unit test).

- PRIMARY (load-bearing): A CI test under plugins/dso/tests/ scans every SKILL.md under plugins/dso/skills/ AND every agent dispatch prompt under plugins/dso/agents/ for ticket create story|task invocations and fails the build when any such invocation does not include an inline --parent= argument in the same command. All flagged sites are remediated within this epic's scope (not deferred). Three pre-existing missing-parent example sites are explicitly remediated: interface-contracts SKILL.md lines 82-87, tickets-health SKILL.md lines 113 and 116, preplanning/prompts/ui-designer-dispatch-protocol.md line 298.

- BACKSTOP: Every orchestrator-context shell block calling ticket create story|task captures stderr via mktemp and runs ticket edit <id> --parent=<id> when "created without --parent" signal observed. Applied only at sites where literal-parent injection at the call site is unreliable (orchestrator constructs parent ID dynamically from session state); site list finalized in preplanning.
| `ticket_link.retry_base_ms` (default 250) | `/dso:onboarding` / dso-config.conf template | Operator edit | ticket-link.sh exponential-backoff loop | N/A — persistent config |

| `.dso/link-failures.log` (structured JSON, fallback path) | ticket-link.sh on first persistent failure (mkdir -p + append) | Append-only per failure | Human review; debug-everything for `link-failures` pattern | Rotation: operator manual. Log grows until operator archives/deletes; recommended trigger: >1000 entries OR >1 MiB → archive via `mv .dso/link-failures.log .dso/link-failures-$(date +%Y%m%d).log`. No auto-rotation in v1. |

| `dso-cleanup-pending` tag | orphan-cleanup.sh opus residual step (Step 5) | Stable (no in-place mutation) | 7271-e463 future epic (residual handoff target); validate-issues.sh exclusion | Removed by 7271-e463 worker after processing — explicit untag via `dso ticket untag <id> dso-cleanup-pending` once the residual has been resolved (reparented, retyped, or closed). content.text: Discovered while triaging failed per-branch reviews on PRs #160, #163, #164 in epic d076. All clean per-story PRs (1-2 file diffs) were producing reviews citing files NOT in the PR's diff (e.g., bridge-inbound.py, ticket-edit.sh) because the workflow computed the diff scope against a stale SPRINT_SESSION_ID repo variable.
- SPRINT_SESSION_ID repo variable was set to "worktree-20260515-200444" by sprint Phase A
- That branch still exists on origin but its HEAD is an OLD commit (deb229115bc4 — from before bug fixes were merged into session)
- merge-base with that old commit produces a 5492-line diff covering all session work since
- Result: reviews on small per-story PRs cite files belonging to unrelated work that landed AFTER the worktree branch HEAD
The session branch's effective head migrated:
- Phase F: created story sub-branch "story/d076-d35e-55db-4843/2abb-11b6-37ca-49dc" via STORY_PR_BASE pattern
- PR #140 opened from "story/d076.../2abb-..." → main; session work continued accumulating on THAT branch
Per-branch-review.yml should look up the PR's base directly when a PR exists for the branch, rather than relying on the repo variable:
This makes the workflow self-correcting: each PR's diff is computed against ITS actual base. The repo variable becomes a fallback for branch pushes without an open PR.
- Phase F (or Phase I session-close) must update SPRINT_SESSION_ID when the session branch's effective head migrates to a new branch name (the 2abb-... rename case here).
- When a sprint completes or is abandoned, SPRINT_SESSION_ID should be cleared. Stale values across sessions are the failure mode this incident exposed.
Workflow should validate that the resolved BASE branch exists and is reasonably current:
echo "WARN: BASE_REF $BASE_REF not on origin — falling back to main" >&2
A workflow that produces a 5000+ line diff for a "scoped per-story review" is almost certainly mis-scoped. Add a sanity check:
echo "WARN: scoped review produced ${DIFF_SIZE}-line diff for a per-story PR — check BASE_REF resolution" >&2
Add a header comment in per-branch-review.yml documenting:
- What SPRINT_SESSION_ID is and when it gets set/cleared
- Why PR base is authoritative when available

Updated SPRINT_SESSION_ID via `gh api PATCH .../actions/variables/SPRINT_SESSION_ID -f value="story/d076-d35e-55db-4843/2abb-11b6-37ca-49dc"` to point at the current session branch. Workflow re-runs in progress to verify scope correction.
- Discovered during user-directed remediation pass on epic d076 (after PR #163's failed review found 4 critical findings in bridge-inbound.py despite the PR's diff only being 2 unrelated files).

Reading \`CLAUDE_SESSION_ID\` (unset by runtime) -> always falls through to the random-UUID generator -> every session-record gets a fresh UUID -> session correlation lost.

content.text: A session orchestrator was observed attempting to close another session's PR because it had no memory the PR existed and treated it as a 'mystery' to be cleaned up. The orchestrator's logic for deciding whether to act on a PR did not distinguish between (a) PRs it had created itself but forgotten due to context compaction, (b) PRs it had created itself and remembers, and (c) PRs created by entirely different sessions. The result is destructive cross-session interference: one session closes another's in-flight work.

A session must be able to: (1) recognize PRs it owns (its own session's prior work) even after an auto-compact that wipes conversation memory, AND (2) recognize PRs it does NOT own (other sessions' PRs) and leave them strictly alone — no close, no comment that implies authority, no merge, no force-push. The default for any PR whose ownership cannot be positively established as belonging to this session must be hands-off.

Post-compact session encountered a PR it had no memory of, classified it as a 'mystery' (assumed orphaned/abandoned), and attempted to close it. Other-session ownership was not detected. No persistent ownership marker exists today linking PRs to the session that created them in a way that survives compaction.
This is a cross-cutting concern touching at least:
- PR creation surface (.claude/scripts/dso merge-to-main.sh and any gh pr create call site) — needs to stamp a session-identifying marker on PR body/branch/labels
- Session identity surface — needs a stable session ID that survives compaction (worktree path? branch name? a sentinel file in .claude/artifacts/?)
- PR action surface (end-session, debug-everything cleanup loops, retro skill, any orchestrator that lists or acts on PRs) — needs an ownership check before destructive actions
- CLAUDE.md / skill rules — needs a Critical Rule on the order of 'never close/modify a PR your session did not create unless explicitly user-authorized'
- post-compact resume detection — when a session resumes from compaction, the ownership marker must be discoverable from durable state (not conversation memory)

content.text: Observed on PR #167 (https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/pull/167), llm-review job 76343247603 (run 25970902666). The llm-review CI workflow failed with a synthetic \`schema_error\` finding, fail-closed, even though no real review finding existed on the trivial 4-line diff.
1. Primary reviewer (code-reviewer-standard / claude-sonnet-4-6) returned a non-JSON response: \`ERROR: LLM returned non-JSON response (length=1818); cannot parse as findings.\`
2. Fallback chain exhausted; dispatch.py emitted a single synthetic \`fallback_exhausted\` pseudo-finding (per its DD3 contract — dispatch.py:9, 50, 327).

3. Schema correction loop ran; it correctly recognized the \`fallback_exhausted\` entry as a meta/synthetic finding (not a real code-review finding) and removed it. Resulting findings array length = 0.

4. dispatch.py:993-998 count-equality check fires: \`finding count mismatch: got 0, expected 1\`. The loop treats this as an error and retries; the retry also returns 0 findings (correctly — the original was a single fallback marker); after attempts exhausted, the loop emits a synthetic \`schema_error\` finding with severity 'important' and the runner fails CI (exit 1).

When the original findings array contains only synthetic-type entries (\`fallback_exhausted\`, \`specialist_error\`, \`parse_error\` — already enumerated as the synthetic-type set at plugins/dso/scripts/validate-review-output.sh:351), schema correction validly producing 0 findings should NOT be treated as a count mismatch. The count-equality check should compare counts of REAL findings (excluding synthetic types) on both sides, OR the synthetic-only original should short-circuit before the count check fires.
No exemption for synthetic-type original entries; correction's valid 0-count is treated as failure.

- Trigger the primary reviewer to return non-JSON (occurs on ~small-diff PRs where the model emits prose instead of structured JSON; see ci-llm-review run 25970902666 turn-0 stderr 'Anthropic cache_read_input_tokens did not increase on turn 1 (prev=16325, current=16325)')
- Schema correction (any attempt count) removes the pseudo-finding -> 0 findings remain
- dispatch.py:995 reports count mismatch -> retries exhausted -> synthetic schema_error -> CI fail

CI fail-closed on infrastructure-only failure: blocks merge of correct, finding-free diffs whenever the primary reviewer's first response is non-JSON. Re-running the workflow may succeed (different LLM response) but the user experiences spurious merge blocks on trivial PRs. Observed: PR #167, a 4-line typo fix (CLAUDE_SESSION_ID -> CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID), blocked by this exact path.

At dispatch.py:993, before the length comparison, filter both sides to non-synthetic types using the synthetic-types set from validate-review-output.sh:351 (\`{'specialist_error', 'fallback_exhausted', 'parse_error'}\`). Compare counts of real findings only. If the original was entirely synthetic and the correction yields 0 real findings, that is the correct outcome — do not retry, do not emit schema_error.
- Recent commit db971905a4 'docs(tests): document severity demotion rationale in schema_correction docstring (eac2-16ff)' — related work in same area

content.text: The CI `llm-review` job on PR #165 (https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/pull/165) has produced systematically-repeating false-positive findings across 3 consecutive cycles. The pattern is consistent and indicates the reviewer is not receiving the full cross-file diff context when constructing findings, despite being instructed to review the whole diff.
### Repeat false positive 1 — `origin_main_sha consumer not visible`

Reviewer claim: "New state field `origin_main_sha` is captured and stored but the comment claims it is `Used by --resume freshness check` — however, no consumer code is visible in the diff. The diff shows merge-to-main-direct.sh was modified (index hash changed) but contains no visible content changes."

Reality: the consumer IS in the SAME commit (`6c305025af`), located in `plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main-direct.sh` at the `--resume` block around line 935+. The code reads `origin_main_sha` from the state file, fetches `origin/main`, runs `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, and resets `completed_phases` on staleness. Verified by:
which returns multiple hits. Test coverage exists (`tests/scripts/test-merge-to-main-resume-freshness.sh`, 6 passing tests).

Despite a PR-thread defense reply pointing at the consumer file, the SAME false positive resurfaced in subsequent cycles — suggesting the reviewer either does not load defenses or its diff window does not include the consumer file.
### False positive 2 — `Lock file behavior documented but not implemented`

Reviewer claim: "the concurrency model docstring claims flock-style locking at /tmp/merge-to-main-lock-<shasum>, but grep reveals no lock file creation, flock calls, or mutual-exclusion implementation."

Reality: lock IS implemented in `merge-to-main-direct.sh` around line 348+: `LOCK_FILE="/tmp/merge-to-main-lock-$(echo -n "$MAIN_REPO" | shasum ...)"`, `_wait_for_lock`, `_acquire_lock`, `_release_lock`. The function `_is_lock_stale` is defined in `merge-helpers.sh`. **25 tests** in `tests/scripts/test-merge-to-main-locking.sh` cover this code path and all pass. The docstring added in PR #165 only describes the existing mechanism.

Reviewer claim: "the diff introduces a new test file at tests/scripts/test-merge-to-main-resume-freshness.sh, but the diff ends immediately after the file header (only shows new file mode 100755). No test assertions, helper sourcing, or test functions are visible."

Reality: the file is 138 lines and has 6 passing tests. Verified by `bash tests/scripts/test-merge-to-main-resume-freshness.sh` returning `PASSED: 6 FAILED: 0`. Either the diff payload was truncated before reaching the reviewer or the diff parser silently dropped the file body.
1. Truncates the diff at a size threshold without warning, dropping content past some line/byte cap;

2. Uses a per-file diff window that excludes cross-file references — so a reviewer looking at `merge-helpers.sh` cannot see the consumer in `merge-to-main-direct.sh` even when both files are in the same commit;
3. Does not honor PR-thread defenses (the cycle-1 defense reply for the same finding was ignored in cycles 2 and 3);
4. The context-augmentation loop (`review.context_aug.*`) is either not firing or not fetching the cited consumer files.

PR #165 cycles 1, 2, 3 all triggered llm-review with the same diff. Cycle 2 and 3 added additional commits but the original two commits (5d49a2338d, 6c305025af) were unchanged. The false positive about `origin_main_sha consumer not visible` appears in EVERY cycle.

P2 — autonomous resolution loop cannot converge when the reviewer systematically cannot see the consumer code for state fields. PRs requiring cross-file feature implementation (state init in one file, consumer in another) will be blocked by repeating false positives. `review.max_resolution_attempts=3` is exhausted on PRs that are correctness-clean.
- `dso_ci_review/runner.py` and how the diff is constructed before being passed to the model
- `review.context_aug.*` config keys — verify the context-augmentation loop is being invoked; check `docs/contracts/ci-review-context-request.md`
- Whether `review-github-defense-store.sh` defenses are being loaded into the cycle-N+1 prompt
- The mirror-defenses-to-pr.sh wrapper: are the cycle-1 defenses visible to the cycle-2 reviewer?
- Diff size / line caps: is there silent truncation past N lines or M bytes?
Bypass llm-review (admin merge) when the failing findings can be evidenced as false positives via PR-thread defense, until this is fixed.

content.text: DSO sessions create PRs without any session-identifying marker. When a session resumes from auto-compact (memory loss) or another session encounters the PR, destructive PR-action code paths in merge-to-main-pr.sh, debug-everything, phase-10-merge-verify, and end-session resolve target PRs purely by current branch name. A post-compact session was observed classifying another session's PR as a "mystery" and attempting to close it. The Claude Code runtime sets CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID per session (UUID); this epic stamps that as a Session-Id: trailer on the PR body at creation. Following the bot-psychologist R2 lesson from the prior epic (7510-0198) — load-bearing enforcement must be structural, not behavioral — the canonical action path becomes a single wrapper script pr-destructive-action.sh that internalizes the ownership check, AND a PreToolUse hook intercepts any bash invocation of "gh pr (close|merge|edit|comment)" that does not go through the wrapper. SKILL.md and CLAUDE.md instructions are framed as negative directives (prohibitions) pointing to the single permitted path, not as procedural "remember to invoke X before Y" composition that the prior epic's bot-psych review identified as behavioral-drift-prone.

- plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main-pr.sh stamps "Session-Id: $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID" and "Generated-By: dso-merge-to-main-pr.sh" trailers into the PR body at create; the value is shell-quote-sanitized before injection; shell unit test asserts both trailer lines are present and that a synthetic newline-containing session ID is rejected at sanitization with a clear error.

- New plugins/dso/scripts/pr-owned-by-session.sh <pr-number> calls gh pr view --json body, parses the Session-Id: trailer, compares to $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, and exits 0 (own), 1 (foreign), 2 (absent), 3 (api_error) with structured stderr identifying the case; shell unit test covers all 4 exits with synthetic fixtures; the helper itself never invokes gh pr <destructive>.

- New plugins/dso/scripts/pr-destructive-action.sh <pr-number> <action> [args...] is the single permitted path for destructive PR actions: it internally invokes pr-owned-by-session.sh, then on exit 0 executes gh pr <action> [args...], on exit 1/2/3 emits structured stderr with the case identifier and exits non-zero (fail-closed). Shell unit test covers all 4 internal-check outcomes end-to-end.

- New PreToolUse hook plugins/dso/hooks/check-pr-destructive-action.sh parses the Bash tool command string and blocks any invocation containing gh pr (close|merge|edit|comment) that does not also contain pr-destructive-action.sh; hook integration test asserts the block fires on a direct "gh pr close N" invocation and does NOT fire on "pr-destructive-action.sh N close".

- CLAUDE.md "Never Do These" rule 25 (negative-directive form): "Never invoke gh pr (close|merge|edit|comment) directly. Destructive PR actions go through pr-destructive-action.sh (the only permitted path). Direct invocations are blocked by PreToolUse hook check-pr-destructive-action.sh." Rule additionally documents the exit-code contract (0/1/2/3) and the rationale (session ownership; see fe66-f05b).

- All call sites in shell scripts that previously called gh pr (close|merge|edit|comment) directly — merge-to-main-pr.sh:437/549/1295 — are migrated to invoke pr-destructive-action.sh. SKILL.md sites — debug-everything/SKILL.md:1175, phase-10-merge-verify.md:51, end-session/SKILL.md:242 — are rewritten as negative-directive instruction blocks naming pr-destructive-action.sh as the only permitted path; the rewrite is in addition to the PreToolUse hook (which is the load-bearing enforcement).

- CI test under plugins/dso/tests/ scans every .sh file under plugins/dso/ for gh pr (close|merge|edit|comment) invocations and fails the build when any such invocation appears outside pr-destructive-action.sh itself. SKILL.md files are explicitly excluded from this scan (false-positive surface — prose containing the script name in instruction text would pass meaninglessly per bot-psych analysis). Behavioral compliance on SKILL.md sites is enforced by the PreToolUse hook at runtime, not by the grep test.

- Two-session integration test: simulate session A with CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=session-A-uuid creating a synthetic PR (trailer stamped); switch to CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=session-B-uuid and attempt close/merge/comment via pr-destructive-action.sh — all three refused (exit 1, structured stderr). Positive case (session A acts on its own PR) succeeds. Edge case (PR with stripped trailer) returns exit 2 absent — included in the same test.

- Pre-existing un-trailered PRs migration: a one-shot script plugins/dso/scripts/backfill-pr-session-trailers.sh lists all currently-open PRs and, for each PR whose author matches the local "gh api /user --jq .login", prompts the operator to either (a) stamp this user's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID as the trailer retroactively or (b) skip. Script logs each decision; idempotent (skips PRs that already have a trailer). The migration is operator-driven, never automatic, never claims ownership for a session not actually the owner.
- `[ -n "$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID" ]` returns 0 at sprint Phase A start.

- The preplanning empirical-probe task (already named in the existing SC list) has been executed and its findings written to a ticket comment on this epic. The comment records: (i) the observed value at sprint start, (ii) the observed value after at least one compaction event (forced or natural), (iii) whether stability holds. If stability does NOT hold, sprint dispatch is BLOCKED and the design is revised — this remediation makes the artifact (ticket comment) load-bearing.

- Verification at Phase I: `.claude/scripts/dso ticket show 53ef-d6fd-5ca5-4d62 | grep -E "CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID.*stability|empirical.*probe"` returns a comment with observed values across the probe scenarios.
- `plugins/dso/scripts/backfill-pr-session-trailers.sh` exists with the executable bit set (`test -x` returns 0).

- The 53ef sprint operator runs the backfill against the operator's own currently-open PRs in-session before Phase I, and the script's decision log is captured as a ticket comment on this epic. If the operator has zero un-trailered PRs at sprint time, the script is invoked against a synthetic fixture and the fixture-mode log is captured instead.
- Verification at Phase I: `.claude/scripts/dso ticket show 53ef-d6fd-5ca5-4d62 | grep -E "backfill.*decision log|backfill.*invoked"` returns the captured artifact.
Converts the audit's prose-only external dependencies into structured in-session artifacts (ticket comments) that gate sprint closure.
- 7510-0198 (DSO orphan story/task prevention) — same R2 structural-enforcement pattern; coordinate the new plugins/dso/tests/ CI grep test layout to share scanner harness
- 0777-0f3d (multi-agent coordination) — pr-owned-by-session.sh returns 0 for all agents sharing the same CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID; document this explicitly
- 0cf2-42b5 (sprint SKILL.md refactor) — coordinate SKILL.md negative-directive injection with the refactor's phase layout
- 2239-1545 (cross-runtime harness adapter) — CI grep test targets .sh only, isolating runtime portability concerns to the hook implementation
- 70f6-05f1 (Clash parallel review) — Session-Id is immutable once stamped; document the ordering guarantee
- fb32-215c (workflow-config PR vs merge flag) — both PR creation paths (auto-merge mode and PR-only mode) must stamp the trailer

Adopt the bot-psychologist R2 redesign in full. Single permitted invocation path via pr-destructive-action.sh wrapper that internalizes the ownership check. Load-bearing enforcement via PreToolUse hook that blocks any direct gh pr destructive invocation. CI grep test scopes to .sh files only (SKILL.md prose generates false positives). CLAUDE.md rule and SKILL.md instructions are negative-directive form ("never invoke gh pr X directly; use the wrapper"), not procedural composition. Sanitize CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID before injection. Distinct exit codes (0/1/2/3) for own/foreign/absent/api_error. Operator-driven backfill script handles pre-existing PRs. Preplanning verification task confirms CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID stability across compaction before sprint dispatch — if the variable is not stable, the design is revised before implementation.
- CRITICAL — CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID stability across compaction unverified — addressed by preplanning empirical verification task
- HIGH — CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID unset in non-Claude-Code contexts — addressed by fail-closed exit 2 (absent); operator-driven backfill provides manual escape hatch
- HIGH — Concurrent destructive actions in same session — same-session-actors-can-proceed is the intended behavior; advisory lock deferred to follow-on if observed
- HIGH — gh pr view fails or times out — addressed by distinct exit code 3 (api_error); fail-closed at the wrapper; stderr distinguishes from foreign/absent
- HIGH — Pre-existing PRs lack trailer — addressed by operator-driven backfill script, idempotent, owner-only
- HIGH — SKILL.md sites are prose, not shell code — addressed by R2 redesign — PreToolUse hook is load-bearing; CI grep test rescoped to .sh only; SKILL.md instructions are negative directives
- MEDIUM — PR body truncation drops trailer — trailer at end-of-body so truncation impact is detectable; helper exits 2 (absent) if approaching GitHub 65k limit at create, fail-closed
- MEDIUM — CI grep test fails on multi-line gh pr or wrappers — addressed by scoping to .sh only — wrappers scanned same as direct calls

content.text: Concrete failure on d076 epic: orchestrator pushed commit 3f8f62d337 (7 valid Copilot finding fixes + 1 duplicate-CI-trigger fix) to branch story/d076-d35e-55db-4843/2abb-11b6-37ca-49dc at 22:26 UTC. PR #140 had auto-merged the same branch at 22:23 UTC. The push succeeded — git/origin are happy — but the commit is stranded: PR #140 is MERGED, so the new commit has no path to main.

This is the SECOND auto-merge timing miss in the d076 epic. The first was implicit (per-branch review approving an older commit than expected). This one is explicit: commits authored AFTER the merge cannot reach main via the merged PR.
1. Orchestrator (or human) has an open PR with auto-merge enabled.
2. CI completes; auto-merge fires; PR merges.
3. Orchestrator pushes additional commits to the same branch (typical pattern when addressing review findings or adding follow-up fixes).
4. Push succeeds. No error. No warning.
5. Commits sit on the remote branch indefinitely; never reach main.
6. Discovered only when someone notices the diff isn't in main, OR when a downstream CI/review confusion surfaces.
Add a check to `plugins/dso/hooks/pre-push-*.sh` (or as a new dedicated hook):
echo "ERROR: PR for $BRANCH is MERGED. New commits will not flow into main." >&2
echo "       Open a follow-up PR from origin/main instead. Override: DSO_ALLOW_PUSH_TO_MERGED_PR=1" >&2
echo "WARN: PR for $BRANCH is CLOSED. Push may not reach main." >&2 ;;
- gh is not authenticated (CI runners w/o gh setup)
- No PR exists for the branch (genuine pre-PR push)
- The branch is not push-tracked (local-only branch)

`merge-to-main.sh` and sprint Phase F should pre-check the PR state for the branch they're about to push to and refuse with a similar message if MERGED. Catches orchestrator-driven pushes specifically (the d076 case).

Add to "Never do these" or "Always do these": "Before pushing additional commits to a branch with an open PR, check that the PR is still OPEN (`gh pr view <branch> --json state`). If MERGED, open a follow-up PR instead."
- Pre-push hook fires on a branch whose PR is MERGED → exit non-zero
- Pre-push hook allows push when PR is OPEN
- Pre-push hook allows push when no PR exists for the branch
- Override env var (DSO_ALLOW_PUSH_TO_MERGED_PR=1) bypasses the check
- Direct cause of follow-up PR #168 needing to exist after PR #140 auto-merged
- Cross-references the architectural class of "auto-merge timing" bugs: per-branch-review approves an old commit, OR follow-up commits arrive after merge

content.text: **Filed by d076 post-mortem analysis (`docs/findings/d076-postmortem-analysis.md`) — implementation deferred to a remediation sprint.**

When completion-verifier returns FACTUAL FAIL on a validation-class success criterion (an SC whose entire purpose is end-to-end exercise — typically the last SC in the epic spec, named "validation acceptance" or similar, and explicitly requiring a real-world exercise), the override pathway must require: (a) a successor-epic ID exists in `open` status that explicitly inherits the failing SC as one of its own success criteria; (b) the successor is linked back via `relates_to` with a "validation-inheritor" relation comment. Without (a)+(b), closure is refused even with user override. Validation-class SCs are a distinct verdict class from collectible-evidence SCs and are not eligible for the standard override pathway.

f61f-7e0a-36d3-4e7d SC8 was the explicit end-to-end validation SC ("validation sprint of at least 1500 total changed LOC across at least 3 stories runs the entire pipeline end-to-end"). completion-verifier verdict was FACTUAL FAIL. User authorized override on 2026-05-12 with the rationale "DD1 (real validation sprint pass) → override applied" and named two blocking bugs. Both blocking bugs are now closed but no validation sprint ever ran on the f61f architecture; d076 became the de-facto successor but its success criteria do not include "exercise the f61f architecture end-to-end." The validation responsibility was lost in the closure cascade.

Additionally, commit 8df0867531 created docs/findings/validation-sprint-artificial-marker.md whose own message reads "This commit does not represent real story implementation — it exists solely to produce the per-story CI review artifact required by the DD2 mechanical proxies." This artificial-validation workaround was permitted to satisfy mechanical proxies even though the author knew the architecture could not actually satisfy SC8.

f61f closed 2026-05-12 with SC8 FACTUAL FAIL. d076 closed 2026-05-15. PR #140 (the de-facto end-to-end exercise) landed in main 2026-05-16 — i.e., AFTER both supposedly-completed epics. No epic on record has SC "exercise per-story PR architecture on a real ci-pr sprint."
A two-tier verdict model (collectible-evidence-gap vs. feature-doesn't-work) plus a successor-handoff requirement is cheap and prevents the silent inheritance gap that drove the d076 rescue.
Affected agent: completion-verifier. Affected skill: completion-verifier SKILL.md (closure protocol). Affected workflow: epic-closure path in /dso:sprint Phase I.
